I don't even know where to begin. It's absolutely brilliant. Senua is a wonderful protagonist on the suicide mission of all suicide missions, marching into the Viking hell to rescue the soul of her best friend. Even in the game's opening credits as the Pict Warrior Senua paddles up a river through very ominous mist I knew this was going to be good. It's a rarity to see a game that has a near perfect balance of several aspects of gaming such as the walking simulator, action adventure (DMCish), and some light (albeit slightly simplistically infuriating) puzzle solving. The combat doesn't have an overly complex system but it's fast, smooth and very responsive and I can't tell you how glad I am Ninja Theory didn't succumb to the temptation of Matrix style acrobatics. Despite the basic mechanic I found with the threat of permadeath looming like a noose caused me to make incredibly stupid mistakes multiple times because it increased the stress. Over all the fighting is fun but if you've played DMC or Dark Souls or games of that ilk you might find it boring or too easy. In that case I'd suggest putting a headset on, close your eyes and rely on Senua's voices to guide you through. See how THAT goes.
After about 2 hours I began thinking Senua might already be dead, but the truth is far worse.
Anyway. The game looks simply stunning, it honestly puts so many AAA titles to shame by how it looks, how it plays and the story itself. It's well cast so you really feel at times that you're right there with Senua, taking every blow when you mistime a block or aren't fast enough outrunning some hellish horror.
I highly recommend taking your time with this and find ALL the Rune lodestones. Not only do you get some interesting lore and Norse mythology but if you find them all you get a bonus cutscene that really ties it all together. I think if you speed run it you won't get anywhere near as much out of it.
I can't recommend this game enough. It's an actual 11/10.

Wow.
What an incredible game.
You can really see the attention to detail and accuracy of the game developers in depicting mental illness in an interesting and exciting storyline.
As far as gameplay goes, you can expect dark souls-type combat with lots of puzzles to figure out. Progression is extremely linear, and there are no decision points. Normally, that would turn me off from a game, but with the topic being mental illness and psychosis, one of the main takeaways should be to empathize with the level of helplessness someone suffering from pschosis feels.  Just as Senua doesn't get to turn off the voices in her head, so too do you as the player not get to determine the path ahead.  One thing I came to realize as I was finishing the game  was that as much as it is about mental illness, it's also about the human condition in general. Death will confront all of us eventually. How will you handle loss? How will you survive when your loved ones leave you or give up on you? You may not hear voices in your head, but even in our modern society of science and rationality, we still struggle to understand and process death. Senua's Sacrifice helps show the weaknesses and the strengths of the human person found through the process of grieving.
The graphics and game audio also deserve a huge round of applause. This game sets the bar for me as far as realistic human features and movement go; just worlds beyond any other game I have ever played. It's almost painful to realize new games coming out right now aren't going to look this good.
My only critique would be the music towards the vey end gets less celtic and more modern...it felt a little unimmersive. Overall, I highly recommend this game.
EDIT:
Obligatory "play with headphones". I should also add that I switch to a controler early on because I'm very used to the For Honor system of combat, and the game feels very similar to For Honor in how you lock onto opponents and have to make split second decisions to block, parry, or dodge.

So to start off here, this game was on my wishlist for a long time, since it was released on steam if memory serves correct. I received $20 for christmas, and was between buying either AKIBA'S TRIP, or Rocket League. I am so happy I chose this one. This game was a lot of fun from the get go. I got into it for the "combat" aspect, and stayed for the awesome story. I only had a chance to play this for about a hour initially, afterward it was all I could think about. I wanted more, I hungered for the story. I wish I was more of a writer so that I could give this a proper review. Alas, I'm not.
When I went to purchase Akiba's Trip I was initially worried about the 30 fps frame lock. As soon as I got in, I found this to have been a silly thing to worry about. The game doesn't look bad in 30 fps. I'm used to playing games in 60 fps on my rig, and while yes it is nice, I really didn't notice the frame lock in it. I had a few issues with the game starting up, but once it was running, nothing happened to it. I found this in my case the game didn't appreciate being in fullscreen, but would run just fine in windowed mode. Not a very big drawback in my book.
Combat was fun for most of the game, but it tended to get a little boring at parts, though it was intense. Essentially you brawl with the enemies and attack three regions: the head, torso, and legs. Each region has its own health and when you damage it enough, you are then able to strip the enemy of their clothing in that region. At a certain point in the game you gain the ability to "chain strip". When you strip an enemy of an article of clothing, if there is more enemies that have clothing that is ready to come off, you get a button you have to push. If you push that correct button, you move to the next target and remove that piece of clothing. This chain can go up to somewhere around 10 (don't quote me on that) consecutive strips before your character does a special move where you press an extra button, and something "good" happens. I'll leave that part for you boys and girls to find out on your own.
Customization in this game is fun, you can customize all of your clothing, items, and weapons all the way down to what underwear you are using. You are allowed to see your partner's equipment from the get go, but you aren't allowed to do anything with it until maybe halfway into the story. I went from wearing a boring T-shirt and jeans to a military uniform at the end of the game. The possibilities are endless. Well, as endless as you can get anyway.
I played this game in English, and the voice acting was actually rather good. I didn't spot any translation hiccups throughout it, except for the ones that were purposely done. Though I was rather tired while playing most of the game. The voices picked for the characters was spot on in my opinion, someone needed to be shy sounding, they sounded shy. Someone needed to sound smart, they sounded smart.
Story...story. Difficult one to approach withough giving spoilers, but if I had to put a general description on it... It would be halfway your typical run of the mill save the world story, and half a sci fi romantic thriller. Or something like that. I don't wanna go into too much detail, but It's like: boy is kidnapped, girl rescues boy, boy helps girl fight supernatural monsters that want to terrorize city. I don't describe it as very appealing do I? It's one story that had me engrossed the whole time, so they obviously did something right, as I'm a bit of a stickler on stories. If I'm willing to go through all the trouble to play through all the routes in this game, I'm hooked. Speaking of, there is 5 different routes you can take in this game, sorta like a VN but, more engaging.
As for actually playing this game, I would HIGHLY recommend a controller. I didn't try it out with the mouse and keyboard, but just from the few times I moved the mouse or accidently pressed a button, I imagine it would be a nightmare.
As for an overall rating for this game, I would give a solid 9/10. Had the combat been just a bit more......exciting (?) I would have given it a 10/10. I am currently in my second round of playing the game and plan on getting the whole way through all five routes. Geez, I made a bit of an essay didn't I, whoopsies. In the end, if I had to pay for this game again, I definately would, even at the full price.
tl;dr: You really should take the time to read what someone works hard on to write, but if you have a controller (or not), like anime, and enjoy beating people up and/or stealing their clothes, go for it!

This is one of these cases where i would choose a more ambivalent option than "yes" or "no" if steam would allow it.
If you were bored by it before you will be bored now after the update as well.
However if you like the concept of No Mans Sky and only didn't buy/play it because it felt too unfinished now is a good time to grab it (on sale exclusively, its still not worth 60 dollars by any means.)
They spread the game out more (Which is good because you no longer feel like you've seen everything after 2 hours)
They gave you actual things to do (base building, crop growing, vehicles you can work to obtain and more)
They polished it up (performance is acceptable on my older mid tier rig now)
They are working to implement multiplayer
They used community mods as indicators which features were missing and which should be removed or changed. (might seem lazy but what better way is there to determine which changes should be prioritised?)
They made the achievement messages skippable (No more running for your life in panic because your amazing "milestone" of having played the game for 5 minute keeps you from using your weapon!)
Its still a more shallow game than some might expect and it requires a certain ability to immerse yourself.
Before you buy make sure you understand what kind of game this is because there is still a lot of misinformation!
If you are looking for a more hardcore (read: more features, no handholding) gaming experience with similar/related features i recommend checking out Empyrion - Galactic Survival.

This game is consistently available for under 20 cents.
It's not great, but it does two things exceedingly well that are rare features in many other games, AAA or indie:
1) Fairly impressive terrain destruction. Instead of handling destructible terrain in the traditional way of having set destructible parts of the environment which will explode in a physics-based manner, Caster just creates entire levels out of fully terraform-able terrain. It's easy to create dents, craters, hills, and mountains out of the world around you on a whim, and that feels pretty cool.
2) Empowering movement. Your character has two big movement abilities which make it very easy to cover huge distances in short time. There's a "super jump," which behaves like a double jump with absurd height to it, and a dash ability which increases movement speed, and allows you to run on water and up any walls. It feels fantastic and I haven't played with anything quite like it before.
Outside of those two features, Caster is pretty dull. The combat, music, aesthetics, graphics, and general polish are all sorely lacking. That said, if you can spare fifteen cents and fifteen minutes, I'd recommend checking this game out for just long enough to experience how fluid and satisfying it is to run around in this game's world.

Pros:
Interesting Story.
Mechanics learnt gradually.
Re-playable missions.
Good mixture of stealth and combat.
Good combat mechanics.
Cons:
Repetitive missions.
Un-skippable long cut-scenes.
Music is short and only plays at certain times, leaving long periods with only abidance sounds.
Story:
Assassin's Creed has two main stories: That of the present with bartender Desmond Miles who has been captured by a large pharmaceutical company called Abstergo and forced to re-live the genetic memories of his ancestor Altair, and that of Altair himself, who is an Assassin in 1192, during the Third Crusade, sent on a mission to kill nine men who bring war apon the land.
Desmond is told that Abstergo seeks information from him, and that a machine which can make him relive the memories of Altair will help uncover than information. While in the past, Altair makes a series of deadly mistakes which harms the Assassin Brotherhood. He is demoted by his master and sent on a mission to kill nine men. Some of them Crusaders, some of the Saracens. But all are working together for an odd purpose under the leadership of the French Crusader, Robert de Sabre. With each kill, a rank, equipment and abilities are returned to Altair and he will learn more about why these nine men work together.
Assassin's Creed largely takes place in the Holy Land of 1192 in five locations: The mountain fort and village of Masyf which is home of the Assassins, The Saracen-controlled cities of Damascus and Jerusalem, the Crusader-controlled city of Arce, and the Kingdom, which represents the lands in-between all four cites.
In Damascus, Jerusalem and Arce, three each of these men wait. Altair must travel to them and preform investigations to uncover his target's location and use the information to decide how to approach and kill each target.
Mechanics:
In order to find a target, Altair must preform a series of Investigations. These take several forms: Eavesdropping on conversations to learn information, pickpocketing letters which explain more about his target's purpose and helping fellow Assassin's by assassinating other targets amongst others.
While playing as Altair, you spend your time in one of two states: Low Profile and High Profile, which are changed by pressing a button. In Low Profile, Altair preforms socially acceptable but slower actions, allowing him to navigate his way without drawing attention, such as following a target or remaining hidden. In High Profile, Altair preforms aggressive and socially unacceptable actions, allowing him to run or enter combat. Knowing the right time to use Low or High Profile is key.
The Blend mechanic allows Altair to blend crowds to help me remain hidden. This can be done either alone, or within groups of roaming monks to help him access places guarded. If guards are chasing him, he can attempt to blend within crowds, benches or haystacks to lose their sight of him and return to being hidden.
Almost every building or surface is climbable, allowing free running and parkour to get you to locations and out of trouble, from leaping from beam-to-mean, to climbing up a tall spire. If it sticks out, you can grab onto it. This also allows you to see the city surroundings.
Once investigations have been completed, Altair can then attempt to assassinate his target, which can often be done in multiple ways. The environment allows for multiple approaches to a target, and mission replayability means a player can play the mission again and try to assassinate a target in a diffrent style.
Each time a target is killed, Altair and the target engage in conversation, and each target always defends their actions, believing they are doing good and leaves Altair wondering if they really are deserving of death.
Combat mechanics:
Altair has access to five weapons: A sword, dagger, hidden blade, throwing knives and his fists. The sword is a slow but powerful weapon, the dagger is faster than the sword, but deals less damage. The hidden blade is a one-hit, one-kill weapon, but only to character who are unaware of Altair. The fists are used for beat-up missions, where Altair attempts to get information from un-cooperative people.
Combat is preformed in the both Low and High Profile states, and which state you are in determines the actions taken. For example: Wielding a sword in Low Profile and pressing Action allows Altair to attack, built pressing Action in High Profile allows Altair to counter an attack in-stead.
Altair can also grab people to throw them off ledges to their deaths, or just down on the ground so they are out of combat for a few seconds. However, the enemies also have access to the same abilities Altair has. Enemies are split into three categories: Solders, Elites and Commanders: Solders are weak but often come in larger numbers. They take only a few hits to die and die to one counter-attack. Elites deal more damage, have more health, can grab and throw Altair, and take two counter-attacks to die. Commanders have even more damage and health than Elites, can break Altair's defence to leave him exposed to an attack, can counter-attack themselves and die to three counter-attacks. The can easily be identified by their uniform. Diffrent combat stratus are needed to fight depending on who you are facing.
Music:
Music is good, but sparse. Every time Altair enters a new location, a certain music track will play, but it is short, acting more like an announcing theme than actual music, and won't play again for some time. There is also a track for Altair being chased and Altair in combat, depending on what city he is in. While outside of combat, music is replaced by ambience.
Other:
There are alot of collectables: Each location has one hundred flags to collect (with the exception of Masyf, which has twenty) as well as sixty Templars to assassinate spread over the Holy Land and View Points to Synchronise. All locations can be revisited after the first time there.
Overall, a great game. Well-written story but the cut-scenes are long and un-skippable, so any replays means you have to watch them all the time. Missions can be replayed to assassinate a target how they want and in a diffrent style each time, but investigations often lack variety. Hunting collectables can be fun, but also irritating without a guide after so many have been found.

If you played Assassin's Creed IV: Black Flag before trying this game, you are going to be dissatisfied with the controller layout and overall feel of the game. But storyline-wise, PLAY IT.
If you are like me and love playing console originals that have been ported to PC with a controller, then I would not suggest sitting too far away from the screen with this game. When it says partial controller support, it means it. The first time you run the game you are gonna be required to use the keyboard and mouse to skip the long intro cutscene (you are gonna want to do this every time you run it actually) and to actually get to the main menu. After that, you gonna need to re-map ALL of the controls. The triggers don't register, so use the bumpers instead. Not to mention, if you are indeed coming from some of the later AC's, the combat and parkour system will feel VERY sluggish/non-responsive. But this is the first game: of course it will be that way.
Beyond that, the game is awesome so far. The storyline, I will agree, is VERY repetitive, but pay attention to the meetings with the leader. This is definitely where they introduce the Templars and WHY the Assassins hate them. Not to mention, you start to see the changes in both Altaïr and Desmond with every meeting / Animus break.
Okay, time for my little goings-on about the graphics.
While not as intensive as Black Flag, the graphics for AC1 are both crisp and pretty detailed given when the game was published.
Overall, 9/10 because of repetitiveness. Granted, basically having the job of "Hitman" would be pretty repetitive - "Go here. Kill this guy. Come back unseen."

+ Various weapons and fighting styles, use hidden blades and swords to strike down foes.
+ Free climbing and running, you can scale walls and buildings. A lot of the environment can be interacted with.
- Constant crashing on the latest GPU's, GTX 970 4 GB (2015), to the point of being unplayable.
- The game world seemed really dull during my brief playthrough. It's quite bleak and lacks a lot of colour. The controls were also an abomination.
- Graphically it's nothing fantastic. Even during release it was arguably poor graphics for its time.
- For a game about assassination it's surprisingly lacklustre when it comes to the act itself. It's not really a stealth game, there aren't many creative ways to carry out assassinations...it's just odd. Assassin's Creed II struggled with this as well, but it was far more fun and interesting, so I can forgive it.
- Constant repetition with menial tasks, like eavesdropping, interrogation and pickpocketing. Boring.
- Pause interface is obstructive and annoying.
Overall Score 4/10
In my experience the games in the Assassin's Creed series are decent but have never had that 'wow' factor. Assassin's Creed is probably the worst, and well worth skipping. Starting with Assassin's Creed II is your best bet. You won't miss out on much of the vital story anyway, and you'll save yourself from this painful game.

9/10 If you/re into the point and click genre, you will definitely like Syberia. Syberia is a classic point and click quest. This game did not brought anything new to genre, there is no challenging puzzles, but still, this is one of the best games in this niche.
Kate Walker, a young lawyer from the United States, arrives in tiny european town to sign a contract with owners of old toy factory. At first this journey looks like a routine job, but it quickly turns into long, difficult and amazingly interesting adventure.
Game is very beautiful. Art style is fantastic, every screen is well created with a lot of attention for small details. Also, there is excellent, slightly melancholic soundtrack, that fits perfectly for the mood of the game.
Storyline is well designed, characters are charismatic and it was especially interesting for me to observe how gradually changes the personality of Kate Walker. With time she realizes that money and career is not the most important thing in life, there is something else... something important and special. From my point of view, Kate Walker is attractive and interesting character, she got true individuality. Ending of the first part is one of the most touching scenes i had ever seen in games. I took a tissue.
Puzzles are logical, they fit well in the story, i did not noticed anything annoying or non-logical. Puzzles are interesting enough but not difficult or challenging and maybe it is for the best, so they do not distract player from the story.
Can i give a little criticism to this game? Well... i did not like the animation of characters. Kate Walker looks good enough, but other characters move as dummies. It looks especially ugly if compare animation of characters with stunningly beautiful suroundings.
Sometimes there is a little too much of old cliche. Crossing the border between Europe and Russia looks like expedition into depths of Mordor. And when it comes for Russia there is always "slums, bums and drunkards" and other "winter-vodka-bear" stuff. Well...
...nevermind, i just can not criticise this game. Syberia had touched my soul.
I played a lot of games and i can say this words for only few of them: this is masterpiece. Strongly recommended.

My friend gifted me this game nearly two years ago and I cannot thank them enough. Skullgirls is the only 2D fighting game I've really gotten into and I normally don't mind fighting games. The game is simple to understand and even decent to play with a keyboard (controller is definitely preferred, though), even for a noob like me.
Skullgirls has enough fanservice, risque and references to other games and shows, to keep it interesting.
The lore is also interesting and makes me want to learn more about the characters in the game. I really wish that LabZero would add more DLC characters to expand the plot (or release a comic of some sort. I'd love that too). I would definitely buy more DLC for this game if they came out with it (I already own all DLC at this time.)
The art in the game is absolutely beautiful. As an artist myself, Skullgirls has heavily influenced my art style. It's a nice balance between more western style and also anime style. The music in the game is also excellent and fits perfect with the stages in the game. (Fun fact: the composer for Skullgirls is the composer for the Castlevania series!)
There are a few issues, though. The anti-infinite combo system could be better. It only works on legit combos, even though you can still catch a person and spam them to death without it counting as a combo (unless my friend and I just don't know how to escape lol). It also takes a bit to build up so even when the attacks do count as a combo, the enemy could still do a huge amount of damage to you.
LabZero has also announced that they are not updating the Steam version any further while (I believe) the Playstation 4 version still recieves updates.
LabZero has a great series in their hands and I will continue to support their future content.

With Dragonball FighterZ on the way and Marvel vs Capcom Infinite coming out in a few days. I wanted to take the time to reflect on one of the better 3v3 fighters out there. Skullgirls offers both a suprising depth and accessibility to people who have never played either a fighting game or a 3v3 fighting game. For me, this was the first fighting game I got into after seeing a video on it. I was impressed by how well animated the sprites were. The first thing I tell people who want to learn fighting games is to buy this and play the tutorial. Unlike other fighting games with as the street fighter series, Skullgirls tutorial offers a look into important concepts. For example there is a part of the tutorial for both how to do mix ups, practice blocking mix ups, and where mix ups are not safe on block and can be punished. The gameplay on the other hand is different. While not revolutionary like the tutorial system, it offers a robust mechanically deep gameplay. The netcode is also phenomenal allowing to set the amount of buffer frames. The 2 downsides to online play is that in my experience it takes forever to get a match and if you are a beginner you are going to get your♥♥♥♥♥handed to you by people who know every reset within a combo and how to extend a combo to avoid the anti infinite system for as long as possible.
EDIT: Apparently the netcode is rollback not frame delay. It uses GGPO netcode so its not the same as SFV's rollback netcode.

Okay. I want to get something out of the way that has been making me rethink I still want to play this. Now, this game has DLC characters that are all seperate, etc. as well as a character color bundle. Now I bought all these as soon as I could, and apparently they were free? I don't know, I guess I didn't have the game at that time, BUT that's not the issue. The issue is when an upgrade came around.
The Skullgirls 2nd Encore Upgrade came after all the DLC characters were released as well as the colors. This 'upgrade' or 'update' as I'll call it adds some more modes, voice acting, but more importantly, it includes 'all DLC characters as well as the character color bundle'. Do you see the issue? I bouhht these things before that was even released, which the upgrade was spaced out over a wide amount of time, in which I probably would have bought the characters and colors anyway, BEFORE it got released. It literally shpuld have JUST been an update, not a 15 dollar DLC.
But, besides my upsetted nature towards having to pay for a duplicate copy of the DLC I have and feel like I wasted money, I enjoy the game. It's a fast-paced 2-D fighter that, in my opinion, is better than say, Mortal Kombat because of it's 'fast'-like nature; it feels way faster and more of like an anime than realistic fighting, which is slow and can sometimes feel clunky. Maybe it's just the way it is, but I like it way better.
It doesn't have all that many characters like a big AAA franchise fighter like Mortal Kombat, but it's not always about the fighter amount. every character in Skullgirls plays very different, aside from Ms. Fortune and Robo Fortune; only slight changes are made between each. For the most part combos that usually work with one character don't with the other. All in all, it's a fun fighter game that I'd recommend to people, even with my somewhat salty demeanor beforehand.

Shower With Your Dad Simulator is mainly different minigames revolving around a kid and his dad showering. Sometimes, when reloading a level, you have a minigame to play.
Endurodad is the first mode you can try. In it, you choose your pair between three fathers and their kids. Your goal is to reach your dad before the time's out. But if you're showering with the wrong one, it's the end of the round too! Many powerups can appear on the screen: a beer, while not perfect to see, is at least slowing time, the adventure map changes your dad during a limited time, another one is making you have two dads (which means less chance to end up wrong). The more you're scoring, the more complicated it will be: dads being curtains, dads being added, signs slowing you, puddles making you slide, etc..
Dadathlon is based on the same mechanics than Eurodad, apart that you're not choosing your dad: each time, the kid is changing, so it's up to you to find the right one.
Dad Divisions is a mode where the dads are falling down. You need to get them before they touch the ground. But to make sure you don't take the wrong one, you'll have to change the kid.
Soapico is a point-&-click adventure (not taking long) where your dad is an investigator and is trying to find what happened.
The Dad With the Iron Shower is a mode where you need to avoid three ninjas kids and any object thrown at you by the Ninja Daddy.
Inglorious Bathdads is a mode where the kid is in a flying tube and has to touch the tube where his dad is. You can also gun down the others.
That's the content of the game. In reality, the fun comes because you're challenged, either by the achievements or by trying to beat your score.
But it's the humor in it and the fact that it's a parody of a simulator that makes the game very enjoyable. The powerups are not quite recommended for kids - I think about the beer for example. I also appreciated the two dads option, because it's making the job easier and also because of the symbolism of it being included.
The graphics are in the wave of retro gaming: it's pixelised and it's probably a way to avoid criticism about sex as the kids and the dads are naked. So, yeah, there is the equipement between the legs being pictured.
The soundtrack is also good. It's a joy to hear it during your games.
So yeah, Shower With Your Dad Simulator may be cheap but the fun provided in it is real. You make a real bargain here. Don't hesitate at all!

Ultimately enjoyable, but still left some things to be desired.
Having played (and loved) Life is Strange, and hearing that the rewind mechanic was based Dontnod's first game, i was excited to play it.
Aesthetically, the game is lovely. The soundtrack was incredibly unexpected, a huge, sweeping score that could easily be taken from a cyber-punk, Star Wars-esque cinematic opera. The city of Neo Paris is incredibly vibrant, multi-faceted, and really quite beautiful. The combination of these two as you step out of the tunnels and into Slum 404 for the first time was really a moment to behold, and combined with the background history and information that you aquire throughout the game, the world feels deep and absorbing. I desperately wish we could have seen more of it.
The story is very good too, although it sometimes feels like you're constantly changing direction and targets, with no overall goal in sight. This is entirely necessary for the story to play out the way it does, but it's not exactly the most compelling way to move a story forward; it feels very disjointed sometimes. The main character Nilin is sympathetic though (with some *stellar* voice-work) and the surroundings are great to just wander around sometimes. The calm of the Valet robots that look so human and continue to do their jobs cleaning/repairing/(whoring) as the world falls to crap is really entertaining.
Mechanics-wise, the memory remixes are fun, interesting puzzles that lead you to think about the wider ramifications of memories and their power, and you spend a lot of time climbing Tomb Raider-style, with plenty of hidden loot.
BUT most of the game was less memory-hunter based, and more generic 3D beat 'em up/ brawler style. Considering the tone of the game, that seemed a little brainless and repetitive; i was surprised actually. There was WAY too much running down corridors, fighting off multiple waves of enemies, and then running down more corridors. In fact that was 80-90% of the game. A little Final Corridor 13-ish.
I'm not a fan of a combo-based fight system either, and this one felt particularly restrictive, with only 2 buttons to use and a specific timing required to land them successfully. The S-pressens with the timer system and the Jammer did a little to alleviate the repetition, but really i think the game would have been much better with more puzzles, more Neo Paris, fewer(/no?) enemies (outside of bosses)  and with the S-Pressens as the basic fight system.
That probably would have saved me from a few of the game-breaking bugs that this game still suffers with too, mostly happening when a cinematic doesn't play after a fight, or when you're just casually walking somewhere and randomly die because the game has decided you're out of bounds. God bless the Steam Community for their fixes.
Despite my complaints, it's 100% worth playing if you're looking to play something refreshingly non-FPSy and atmospheric. If you're a sci-fi fan (Blade Runner etc.) you'll probably enjoy it, and definitely if you're a brawler fan.

Running With Rifles is a game in which you start out as a simple grunt in an army filled with hundreds of people. It's a simple looking game that can run even on my toaster. You start out as a Private in either the Greenebelts (BOOO) Graycollars (BOO YOU STINK ASWELL) or the Brownpants (YEEEEEEEEEAH!) Depending on what faction you choose when creating a new campaign, you'll be sent to one of the vast, diverse maps. Soon, if you're doing what you should be, you should get into a huge, bloody firefight trying to capture a sector, watching your comrades fall before you, and maybe even dying yourself. But don't worry, death isn't permanent. There's a lot I can say about this game, but to keep it simple I'll just list what I like, dislike, and want in the future.
What I like:
- The ranking system. Start out as a private, kill enemies and capture objectives to get XP, rank up. When you become a corporal you get a mobile radio that allows you to call in mortar salvos, which can be useful if you need to unwedge some pesky Graycollars.
- The radio. You expend RP (resource points, which you get from trading in weapons and collectables) to call in support, such as mortar salvos, reinforcements, and eventually as you rank up even more, artillery salvos and tanks.
- The weapons. Weapons are taken from real life (M16, AK47, LAWs, etc.) and add to the immersion of the game
-Firefights. The firefights you get into in this game are amazing. Watching as a bridge that had nothing but Jersey barriers and abandoned cars turn into a battleground with blood spilled everywhere, corpses strewn about and wrecks of cars is just, ohhh it's so amazing.
- Day-to-night cycle. It's not always daytime in a battle. I dunno if this happens or not, but it'd be interesting to see both sides pull back during night to recuperate and resume fighting the next day.
-The maps. Maps are all varied, some big, entrenched sections of land, some small coastal cities, some tiny peaceful isles caught in the middle of a bloody war. My favorite has to be Black Gold Estuary
- The graphics. Nice and simple, not too demanding. Hope they never change.
RWR is a pretty great game, but there's still some things that I don't like.
- The AI is a bit wonky while driving. Sometimes if you hop in a car with them driving they may turn back and not go to the objective, but other than that they're fine.
- Lack of naval assault/ land assault vehicles. You get APCs that have an autocannon turret, a tank, and sometimes a Humvee, but most of the time you'll get jeeps. For naval assaults you get a rubber boat which doesn't offer much protection, and on Black Gold Estuary you get a badass patrol boat that is armored and armed to the teeth. More on these next.
- The Squad AI is pretty bad in my opinion. If I tell them to move to a position, they should seek out the nearest cover, because most of the time I'm behind sandbags and my squad is hovering around behind me getting picked off by Graycollars.
- 3-faction maps. ♥♥♥♥ those, they're fun the first time playing them but after awhile they get stale, boring, and frustatingly hard. Especially Power Junction. The smallest map in the entire campaign is a King of The Hill map, that's fine. But three ♥♥♥♥ing factions? On the smallest map going for one point? No, it's just too hard to enjoy.
So there's not that much wrong with the game besides wonky acting AI, and the lack of boats. There's some other things I'd like to see in the future of this game.
What'd I'd like to see:
- Halftracks. A mix between a tank, a troop transport, and an APC.
- Higgins boats/ AAVs (Assault Amphibious Vehicles) , just to give landing forces a bit more protection.
- More banter between the soldiers, it'd add to immersion.
- Limited ammo as a toggleable feature. You don't have unlimited ammo for your rifles, and when you run out you either scavenge for weapons or you go back to the armory to resupply. I think it'd make the mobile armory more importance.
Overrall a 9/10, fun game.

Overall I loved it. Get this game if you like platformers and beautifully composed game experiences.

NEW REVIEW...
All right. It's gotten a LOT better from last time. Honestly, I now think it's quite a good game. You can no longer kill yourself instantly by falling off a two-foot ledge, the guns feel like they suck much less, and vehicles handle better.
Really, I only have one complaint: the AI, and its problems with vehicles. Jesus Christ, the AI.
So most of this game revolves around getting places quickly to capture objectives and kill people. Naturally, this means you'll need vehicles. Unfortunately, you'll never get anything, because the AI is a bunch of kleptomaniacal ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s who will steal them at the first opportunity and go joyriding. And I do mean joyriding, because they will not do anything useful. The tanks will go away from the enemy, the transports just go around in circles, there are MASSIVE pileups in narrow areas as your robo-team tries to send a tank down an alley sideways.
It's really annoying. Fortunately, the rest of the game is really pretty fun.
The maps are pretty damn fan. They're huge, and there's cover EVERYWHERE for you to squat behind and plink away at the foe (human or silicon). Getting into a big fight in an enclosed space is a ton of fun, because everybody's slaughtering each other without mercy, and the streets are painted red.  You can call in airstrikes and paratroopers and machine-gun nests and it's awesome.
I actually do recommend this, now. There feels like there's been a lot of improvement. The vehicles work, the guns work, pretty much everything works. And don't get me wrong about the AI--the tank thing is really annoying, but it's hardly game-breaking. Playing infantry is still much more fun anyway.
And the most important thing of all: IT HAS A TUTORIAL! THANK GOD! It's surprisingly complex for a top-down shooting gallery, and I really recommend doing it.
So, yeah, it's pretty good. I'd recommend it most for people with a bunch of bros who can do it together--otherwise, wait for a sale.
OLD REVIEW FOR POSTERITY:
Ugghhh... Where to start?
This is one of those "where the ♥♥♥♥ do you go" kind of games, in a big way. You're constantly bombarded with these radio messages which mean... absolutely  nothing.
The loadout system has  a major flaw, in that it is impossible to figure out how to use it. If you try to figure anything out, pause even for a second to figure out what the ♥♥♥♥ you want to do, you'll get shot by an offscreen enemy, and respawn in a location where your character has to make his INCREDIBLY slow way back to the front lines.
You can't hit any damn thing with the guns, because the spread on the game's "medium" rifle makes a shotgun look like a scalpel, and the rest of the guns have some incredible drawback that you'll never know about until you get killed trying to use it.
Vehicles are OK, but they're so unwieldy and unprotected that you might as well just walk.
There's an elevation feature which would normally make for interesting gameplay, but it relies on some kind of line-of-sight system that doesn't really work. So you can only shoot people at the same height as you, or a different height so long as they're on the very edge of the screen where individual bullets are spread to six feet apart.
All allied and enemy units have these really cool weapons, that you aren't allowed to use for reasons that completely escape me.
Trying to get your hands on a grenade is damn near impossible. Trying to throw them, even more so. Why can't I just press G and throw it? I have no damn clue. Usually, the grenade hits a wall or something next to you because of the idiotic elevation system that makes no sens, and you get blown up.
At least the AI is good, though. If you like being pushed out of cover to get shot, and then left alone on the battlefield while the rest of the team stays in their base.
Also, what the hell's up with that bar on the bottom of the screen? It just kinda twitches around and acts pointless.

Hellblade is a moving, brutal, gutwrenching epic. I enjoyed every minute of it. Hats off to Ninja Theory for taking such a big risk with the story. I can't remember a time when a game created a sense of empathy for me. I felt Senua's pain and suffering throughout the whole story. If this were a movie, it would be Oscar material. This game should win every GOTY award out there.

In nearly every department, the quality of this game is A+.
Graphics, everything looks fantastic, with very few exceptions given there are some muddy looking textures here and there. But it goes beyond just visual fidelity, the way that shadows, light, and various screen effects are used are very mind-bending and awesome to look at.
The voice acting and acting in general (it's all pretty much live-action, either via motion capture or video) is superb. I don't think there's anything to critisize here in the slightest from what I've seen and heard.
The story is, for me, quite enthralling, learning about all of these old Gods and myths both through word-of-mouth in the game, and experiencing them first hand is very entertaining, as well as Senua's own story and background unravelling as you progress. Some people didn't like the ending from a gameplay perspective, but I appreciate what they were conveying with it, and I believe it did its job well.
Gameplay can get a little repetitive or frustrating at times. The combat is fairly simple, there are some different enemy types, you have light/heavy attacks, block/parry, dodge, and kick, as well as a "focus" mechanic where time slows down for a short period. It can be quite entertaining, but basically boils down to just dodging and/or parrying and then spamming your light and heavy attacks until you need to dodge/parry again. It can feel very visceral and satisfying slicing up foes though.
The puzzles don't vary too much, most of them revolving around aligning yourself with certain symbols made using the environment and "focusing" on them, plays on perspective, amongst other things. Occasionally these were frustrating when I got a bit lost trying to find that one last symbol, only for it to be something that looks nothing like the symbol I'm trying to find.
Audio, once again, fantastic, the binaural recording to simulate the voices in your head does as it's intended, with voices sometimes sounding like they're whispering right into your ear (possibly triggering your ASMR if you experience it!) They also have a gameplay purpose, warning you of incoming attacks from behind, as well as giving indicators to your health (on top of visual cues).
Overall, if you're looking for a unique, linear, heavily story-driven experience with some "okay" combat thrown in, go ahead and pick this up. Especially if you like more mind-bending experiences.

Very interesting idea for a game. You play as a local historian who goes to a mysterious mansion no one knows anything about. Once there, you are greeted by a ghost girl named Spooky and are told to survive 1000 rooms of terror. From there, things seem docile.
That doesn't last.
The title was a turn off for me because I won't lie, I detest games that overuse jump scares. And a running "gag" throughout this game takes the form of cardboard cutouts of cute things (and sometimes not so cute things) that make loud noises and appear at random. If that's all the game had going for it, I probably wouldn't have played through to room 1000.
Thankfully, there's more to this game than that.
Not only is it loaded with references to famous video games (ranging from Silent Hill, the Shadow Temple from Ocarina of Time and many more), but it manages to actually have a very good atmosphere. Various noises manage to be creepy, like moaning or the sound a monster makes. The monsters themselves also have a good variety to them, and it's paced so that you'll constantly have to tackle new challenges. Some monsters you just book it from. Others you need to stare at or else they'll follow you and end your life quickly (in what is definitely one of the creepiest Weeping Angel enemies I've seen in a game).
That's about it really. Apparently there are two endings to this game and the one I got was... bizarre, to say the least. I don't feel compelled to get the other one, but still, this is a worthwhile game with a solid atmosphere and good monster variety. Just prepare to hate cardboard cutouts because even for someone like me, they're incredibly startling.
Plus, this game is free. So you literally have nothing to lose by trying it. So give it a go.

Shower With Your Dad Simulator is mainly different minigames revolving around a kid and his dad showering. Sometimes, when reloading a level, you have a minigame to play.
Endurodad is the first mode you can try. In it, you choose your pair between three fathers and their kids. Your goal is to reach your dad before the time's out. But if you're showering with the wrong one, it's the end of the round too! Many powerups can appear on the screen: a beer, while not perfect to see, is at least slowing time, the adventure map changes your dad during a limited time, another one is making you have two dads (which means less chance to end up wrong). The more you're scoring, the more complicated it will be: dads being curtains, dads being added, signs slowing you, puddles making you slide, etc..
Dadathlon is based on the same mechanics than Eurodad, apart that you're not choosing your dad: each time, the kid is changing, so it's up to you to find the right one.
Dad Divisions is a mode where the dads are falling down. You need to get them before they touch the ground. But to make sure you don't take the wrong one, you'll have to change the kid.
Soapico is a point-&-click adventure (not taking long) where your dad is an investigator and is trying to find what happened.
The Dad With the Iron Shower is a mode where you need to avoid three ninjas kids and any object thrown at you by the Ninja Daddy.
Inglorious Bathdads is a mode where the kid is in a flying tube and has to touch the tube where his dad is. You can also gun down the others.
That's the content of the game. In reality, the fun comes because you're challenged, either by the achievements or by trying to beat your score.
But it's the humor in it and the fact that it's a parody of a simulator that makes the game very enjoyable. The powerups are not quite recommended for kids - I think about the beer for example. I also appreciated the two dads option, because it's making the job easier and also because of the symbolism of it being included.
The graphics are in the wave of retro gaming: it's pixelised and it's probably a way to avoid criticism about sex as the kids and the dads are naked. So, yeah, there is the equipement between the legs being pictured.
The soundtrack is also good. It's a joy to hear it during your games.
So yeah, Shower With Your Dad Simulator may be cheap but the fun provided in it is real. You make a real bargain here. Don't hesitate at all!

I really did want to like this game, but there's just too much going against it for me to recommend it. I think people are glazing over some glaring issues.
The story and cutscenes make up about 30% of the game, and another 20% is spent in really tedious U-boat story sections where you just wander around and talk to people or set up the next mission. When you start having fun with the game it sucks you right back into a cutscene. It's about 20 minutes of playing a level for another 10 minutes of cutscenes.
The game tries to pad out it's time by throwing up sidequests that just have you revisit old maps without any incentive to do them. You get absolutely nothing for doing them, and it's just a ridiculous way to stretch replayability. Retreading a map you've already done, backwards, without any story is not real content.
This game doesn't know if it wants to be a cover shooter or an oldschool shooter like DOOM. The new DOOM got it right, I played it on the hardest difficulty only taking damage when I made a mistake in navigating the arena. In this game a firefight will drain your health from full to nothing in as little as two seconds because of the enemy aimbot AI. This game is a corridor shooter where you hunker down and pick off enemies as they funnel into you. The game seems to want you to be this badass death machine, though, with the dual-wielding mechanics and the heavy weapons. On the subject of heavy weapons; they're absolutely useless. There's no reason to use them over the weapons you're given. In fact the only weapon worth using is the assault rifle on single-shot, because everything else packs absolutely no punch.
*Minor Spoilers*
YMMV with the story, but I didn't like it. The game introduces too many characters for you to care about, and ridiculous scenes like a nude Anya firing two fully automatic weapons while straddling BJ is too much for me. It's a good thing the game ends right after this cutscene with another cutscene because I legitimately checked out after that point.
There are no real boss fights, the game ends right in the middle of everything with a cutscene, setting up for another sequel.
One of the developers even says he doesn't consider the game a shooter:
Skip this game, get the new DOOM instead if you're looking for an old school shooter. Anything you might have loved about TNO won't be found in this game. I implore anyone who thinks this is a good followup to TNO replay TNO and see exactly how much has changed, because I don't think people realize how big of a shift this was from the original reboot.

Based on the overall good reviews, catchy music, and the gameplay shown in the trailer, I thought that I would really enjoy this game.  It looks like a whacky, chaotic, and fun to play arcade shooter!  However, the game fails to deliver on that front.  I will give it credit for being goofy, but it takes more than that to make for a fun game.  I would say the premise is where the silliness shines the most: you are basically a toaster that shoots bread at sentient food to stop them from attacking your clock.  Because that's bad, for some reason.  The titular Toast Time mode you activate doesn't seem to do much, though the icon that shows up is comical and enjoyable.
Getting to what makes the game not so much fun though.  Starting off, I'd say the controls are one of the worst aspects of the game.  It's not the way you target enemies, which is as simple as moving your mouse cursor where you want to shoot and clicking.  No, what screws the controls up is how strong the recoil is when you shoot.  Your character will fly back from each shot, and in order to beat stages, especially later game, you are required to maneuver your character to specific places and keep them from going to certain areas, lest they become incapable of hitting enemies because of barriers.  It becomes very aggravating trying to fire a barrage of bullets to beat back enemies while keeping your character under control at the same time.
Another aspect that makes the game unenjoyable is the graphics.  It's not the pixellation that I have a problem with, but the choice in color scheme.  The backgrounds are the only aspects that have color, whereas all important game elements are the exact same color: white.  It isn't just an aesthetic issue, but is disruptive to gameplay.  After all, just imagine playing any other game where your character, your target, your power-ups, the bullets, the platforms, and all enemies were the same color.  It's kind of amazing that it's even playable, yet it does nothing to help the player stay on top of their objective, let alone as the stage layouts become more sophisticated and difficult to navigate and the screen fills up with your bullets and waves of enemies.  If you don't believe me, just pause the trailer occasionally as it shows the gameplay, and try to figure out what you see on the screen.  I've played the game before, and it's hard for me to tell at times.  If the designers had merely given these different elements unique colors it'd be much improved.
One design feature the game has, that I find questionable, is the survival mode.  The way this mode works, it has the player go through the main levels until they fail one.  A single failure is all it takes to end your attempt at survival mode, so if you want to beat it, it requires flawless playthrough.  I will not spend my time even trying this feat (which there is an achievement for) as it is simply not worth the effort, but it's very strange to me that you can access this mode long before you even finish beating all of the main levels.  Theoretically, I could play and beat stages I haven't even gotten to yet in the main game, and considering how unforgiving this mode is, that's downright bizarre.  Definitely seems to be an oversight, though this is more a point of interest than a big complaint about the game.
The final nail in the coffin for me is the sobering statistics the achievements for the game shows.  It only has 9, with 1 of them being an achivement for playing the game for 21,000 odd seconds.  That translates to just under 6 hours.  Even most of those who give a positive review of the game fail to complete this achievement.  Out of all of the reviewers, only 4 spent enough time playing to complete it.  I know most games nowadays, especially cheap ones like this, don't have very long play times.  However, if this game were better designed, this achievement completion rate would easily be hitting the double digit mark, not stagnating at less than 1%.  Steam tells me I've spent less than an hour playing the game myself, but I feel like I've put more time into the game than that, which is not a compliment by the way.  I recommend you spend your less than 6 hours of time doing something else than playing this game.  After all, you've probably spent more time in your life eating toast and enjoyed it more than you would playing this game.

A greatly underrated little game with amazingly energetic music.
Basically a shooter, you use the mouse to aim at silly little smiling monsters who are trying to break your alarm clock.  Your guy Terry isn't hurt by monsters himself, but wherever he fires, he's flung in the opposite direction.  At first this isn't much of an issue, but it isn't too far in where you're having to choose your shots carefully to stop your heroic slice of toast from getting hurled behind barriers and unable to hit his grinning foes.  Additionally crates fall from the sky; shooting one gives Terry a random powerup from all those unlocked.  Some of these require quite a bit of skill to use, but others fill the screen in a gratifying spray of breakfast ordinance.
Additionally, each level rates you on the now-traditional three star scale.  Getting that third star in later levels can become a heroic undertaking.  Sometimes it feels as if the third star, on certain levels, requires getting a specific powerup, which is a bit tiring.  Still though, it is a fun little game that's worth a few dollars at least, and has been nearly invisible in terms of promotion.  It's worth a look!

Mixes very good with very bad.
On the plus side, as you can see from the shots, the background art is stunning and imaginative. Also the clockwork fantasy theme appeals on a subjective level, and the script and voice acting are generally fine, bar a few odd casting moments (a cockney-scripted npc read in a jarringly posho way, for example) and fair few irritating characters. Puzzle-wise, the game is pretty fair, especially to begin with, and pixle-hunting is minimal throughout.
However it grows increasingly exasperating, with multiple instances of a path, or action, somewhere behind you being arbitrarily "unlocked" only after completing an unrelated action, hence there is a lot of aimless back-tracking. This is made all the more painful, and less forgivable, by the lack of any "fast-travel" function, and the almost absurdly expansive areas go from being an asset to a curse. Some of this is excusable given the game's age, whereas some leads to the conclusion that the game was simply rushed, as the ambition shown by the landscape design isn't quite matched for quality by the rest of the game.
Overall the game would be far better if the work done on the game-world was halved and that time was spent on polishing the puzzles and features instead. The positives will be enough for some (including myself) to soldier through but your patience will be tested.

While I cant say its my favorite game, RWR is probly my multiplayer shooter in a long time. It's large maps, team based game play, and 'your not a hero just a solider' feel are not only novel, they just happen to be fun at the same time!
The game rewards a tatical player, while it naturaly shuns the run and gunner's certain FPS games, makes. If you treat each situation like you might catch a stray bullet and die, you might survive. If you run out there... you will probly die.
Even the stand alone game in single player, is fun. You can capture enmy weapon your faction dose not naturaly produce, and eventualy, your faction will crank the new weapons out just the same. You earn experiance, gain ranks, and are rewarded with more and more gameplay mechanics. Squad members, radio abilitys, etc.
Plus to top it all off, it has a hilariously fitting soundtrack.
If I could add anything to the game, I'd ask for at least one more faction. Lets face it, Green Belts, Grey Collars, and Brown Pants cover three major world powers, but the world is this games oyster, why stop at three? Thats probly asking alot, I know, so I wouldnt be surprised if something like that never happened. But it would be definetly cool.
All in all the game is fairly smooth, very very few bugs, and the multiplayer is easy enough to get into. Worth the 15 bucks.

Remember me was an overall good game that just by a small margin missed being a great game. The main draw for me was the story which I have to say makes the game worth playing just on its own merits. The story mainly held this game up for me keeping my interest until the end. The game play for what I can describe is a mix between Tomb Raider type wall crawling with combat that allows you to make and mix your own combos which I found to be both interesting and useless at the same time. Although you unlock up to a 10-hit combo you will find yourself mostly using the 3 and 6 hit combos as you're never given enough time to chain them all together before someone attempts to attack you. The enemies will swarm around you and attack nearly at random and the prompts above their head leave little time to react and with the lack of a counter system do you find yourself bouncing around hitting your enemy almost in a poke and run type strategy.
Some of the attacks will be utilizing have different effects depending on what you put into your combo for example some of the attacks in your combo might heal you while another cools down your powers. Speaking of powers that's one of the most interesting things about the combat that for me the ability to use certain powers made the combat varied enough that I enjoyed the combat overall. For example one of my favorite powers was the ability to hack a robot changing it from an enemy to an ally which would then attack the others and then shortly after detonate killing two birds and one stone. My only problem with the powers was the cool-down times were quite long of them being up to 180 seconds, of course with some of your combo chains you could shorten the time by utilizing the ones that helped shorten your cool-down time but sometimes when the only way to defeat an enemy was by utilizing a specific power running around waiting for your power to cool down made it feel like you weren't taking on your enemy as much as waiting for the right opportunity to attack.
One of the coolest features of this game where the memory remixes you were able to basically hack someone's mind and change what they were called about a specific event. This made a interesting break from the rest of the game as it turned those scenarios into puzzles. Although not very challenging it would take you a few tries to get the right combination to complete the scenario. There are quite a few Collectibles within this game which actually serve a purpose when you collect them depending on what you picked up they can add more health or more experience. They're also collectibles which give you a better understanding of the world these can be read but it's not required to understand the story. I found myself looking around trying to find most of the collectibles but I ended up only finding around half. Overall a great game only held back by platforming that didn't really feel as good as something like Tomb Raider and combat that overall was fun but didn't feel fully fleshed out. The game is also very linear and to some that's a turn off, I didn't mind it though.  If you find this game on sale and it looks interesting I do highly recommend it at a discounted price it will take you around 10 hours to beat so if you're looking for a short game with an interesting story and some decent combat this one's for you.

-Actual Review-
When it comes to games, I'm a sucker for Cute Anime Girls, Extensive Customization, and Movement.
Upon seeing this game, I had pretty much instantly decided I was going to buy it.
I looked at the screenshots, and read a few reviews, and from what little I got from it all, I decidede it was a game I was going to buy, on sale.
Near Murican thanksgiving, I notice the numbers on the price have reversed order, and the $32 dollar game, is now $23, so I take my chance, and grab it then and there.
After playing it....I honestly would be fine saying its worth 32 bucks. at least for ME.
I didn't really think there would be much to it... some clothing customization, some weapons, boring as♥♥♥♥♥♥combat, and some fanservice...I thought I was buying a $10 game for double the price, but really theres a fair bit of detail in this game that I wasn't expecting.
At first, it was small things, like the fact there's an ongoing 'twitter' story, where lurkers of the internet have conversations about the events, you as the main character, are participating in...it expands the story a bit in a way, that makes sense, even if the story isnt anything really worthwhile, its a nice touch.
Then I noticed the Visual Editor settings, for the world itself. the ability to change more than just the contrast, but the tint of every shadow, the fog, the color of the sky, how much bloom and blur there is. you can change the colors and design of the world anytime. which, for most, is worthless crap. but for folks like me, its nice to know that at any time, I can change the world to become an eternal sunset, or even convert everything into pure black and white sillohuettes.
Then, began the Combat... Although its certainly not terrible, its also not all that fantastic either.
Attacks are focused on High, Medium, and Low. you damage the opponent's clothing before you rip it off of them...remove everything they have on, before your opponent, does the same to you.
Now, I like this system, because its the same for the player....your three main articles of clothing become your health bars. where reaching Zero is dangerous, but doesnt kill you.
However, where this falls apart, is in the weapons.
The game, does not take itself seriously, and it expects players to do the same. where this is an issue, is that, SOME weapons, attempt to be funny. forcing your combo to finish in a hilarious forward dive attack that leaves you on the ground for a few seconds. or converts your moves into ridiculous dance poses.
This is fun, yes, but its also VERY frustrating when your BEST weapon, has some combo attack that leaves you wide open for the enemy to steal your pants. (Or skirt, I'm not gonna judge)
However, this is remedied upon playing New-Game Plus, or completing certain storylines, where you eventually get weapons that have you fighting more seriously.
Aside from combat, there's very little in the game to expand upon...the story, although decent, is little more than an attempt to make a 'logical' reason for why you need to rip off your opponents clothes, while mixing in some 'drama' so that the dating sim part of the game works as well.
The story does its job, and rather well at that....but to judge it as a story on its own, without the gameplay. its worthless.
I also reccomend finding your own music, as the soundtrack of the game is rather plain, and the combat music is especially bad. (Though when compared directly to the above average combat itself, I guess they sorta go together)
In the end, I can really only say this, to truly summarize my entire point about this game,
Take the most droll, uninteresting, and yawn-inducing Slice of Life anime you can think of, and have it meet in the middle, with Kill La Kill.

I hate to say that I wouldn't recommend Syberia, because there are aspects of it that I really loved, and the amount of good reviews it has gotten has made it one of the few games I considered buying at full price (although luckily I snagged it and Syberia II on sale) but overall Syberia's gameplay takes most of the enjoyment from the game, takes it outside, and beats it relentlessly with a baseball bat.
I have about 9 hours listed for playing Syberia, but I'd say only ~4 hours of that was actual gameplay, and the rest was simply clicking furiously at the edges of endless screens trying to make Kate Walker run through pointless scenery until I could get to the actual objective. I've played plenty of adventure games with click-based movement before, but what makes Syberia comparable in enjoyment to a lobotomy is that for at least the first half of the game 95% of the rooms and screens you run across have no objects, objectives, or point whatsoever except to look pretty, and you're left having to run across giant maps with maybe 3 useful rooms in them altogether, all of which are spread out.
Oh and here's the solution to every other puzzle: You need a key. Chances are it's nearby. If you don't need a key then prepare for some moderate-yet-annoying pixelhunting, and running through every room 3 times because you got everything right but now there's an extra little something you need to do that seems to have no point other than to add another 30+ minutes of "gameplay" to Syberia.
I will say the story is interesting enough. It could've been more in-depth but that would've cut into Kate's marathon time I'm sure. I liked listening to Kate's phonecalls as a side-story. The art -as pointless as it was at times - was very well done and pretty especially considering when the game originially came out. And I really did love all the characters within the game, as the majority seem very well thought out.
Syberia is pretty, interesting, and it sure does seem like a classic adventure. But the long dragging gameplay will eventually have even the most casual point-and-click gamer feeling more like they're just doing a chore.

Bought this game randomly just for the fun of it. Yeah, I do that sometimes, it's not even my genre. But wow, I got myself a piece of gold here. I am not much into the Point'n'Click genre as said, but it is good to know that there are games like this which convince me to actually poke my head below the surface (poor metaphors, yay. no seriously wtf did I just write there).
Well, technically and graphically, this game is... well. Just keep it's age in mind, it's from 2002 yo. But considering that, these backgrounds are just WOW. Probably some of the prettiest and most detailed I know of (operative word is 'I'). Cought myself acting up to take a neat screenshot here and there.
The gameplay is quite slow paced, like in most of the genre's games (I guess; me lacking experience here) - But sometimes I could strangle Kate for her unbearable stair-walking behavior (JUST CLIMB 'EM DOWN ALREADY ahh, wrong side of the train again FML), just saying. The puzzles are mostly comprehensible and challenging enough so that even a beginner like me can solve them just by thinking. No actual brain- or logic breakers here (I still had to take a walkthrough four or five times, but mainly thanks to my own stupidity). The items are mostly located at logical places, the solution may be even located just next to the keyhole where it should be by logic. I like this!
The story is really intense for what I have felt. I actually felt the necessity to accomplish Kate's mission in the first place and solve the problems not for the problems' sake, but to finally get to that damn Hans. Just like Kate, over the time I really got involved into the story behind the automatons and their creators (I inhaled EVERY document - including Anna's wole diary). I can't remember being confused about details that I didn't catch - simply because I did NOT miss out on anything. This is a rare event in more gameplay-driven games like shooters - maybe I should play more games of this kind; or play games in my native language more often... on the other hand... ugh, still prefer the original voices. German localization sucks in most cases. anyway B2T
Long story short: I had tons of fun playing it and figuring out the ways through the story. It became one of these games I enjoyed putting 14 hours of my precious free time into without regrets. The end came a bit sudden for my taste, but the story does not end there; and some day I WILL get myself the sequel(s), definitely.
I can just highly recommend this game to whoever is looking for an involving, story driven experience with an interesting setting - and maybe, like me, having never touched Point'n'Click before.
And if you are really, REALLY not interested into that genre AT ALL... Man, still give this one a try.
I did, too.
PS: Maybe it is just me, but I think I had some sound issues on Windows10, which (I am sure of) weren't there on Windows7. Some of the sceneries had almost no sound at all. But if that's in the game: a little minus for sound design ;D

I played FIFA since 2015 until now. Then, this year I try to in this game. A bit uncomfortable with the pitch at first. But now, start to love it. Both FIFA and PES is the best soccer game.

I really cannot say enough positive things about this game. After editing the proper kits and teams into the game, it hands down defeats FIFA in gameplay (and I would even say graphically as well, though setting up the graphics can be a hassle as I had to use Nvidia Inspector). To me PES is a futbol simulator, whereas FIFA is an arcade game that has better online features. However, I mainly play offline modes, which makes me prefer PES.
It takes a while to get used to the controls coming from FIFA, but once you do, it really is a satisfying game. I feel that the control you have over your player and what you do is so much greater, especially when you include the ability to turn on advanced shooting which lets you pick what area of the net you want to shoot at and how hard (which is actually fairly difficult to do with most players).
Not to go on for too long, PES does have some problems, but if it launched with full licensing and an online Pro Clubs mode like in FIFA, I would not buy another FIFA game. Period. However, EA makes a living in the sports game world by buying out the licensing to certain things (such as the NFL, NHL, and many of the futbol leagues most know of) because they know they cannot compete mechanics wise, which makes this review necessary.
If you enjoy the AI teleporting to you, goalies not diving for the ball, and physics defying gameplay, I would recommend FIFA. If you enjoy a game that requires you to have put time into it and have a basic knowledge of how to play futbol, I would recommend PES.

The first entry in the never ending Assassin's Creed franchise. This game is what started it all for Ubisoft, love 'em or hate 'em. This game features a conflict between Templars and Assassins in a historical setting. If you love history then this is a great game for you. The atmosphere in the game is very good, it makes you feel like you're alone in this dark and deadly journey for redemption. The three main cities you explore are nice and detailed. The stealth aspect isn't perfect, but it is interesting and fun to play with. The combat is also interesting, but once you get the hang of it, it becomes easy. The story, if you pay attention, is great and mysterious. There's also a parcour system that allows you to climb buildings all sneaky like.
However, this game has many flaws. Towards mid-game point, the game becomes very repetitive, having you doing the same missions over and over again. What sucks is that to progress in the game, you must do these boring missions to get the next piece in the story. At points you might not care for the good story this game has because of tedious tasks.
I love history and conspiracies, so this game was right up the alley for me. The combat and stealth was intersting at first but the game does get repetitive. I really like this game and it's one of the better ones in the franchise in my opinion. It's a risk, but you might enjoy this game if you're more into story than gameplay.

It's good, really, but...
It's fun to start off with, but it gets unbelievably repetitive way before the end. The mission types repeat and repeat and repeat, and one (eavesdropping) doesn't even involve gameplay. Climbing viewpoints gets tedious most quickly, and there are (by my count) 91 of them in the game. Some aren't that high, but some are these ridiculous towers it takes probably well over a minute to climb, sync and dive from.
The free running feels good, except when you randomly stop climbing or you randomly fail to jump to or grab something or it just doesn't respond properly in the heat of the moment.
The combat is alright, but it doesn't really make sense that when you're surrounded by enemies, only one attacks you at any given time.
The graphics are still decent, but even with the highest settings there's heavy LOD-popping going on as you roam around, especially in 'the kingdom', the area in between the key cities. And the shadow resolution drops, jarringly, for anything further than a few metres from you. People even popped into existence before my eyes once or twice. You do get to ride a horse through the kingdom though, which is strangely satisfying.
The story is alright but the most interesting part is the 'present day' stuff, which really doesn't tell a proper story, more like the first couple of chapters.
Oh and you know what's the most annoying? The drunks, beggars and deranged who annoy the absolute shitzu out of you any time you're on street level.
So... I strongly suggest watching the cutscenes on YouTube and skipping right to the second game, unless you're the neurotic type who feels compelled to play through all of them (like me). But if that's the case, play in short bursts and definitely don't waste your time trying to collect the hundreds of flags scattered through the game. There's no fun to be had doing that, and not even any pointless achievements.
Also, the game has no subtitles whatsoever.
Let the good times roll...

Remember Me is a game that takes place in a 2080's, futuristic Paris. It is a story-driven game made by DONTNOD Entertainment (Life is Strange). It has beautiful graphics and a great storyline keeping you on the edge of your seat wanting to play more and more. It is split up into 8 episodes that take place in different areas around Paris and normally introduce new enemies changing the rules of the game.

-Constant Changing of Mechanics
-No Bugs/Glitches

-Repetitive Combat

Gameplay:
The gameplay in this game consists of making your own combos and using them to your advantage. Before or during a fight you can go into the combo lab and change your combos to appeal to the enemies your fighting. Combos are used with X and Y (Example: X, Y, Y, X, Y) and there are 4 different combo slots and combo moves to implement. You can outfit your combos with a Damage Multiplier, Health Regenerator, Cooldown Regenerator, or Loop.
Aside from the combat there is Parkour. The parkour in this game is very straightforward, you cannot pick your path. The game is set on one path the entire time that you have to follow, no branching out on another for a different outcome in the end. While doing parkour there is an orange arrow that follows you around and tells you where to go, making the game annoying because it's always telling you where to go.
7.5/10 I would recommend this game to you and all of your friends.
