I just completed this game and find myself perplexed by it. The visual style of it was pretty darn impressive, both artistically and graphically, to an extent. Most of the voice acting was good enough, and I had very few glitches and only one crash I can recall. Why, then, am I not recommending the game? Well, because those are the only good things I can really say about the game from my experience, except perhaps that it was a good idea that did not turn out well.
Is this an awful game? No. However, the game fails almost entirely on its gameplay, explaining the world you're in, and the plotline itself. The gameplay largely consists of much crappier versions of activities other games have already done. Did you think the modern Tomb Raider or Uncharted games did a decent enough job of climbing sections? Well, Remember Me does a far crappier version of these. Perhaps you thought the Batman Arkham games had some enjoyable third person brawling combat? Get ready for a very poor man's version of that system. Not only that, but the game is set in a sci-fi location where memories and tech are everything...in presentation, at least. In actuality, 90% of your controntations in the game are punching and kicking the crap out of stuff.
In regard to the game explaining the world you're in, they just didn't even try to have a coherent set of rules for this future setting. You can alter memories, but it's only important maybe 5 times in the entire game. There are "execution" moves you can pull off that don't kill enemies but do a blast to their head. The game never tells you exactly what this does. It's implied that it messes with their memories. There is more involving stealing memories as well as having a hologram arm thing that shoots projectile energy...but it doesn't seem to have a port to fire the energy or anything like that. The technology is never explained and feels terribly out of place. It -looks- nice, but this game's only positives tend to be graphical. The plot of the game largely relies on various pieces of technology and things these pieces of technology do, when you're still trying to grasp what this tech does, and there are mutant things you fight which the game does a terrible job of explaining what they are as well. This is one of the most poorly constructed games as far as explaining how stuff works in that universe, that I've ever seen.
Remixing memories is decent enough, but by the last two times I had to do it, I was well past the point where I wanted the game to be over. The game has 8 chapters, the last of which is super short, but by the time I was finishing chapter 5, I was very ready for the game to be over. If not for the game's visual presentation, the fact I paid for it, and that I really like science fiction settings, I do not believe I ever would've mustered the willpower to complete this game. I doubt I will ever play it again, as trying another game or replaying any of dozens of better games was a far better use of my time than this.
Since the visual look of the game is its strongest point, I'd actually recommend that if you want to enjoy this game, that you just watch a few Youtube videos to see the city and everything. It looks great. That's about all there is to really like about the game, though. In a few years when graphics are far better in so many other titles, this game will have nothing it does better than other games, so I cannot recommend it.

Well, it was on sale for 17 cents. I expected absolutely nothing and got a bit more than that. All in all, it's a pretty good game... It's strikingly evocative of a sort of slightly-crappy but still "Cult classic" PS1 game, from the visuals to the early-2000s-esque techno music in the background- Which might turn some off, but honestly, it's exactly the sort of game I feel I would have rented at the video store growing up.
The gameplay's fairly simple and straightforward: Run around at high speed, shoot at enemies, rinse and repeat. The first weapon you get shoots rather slow-moving lasers- Brings back memories of the golden days of fast movement speed tied with non-hitscan weaponry, at least for me. As you progress through the levels, you pick up more abilities for your suit, as well as upgrade the abilities you already have, eventually ending up basically flying around the map at the speed of sound spamming homing missiles that kill everything on the screen pretty much automatically. The game has one of those really early terrain deformation systems, where you can raise or lower points on the map to your heart's content (After acquiring the weapons that let you do so, of course), which is cool I guess? It kept me engaged for the two and a half hours the main story lasted.
Onto the story: To put it mildly, there isn't one. Really, there's three characters: You, a mute anime-ish-looking boy/girl in a suit of what can only be described as power armor; a two-dimensional portrait of a lady that gives you instructions at the start of each level and congratulates you at the end of such; and the commander, who you never even see and who only shows up through text at the beginning and end of the main story. The story itself is that there are a bunch of bug-things and you have to shoot them. It's really not that deep. It also happens to stop halfway through and suggest that you should wait until some sort of update.
The graphics are like a Nintendo 64 game, and not a good one. Enough said.
All in all, it's not what I'd call a great game, but if it's on sale, go ahead and pick it up. Put it this way: It's cheaper and much more fun than going to Wal-mart and getting a gumball from one of the machines.

The first game in the Assassin's Creed series is the game you should either start the series with, or go into with lower expectations. That's not to say this game is bad, it's just one that has sequals which far exceed the original.
Advertising itself as a "next-gen" (beginning of Xbox 360/PS3 era) game, in retrospect this game definitely looks (emphasis on the "looks") that way. Set in the 12th century during the Third Crusade, AC1 tells the tale of an underground battle between two opposing factions that has gone on since the begginnings of our species, and you play as Altair, a member of the Assassin Order. The plot is not the most exciting part of the game, but the ideas about human nature were enough to keep me interested into it to a certain extent. The characters are forgetable, besides our protagonist. Altair is a rather brash Assassin who fails a mission in the opening act of the game, and this game details his journey to get back to his previous rank within the Assassin Order. Besides the out of place American accent (ugh), Altair is a rather badass and interesting protagonist who keeps the plot afloat.
On the other hand, the world which the game is sent in is rich and engrossing. The graphical quality greatly reflects the world of the Crusade, and cities are full of NPC's which go about on their day. The sheer size of the maps will surely impress if this is your first AC game. Immersion is also something this game nails on the head, despite its numerous flaws. The soundtrack may not be entirely memorable, but it nonetheless fits the game extremly well. Voice work (minus Altair) is definitely of a high quality and fits in as well. However, do not look to this game as a history lesson that is 1:1 with reality. This game does take history and makes it fit into a video game, and isn't entirely accurate (which the game acknowledges).
This goes into a part of the game that is really up to opinion when it comes to the story: You're actually reliving the memories Altair, who is the ancestor of our true protagonist Desmond. Here you meet Lucy and Videc, one of which is a rather bland assistant character, while the other is an evil scientist. While these characters came across as rather boring to me, Desmond's character really makes them seem like works out of Shakespear. Desmond is an EXTREMLY bland character, and one that I honestly didn't care about. The game pulls your out of the Animus (the device used to relive memories) after every chapter, and these segmants are real pacebrakers, despite some interesting conversations between Desmond and Videc here and there.
Another issue I have withe the games story is how abrupt the ending is, and a plotpoint that comes up near the end of the game without explanation and just feels like it's there to break immersion and be picked up later on. While I wont go into details, the game definitely makes it feel as if it NEEDS to have a sequal, whether you as the player likes it or not.
While it may seem as if I hate this game, I must say I actually did have an enjoyable experience with the gameplay. Sure, the game is repititive with the same objective structure being true for 85% or so of the game: Complete 3 missions, and assassinite your target. While this may definitely be a problem for some, the gameplay does work quite well to break this problem apart.
A staple of Assassins Creed is its parkour and stealth mechanics, and both are present and enjoyable to do here. Soaring across the games three cities is enjoyable, and stealth can be very rewarding in the game as it is quite difficult to pull off compared to the sequals. Combat is also very rich, and has many sides to it (even though it becomes pathetically easy with counters). You can dodge, block, grab, and slash at your opponents with various tools at your disposal: a sword, a shortsword, throwing knives, and the iconic hidden blade (and also your fists, of course).
The objectives your are required to complete before assassinations are quite repepitive however, and may be something you may not enjoy. I personally found informer challaneges to be very tricky, while pickpockets and interrogations were far too easy. And eavesdropping is... well... sitting on a bench, and that's that. Assassinations are, however, very enjoyable and can be done in a variety of manners, and are followed by extremly intense escpae sequences that will keep you on your toes.
While there are some optional activities (saving civilians, collect-a-thons, and scaling every viewpoint), the game doesn't offer too much else. and is purely an action adventure game rather than an RPG (like its sequals). This is why Assassin's Creed is honestly a game that doesn't have too much replay value, even though the adventure is about 15 hours and is overall enjoyable, if not repitive for 85% of the journey and telling of a story that isn't too memorbale, despite the immersive world presented. $20 may be a bit too much for how shallow AC1 is (and considering you can buy the more polished sequals for the same price), and if you're curious I would advice that you wait for this to go on sale and to have an open mind. However, the game should keep you entertained enough to be interested in AC2, which is definitely a GOOD thing.
Overall, AC1 is a decent first game into the AC franchise, and one you should approach with some caution, and avoid if you've played the other AC games (unless you're extremly curious). I would give this game an overall 7/10, however if I had to take replayability into account it's definitely a 6/10.

The start of the now long-running Assassin's Creed franchise, you are placed in the shoes of Altaiir, an assassin during the Crusades. This game possesses a very historically-centric plot and the parkour gameplay foundation that the franchise, and many others, now use.
First off, the gameplay has aged somewhat badly, particularly if you've played any other parkour movement games released since. The movement in this game is noticeably slower than its sequels, especially when climbing up the sides of towers and buildings. The combat, however, is both better and worse than that in the sequels. It is much simpler, not allowing nearly as many options in combat and can be very slow when fighting multiple opponents. On the plus side, it is more difficult than the newer Assassin's Creed games, actually providing somewhat of a challenge in combat.
Now, the real highlight of this game is the plot. While it may be told in a very weak way, with you doing the same things over and over in different locations and being rewarded with a monologue, it is a very thematically/morally strong plot. It addresses the nature of good and bad on a very deep level and if you enjoy philosophy or analyzing morality, you will love it. It's truly a shame that they dropped this plot strength in the later iterations of the game.
Overall, I'd recommend the game, as I feel it is still great fun, and the message is simply unforgettable.

tl;dr: Akiba's Trip is certainly a good game, but not exactly a great game.
Let's be honest, if you're seriously considdering buying this game, you're not the type to be put off by the fanservice or esoteric otaku culture, so let's ignore that and just look at the game it self.
Let's take a look at a few things this game does well:
+ Solid anime-esque 3d art
+ large and detailed world based on real life akihabara
+ a sense of humor as silly as it is refferential and esoteric
+ lots of clothes and riduculous makeshift weapons to play around with
+ multiple endings and some cool features to mix things up in a NG+
That said... there are a few things this game doesn't do so great with:
- Controls are horrendous! They take a few hours to get used to and even then they're not that great...
- Combat is clunky, mostly because of the controls, and even then, a repetitive, boring slog.
- Fairly short compaign if you don't do any sidequests...
- English voices are lackluster. Not terrible, but not great either.
If you think you're going to enjoy this game based soley on it's art and concept, then you probably will. Akiba's Trip is a good game that could've been a great game if the controls weren't total garbage and the combat wasn't thoroughly boring, but if you're fine with pushing through bland, and occasionally annoying gameplay, there's a lot of fun to be had with the story and characters. So yes, I do reccomend it, but not without reservations regarding gameplay.

Edit: XSeed support has been more than helpful in solving my issue! For anyone having an issue with the game where the game loads and plays fine when all of a sudden your fps drops severely for about 5-10 seconds before resuming again, this was the fix provided to me:
- Go into the game files for Akiba Strip (Generally at C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\steamapps\common\Akiba's Trip Undead & Undressed)
- Go into the folder lang_jp
- Rename the folder movie into something else (For example, movie123)
- Go back into previous folder and find folder lang_us
- Rename the folder movie into something else as well
That should fix the issue. I was told this issue persisted as it has something to do with the in-game movies not loading properly. Doing the above disables the movie (As the game can't find the movie folder to play the videos from). This is likely a codec issue as i was told.
A genuine thank you to Ken from XSeed support for helping me out with my issue!

Akiba's Trip (I swear the design at the title screen makes me think it's really Akiba Strip. Check it out if you don't believe me.) is certainly not something like everything else. That alone is the single most important reason why you would want to buy this game.
This is no Saint's Row or GTA but it can feel like one when you're doing the side quests.
Crossdressing to get guys to stop hitting on a girl? Only to kick the♥♥♥♥♥♥out of them for hitting on you? Hell YES!
Hunting down cursed urban hardware? Whuuuuut?
Stopping a labor law protest coming from 48 girls...only to beat all of them to death in a survival scenario?! (Forget stripping them! I'm UNDER ATTACK BY 48 GIRLS!)
Just...WOW....JUST...FREAKING...WOW JAPAN!
You start off as a guy that fell for a shady job and got turned into some kind of demi-vampire but you get saved by a random girl. (you learn more about her later and why.) After you get busted out you investigate this town which is actually a rl city from 80s Japan. Unfortunately other people are being turned into these demi-vampires, known as synthisters, and you have to best them in combat by ripping their clothes off so that the sunlight takes care of the rest. Simple....yet not so...
The game itself is a Aerial Camera 3D brawler. You control your camera with right stick and use 3 buttons for attacking the sections of your victim's bodies. Y for head, B for mid section, and A for low section. After you bust up the durability of your opponent's clothing enough you then hold one of the corresponding buttons for an attempt to rip off the clothing. So the combat is very simple and easy to pick up on. You can also use some special moves too with the different weapons available. To negotiate your targets the one your character will attack will have a ring around them when you align yourself before you start button mashing. Careful though, you're partially like the synthisters too and your opponents will be trying to strip you too. If you lose your headpiece/top/bottom altogether, you die. There's a lot more to the combat than just these. This is just the bread and butter stuff. There are counters and blocking and unblockable attacks.
This game has some kind of date sim/RPG story element into it in which it has several endings, all dependent on which of the girls you meet feels about you depending on the dialog choices you choose.
And mostly...that's pretty much it. The game is short but it does have a few problems.
First and foremost. The maps are very small.
To add to the very small maps. If you're forced into combat in these small streets or alleyways you can be shoved near the exit points as you're fighting. You won't automatically exit the map while in combat but the camera fixes and zooms out and does that almost instantly which isn't just annoying but also screws up your concentration and view. On my first dry run, it was frustrating but I guess it's something you can train yourself to get used to. You're doing to HATE places like Junk Street.
Secondly is how missions are handled. The main missions are instanced on their own map even though you travel to the map it's at. They start AUTOMATICALLY when you enter that map. It does save you the trouble of looking for an npc but that's where the problems with the side quests come in.
The side quests are marked by Red ! Points however the game has no local radar or any icons to view quest NPCs. In order to find quest npc objectives you have to make sure you have the Npc titles turned on. (Turn them on by pressing Y when not in combat and you'll see the npcs classes i.e. Otaku, Maid, Gothic Lolita, schoolgirl, etc.) Regular npcs are yellow titled and side quest/objective npcs are Red titled however with no radar some of them are hard to find and the side quests have expiration timers. You do get a good bit of time, don't get me wrong, but when players want to start something they shouldn't have to strain their eyes fishing for out of place NPCs in a sea of yellow words. On the plus side, because the maps are very small, this isn't as bad as it sounds.
All and all I think it's the closest Japan's coming to making a good and decent open world game but it still feels like it has it's constrictions but it's still nice. Grab it on sale...just don't tell your friends or your parents. :)

Full Review:
While Conflict is an awesome series that I highly recommend people to play, even though it is dated, I do not recommend playing this PC Ported version. It's rife with glitches and bugs which are glaringly apparent from the start.
From the first training mission I found my character unable to drop down off of a ledge. Instead, he continued to bug out and "float" accross the map as I moved him in different directions. In doing so I was able to go behind the railing where the staff sergeant stood and poke around "behind the scenes" a bit.
However, this didn't stop me from pushing forward into the game. "So," I said to myself, "I'll just say forget the training missions and try to play the actual campaign." This also, did not end well. I decided to play it on hard mode as I always enjoy a good challenge. I died a lot, but I'm not one to complain, just learn from it and learn the game mechanics (or in this case, remember, as it's been many years since I last played).
As I continued further into the map I got myself cornered inside of a building with 1 way in, 1 way out. The enemies kept coming, but I kept putting them down, shooting them before they had the chance to shoot me. Finally I take a peek around the corner to see if there's more. Yup, there's roughly 3 more. So I fall back into the room and let them continue towards me. Kill the first two... Waiting for that third one. I see him come around the corner, and BAM BAM BAM! Wait... I missed? How is he 5 feet in the air!?!? And I die.
I can deal with the occasional glitch/bug here and there. But from the 55 minutes I played, I ran into approximately 5 or more, most being identical glitches that were reaccuring. I figured that maybe I was the only one having issues, but I've read quite a few reviews stating as such.
No matter how high your nostalgia level is, please, for your own safety, and so you don't get any heartbreak, do not purchase this until it's been probably ported for the PC.

Call of Duty 4 Modern Warfare is one of the most influential games of the modern era. It almost single handedly paved the way towards modern military shooters becoming a trend. Gone were the days of countless World War 2, Vietnam and space shooters. Now was the relatively untapped potential of modern day shooters.
Prior to Modern Warfare, modern military shooters were usually akin to sims. Games like Rainbow Six or Full Spectrum Warrior are good examples. Very tactically complex games with little run and gun action. Modern Warfare replaces run and gun with stop and pop. You use cover to your advantage and duck out with iron sights. Call of Duty 4 is the game I see as popularizing iron sights and probably utilized them the best compared to other games at the time. Moving and firing from the hip is wildly inaccurate but holding your sights down would increase your accuracy dramatically but slow your movement and narrow your field of view. It's an extremely immersive mechanic and one that was designed to compensate for the limited accuracy of analog sticks.
That's not all that Modern Warfare gave us either. Modern Warfare also paved the way for progression based multiplayer. Contrary to arena shooters, Modern Warfare instead focuses on letting you customize your arsenal with sights, scopes, underbarrel grenade launchers and even color schemes. And you unlock all of this gradually the more you play. It feels akin to an RPG where the more you play, the cooler your guns become and the more efficient you are at taking other players down. This is still the dominant system in first person shooters and even more popular franchises like Halo and Doom started to use it.
And lastly the singleplayer in Modern Warfare is fairly good. It is a mostly scripted and linear shooter with plenty of good set pieces and moments. Along with prior staples of the series like having multiple protagonists and viewpoints across the story.
One other thing to note is how much of a PC game Modern Warfare 1 was compared to it's sequels. It has a console, a full SDK and map editor, dedicated servers and so much more. It allowed for things like bots to be added. And even close to 10 years after release you can still find enough people who want to play this game to fill a server. As derivative as later titles in this series got, you have to admire a charismatic and influential game like Modern Warfare. Very few first person shooters have such a lasting legacy that stands the test of time.

Quick Summary: Third Person Action game in a semi-dystopian world with intriguing story, but some buggy gameplay. The combat is mostly hand to hand with a simplified “combo” system where you alternate between punches and kicks. Overall it’s a fun game and makes you think about the benefits and drawbacks of memory manipulation.
You play Nilin, a “memory hunter” in a world where technology now allows the storage and deletion of human memories. Unlike the “Total Recall” movies, the technology can’t really make up new memories and implant them into people. Instead, it’s possible to selectively delete memories and/or remove them from people and give them to someone else. As a memory hunter, Nilin is able to do a whole lot of unusual things such as steal passwords from a person’s mind, “remix” memories, and use cyber power attacks in combat.
The game is mostly linear with a lot of free climbing like Assassin’s Creed or Tomb Raider games, and the combat is similar to the brawling in the Batman Arkham games or Sleeping Dogs. However unlike Batman, Nilin doesn’t “counter” attacks, only dodge. Also, note that unlike the Arkham games the reaction time is shorter (You pretty much have to dodge as soon as you see an attack warning). The combo system I mentioned earlier is based around unlocking punches and kicks as you “level up.”  These attacks can be chained into 3, 5, 6, or 8 hit combos which do increasing damage as they get longer. This is why the short reaction time to enemy attacks is so annoying (they keep interrupting combos).  Other special powers you can unlock throughout the story are Fury (short term damage boost), DOS (area effect stun), Logic Bomb (area affect damage) along with a couple others.
Pros:
+A unique and complex world with a thought provoking story line.
+The boss battles are interesting because of cyber manipulation of virtual worlds based around memories.
+The “memory remix” sections of the game let you view and make subtle changes to a person’s memory, with the overall effect of making them remember things that never happened. It’s like the butterfly effect in action, tiny changes can change the outcome in drastic ways.
Cons:
-The game has some noticeable bugs, like the sound suddenly cutting out, or not being able to aim your spammer “gun” at various points in the game.
-The combat system is really annoying when you’re surrounded by enemies and can’t get a combo going because everyone keeps attacking. In the Batman games, the enemies usually attack one at a time (or you can use a multi-takedown). In Remember Me, you have to dodge and start your combo over.
You probably have Remember Me from the Humble Bundle last year so don’t be afraid to give it a shot.

Syberia is a point-and-click adventure game in which you play as Kate Walker, attempting to track down the owner of a toy factory in order to facilitate a sale. Through the game you move through a series of locations along a railway line, each of which has a series of puzzles which need to be solved in order to allow your trip to continue.
As noted in many other reviews, Kate moves rather slow, but can run if you double-click. However, when moving up/down stairs, or any other obstacles, she does move at a slow pace. As there is an unfortunate amount of backtracking involved in the course of the game and they frequently have these sorts of stairs, it can lead to a stuttered, somewhat lethargic pace.
The story feels meandering until you reach close to the end of the game, when it starts to pick up. As this game takes place in a fictional history, some items (such as how a railway would supposedly work) don't really make /sense/. If you're the sort of person where these sorts of things bother you, you might want to pass on this game. Ultimately, the question which needs to be asked is whether point-and-click adventure is something which appeals to you - while it can take some time to get truly gripping, the story is worth experiencing, provided you like that sort of gameplay.

The game is set in a futuristic Neo-Paris. People now have a brain implant called the Sensen created by the mega-corporation Memorize. Sensen allows people to share their happy memories or remove their unhappy ones. Thanks to this Memorize has an enormous control over the population and has established a surveillance state.
You play as Nilin, a memory hunter whose memory has been wiped by Memorize. You basically start off having an amnesia.
You set off to take down Memorize and recover your lost memories. You're also on a journey of self discovery as you question your motives and actions along the way.
Remember Me plays similarly to all your favourate action-adventure platformers such as Castlevania: LoS or Enslaved.
You do a bit of fighting, puzzle solving and ofc jumping and climbing.
You hit enemies using the X and Y buttons. As usually you can create combos with them by pressing Y-Y-Y-X-X-X-Y etc.
You can ofc shoot flying enemies and dodge attacks by moving the left stick and pressing A.
Classic action-adventure gameplay but a bit simplistic here. You won't unlock any crazy combos. Enemies are very easy to fight and even if you do manage to die you start again basically at the same place.
It took me about 8h to finish the game on hardest difficulty.
Remember Me is one of the easiest action-adventure platformers i've played but its charm is in the magnificent world and interesting story. Neo-Paris is very well crafted and it is a joy to climb its futuristic buildings.
I didn't experience any technical issues with the game. It ran like a charm!
It seems to be very well optimised and I didn't run into any bugs or glitches nor did I have any crashes.
If you're looking for an eye candy tho then you'll be dissapointed. The graphics aren't exactly bad but they were mediocre even back in 2013. The voice acting, however, is supreme.
Overall Remember Me is a good game. Is it worth the 27.99€ is up to You to decide.

Lots of good action, at a certain point combat becomes repetitive, but working to get the the next area is fun and yet challenging. I also  have to say kudos on the sound direction for this game, seriously! Strap on a pair of good headphones and you will see exactly what I mean. The sound really transports you!
Blade Runner also comes to mind with this game for its ambiance. I can remember a long time ago playing Blade Runner on PC and Remember Me has the future setting with great lighting, nice shading and a great overall feel of being in the future. I didn't run across any bugs, game runs smooth and for a title that is 3 years in my opinion it looks AWESOME!
Overall if you are looking to play a game rich in story with a fantastic setting, pick up Remember Me. It is a unique title with a unique combat structure, interesting puzzles and it will make you want to come back for more every time you exit out of the game!
10/10 for me! Would love to see an open world sequel to this!

It starts really good with high presentation values, an interesting story foundation, and some decent gameplay...and it steadily goes downhill.
Voice acting is hit and miss (fortunately the main characters are pretty good). Real misses are the extras that can't deliver "There she is!" or "Get her!" to save their lives. It's actually pretty distracting considering the side characters are alright and the lead is excellent.
The combat is fun for awhile until it becomes boring and then becomes frusturating. Later in, they introduce an enemy that hurts you when you hit them. No caveats, no real workarounds aside from heal yourself, they just hurt you when you hit them, ranged or melee. It's almost an interesting mechanic because no designer in their right minds would ever think that was okay.
The story starts to take odd tone shifts as well, doing momentairly strange things for apparently no reason. One section when you're being chased by a helicopter shooting you with a gatling gun, the sound dampens as you run and the music swells with sorrow for no apparent reason. And then it comes back, with more taunts and more shooting. It's just weird, and hints that development might have gotten a bit chaotic later in the story.
It's funny. I read a lot of the complaints about the game. The camera, the monotonous combat, the bland story. None of it bothered me at first. I was having a lot of fun. And then it was like some switch clicked and all of those little things began to bother me simultaneously.
Bottom line? It's not worth it. It's a shame too. There was potential for something great, and it's clear a LOT of work was put into this one. But at the end of the day, it just can't hold it together.

Remember Me sent me into an existential crisis that took months for me to come to peace with, and which has taken me a long time to even begin to articulate properly.
Remember Me is a very deep philosophical game, wrapped in basic action game that has a vaguely Ubisoft feel to it, despite being a Capcom game.  It works well with an Xbox controller, the graphics and game design are good, and the action sequences are nothing special but customising your own combo strings is an entertaining feature, though it requires DLC to be properly enjoyed which seems a bit rude on Capcom's part.
The real place that Remember Me shines is the story which act as a vehicle for some very clever philosophy. The main concepts Remember Me explore are what makes up a person's identity; how how fallible people's memories are; and how memories, when interpreted differently, can change how a person will act in the future, and hence, can effectively change a person's identity.
The problem I encountered with Remember Me was that it forced me to take a another look at my interpretation of reality. My conscious existence is really only confirmed by my point in time interpretation of the world around me. I am not the years I have lived, nor am I the years I am yet to live, I exist only here and now. I have memories of existing previously, and I have plans of how I plan to continue living into the future, but since both of these things exist only in my mind, and my mind is fallible, what does my existence mean?
If you're looking for an action game, there are plenty of other games you could try, but if you want some philosophy carried along by a serviceable story with your action, Remember Me is a pretty good choice.

I love Running with Rifles. It's so simple, and lots of fun! You start out the lowest rank each game, and progress up soon getting a squad to follow you around, the ability to call in air strikes, or even airborne soldiers. Lots of different guns in the game, many very unique and refelective of their realistic counter part. There's numerous items such as sand bags for cover, deployable machine guns, mortars, C4, grenades, riot shields, bullet proof vests, the list goes on. Plus, if your playing with friends you can overload yourself with items. Doing so makes you less accurate, but you can then bring in stuff for you multiplayer buddies, like extra grenades, or a special gun, or deployable sandbags so you can all make a defendable position.
I love it because you play top down, it allows you a very easy view of the area, allowing you to see the benefits of taking high ground, seeing the accuracy of weapons at varying distances, and just how your allies or enemies are moving.
I REALLY suggest downloading the demo, and trying the game out. I'm not sure what's in the Demo in terms of features, or items, but I love coming back to this and just playing for 3-4 hours at a time. Another added bonus, you can tweak the visual look of the game. If you feel soldiers are too small, or hard to notice, you can adjust the opaqueness, and their borders size.

This is one of the FUNNEST games I've played in a very long time, I highly recommend purchasing this, it is easily worth $60 but the developers are friggin awesome and sell it at a very low price.
This game is like battlefield, but in top-down view.  Running with Rifles in my opinion can easily rival battlefield, if not better.  Single-player is great, the campaigns are pretty difficult.  I'm still on the first campaign and it's been 5 hours lol.  The battles are very rewarding, that feeling after an hour struggle to capture a point is very satisfying.
One thing that might be awkward at first, but maybe not for some, is the aiming system.  When moving your cursor to aim, it kind of "pulls" on your screen.  This system is pretty neat because it lets you see farther and kill enemies that are further away and different weapons have different pull ranges.  I'm still trying to adjust to this, but it's really not too bad.
The movement keys are pretty simple, WASD to move and mouse to shoot, which I like.
At first this game may seem simple, which it is, you can just hop in and start killing enemies, but this game has WAYY much more depth than that.  There is a huge selection of weaponry, you can create defenses such as building crates and putting a turret behind them, calling in airstrikes or supply drops, driving convoy trucks to move your soldiers across the battle zone, defending a captured area, and much more.
I know the "early access" tag will give you doubts, I know that feeling just look at some of my "early access" games.  But this Running with rifles is pretty much completed and can be enjoyed to the fullest experience.  I've read on their forums that this game is due to be released in about two months (assuming no delays), so they're pretty much just polishing this game from this point.  You pretty much have the full game now, but just be aware it can be subjected to change and other stuff.
I can seriously go on for a while about how great this game is, but I'm going to end it here.  If you have a slight interest in buying this game, buy it, you will not be disappointed.  Any fan of shooters will definitely appreciate this game, hell you might even be addicted to it just like I am now :D

Skullgirls is a fighting game that somewhat seems like a love letter to anime and fighting games like guilty gear and blazblue. Like those games, the mechanics focus on combos and setups. Unlike guilty gear(and more like blazblue) it's easier to dive into and the learning curve is much less steep. It's very flexable and open to many loops and links but if you repeat your attacks your opponet can break out of it with an anti-infinte counter system. The system works well and easy to understand(compared to other fighting games) but still has depth while making sure you can't use cheap tactics.
The character roster is somewhat small but each one feels uniqe. This is a case of quality over quanity. The graphics really stand out and have beautiful hand drawn animation, and very creative designs and attacks. The sound design is really good with voice acting that fits everyone well. The soundtrack is interesting with lots of jazz and blues which was very refreshing for genre.
On the downsides the final boss, like many other fighting games, is a bit cheap. While not worst i've fought by far *cough*tekken5*cough* it isn't stunned by attacks which means no pressuring it and you can easily be knocked out of your attacks which can be frustrating. Also the story mode doesn't end without the DLC characters, now I fully recommend those characters as they have the same polish and love as the others, but I don't like that idea. Even if you do finish the story, it will end on a cliff hanger(still better than what happened before the DLC characters though) but it made me want to see what happened, so the story did it's job.

This game picks up right where The New Order left off. Offering new weapons, more gore, and enjoyable gunplay, as well as an improved dual wielding system, the game is great from a shooting-gamer standpoint. The graphics are beautiful, and I enjoy that the game is able to have a balance of narrative and gameplay. The cutscenes in this game do at times seem to overpower the gameplay, and the afformentioned balance was better exhibited by TNO, but I like the fact that the game isn't always just focused on "shoot the bad guy".
I greatly enjoyed this game during my time playing through it, and would recommend it to any fan of TNO, but I do have some complaints as well.
My Complaints:
Sadly, the more serious tone that the first game seems to have takes more of a back seat at times in this game, causing the writing to become inconsistent. One of the games biggest conflicts is fixed with a dramatic twist that A.) doesn't make sense, and B.) detracts from the sombre, serious tone that the game has already established.
In addition to the afformentioned points, the writing in the story causes some characters to say lines that seem out of character. For example, in one sequence, BJ takes the time to call the Nazis "white♥♥♥♥♥fascist Nazi pigs", as opposed to simply saying "♥♥♥♥ing nazi scum" or something of the like. Obviously I'm not trying to promote nazi ideals or anything, but this line simply seems out of character for BJ.
The stealth system, while remaining similar in format to the first game, seems to be less well put together. The game still uses the "press crouch to stealth" technique, which is fine as it is a shooter, but the stealth simply seems broken at times.

The start of this game is really tedious. Movement is slow, you have a sprint bar that needs to recharge after a few seconds, a jetpack that needs to recharge after a few seconds. You have gathering equipment that can only work a few seconds before overheating and needs fuel to work, so you can run out. You have a life support system that helps you live in toxic biomes, and if you're so lucky to start in one, it'll contstantly be beeping and reminding you to also recharge it.
You have to look for minerals to make items so your spaceship can be repaired. The minerals are dotted across the planet in arbitrary distances from eachother. The planets are filled with plants and creatures, and if you're lucky they won't have cries that will constantly assault your ears as you're walk-sprinting towards another node to finish the repairs on your aircraft.
I didn't make it past the early game, there are too many obvious forced longlivity parts to it all. Your inventory is limited, and you'll slowly make it bigger. Your stamina to sprint is low, you'll probably be able to up it. Your craft is small, you'll probably be able to make it bigger. You can build, so you'll make a base and fill it with stuff, the occasional one mushroom or one creature you find on one of the planets you visit.
The progression wouldn't be as bad if it didn't feel as empty, empty in content and soul. Procedurally generated environments and creatures lack may give you a lot to see, but the stuff you see is all forgettable and boring.
If you have the guts to make it past the refund timer, you may have enough fun, but I advise against it.

The hardest battles are fought in the mind.
Though Senua was not born with the so called darkness, or curses, she was born with some specialties that divided her from the crowd. That she had the potential tendencies of what we now call, psychosis. What really turned her into a “witch” was, that her father abused her, abetted villagers to condemn her being evil, bearing darkness, curses... That was when her psychosis tendencies became a major obstacle in her life, that was when she found she could not live a life like any other......
Every victory into darkness brings you closer to defeat.
But she was destined to duel with what was within. Even so, that, whatever “that” was, had become a part of herself, to battle with it would be to harm herself.
And she met Dillion. For so many years, she felt a ray of hope, a ray of light shone through her world. She determined herself to wash herself off the guilt of the plague that claimed hundreds of lives, and the unfair label of darkness. However, what happened was, that when she came back from the wilds, to fulfill her redemption, she found the village had been slaughtered by the Norse, and her most beloved Dillion, was there hanging, to whom a most bloody human sacrifice had been done.
With the sword of Gramr, you may go to Helheim and challenge Hela as an equal.
Senua herself, was actually the goddess of darkness, Hela. There were no actual enemies, no gods, no guardians from the north. It was only herself, her own quest of redemption of her heart. Finally she killed Hela with the sword of Gramr, so she killed her demon inside the heart. And she finally came to realize, that no matter what she does, Dillion could not be brought back. Only way to lay Dillion in peace and to fulfill her redemption was to let him go. So she dropped his skull wrapped in fabrics from the top of the gigantic and symbolic statue of Heilheim, which she had been carrying all the way, and all that, for many years what had troubled her, even nearly destroyed her, was gone in an instant.
This is a sad yet most beautiful story, telling of the Celtic female warrior’s self redemption.
What is most highlighted about this game is that, it has illustrated psychosis to a magnificent level. Not only in the performance shown on screen and audio, presenting hallucination, delusion, voice hearing, but also, it has brought the social involvement into its stories.
It’s unfair for the society to define whoever with the like characters to be psychosis, but it is often the society that has made them this way.
Who would be the evil of Senua’s experiences? The Norse? The villagers? Herself?
NO. The devil behind the scene, is Senua’s father, Zynbel. He witchunted her mother, cursing her of darkness, and made young Senua watch the fire sentence, he abused Senua, made her stay in the dark room all her time. It is him that made every one believe Senua has been cursed, also it is him that has successfully turned Senua’s early symptoms of psychosis into a real threat to her life.
In this way, Ninja theory tells us, that the reaction from the society is a crucial element that causes psychosis. The overall isolation from the public, the bullying, has made it incredibly possible for the psychosis symptoms to come into being. It’s not rare when we hear of some cases where a kid at school develops some symptoms of autism and all that, just because they had been socially isolated or bullied. It’s really considerate for Ninja theory to come to that, in this way they have brought the understanding of psychosis to a whole new level.
You battle with psychosis, then you would be battling with yourself.

I will come to talk about Hela again. As indicated at the end of the game, Hela killed Senua with the sword of Gramr, but it was actually that Senua killed Hela, because Hela then became Senua again after she had desperately dropped Dillion’s skull on top of Heilheim. We could see that, the producers are eagerly transporting the idea that Hela is actually Senua herself.
For so long a time, Senua believed that darkness had cursed her, that she must defeat the goddess of darkness for redemption, and to bring Dillion’s soul back. But it was actually herself that she couldn’t defeat, she couldn’t convince herself that she was innocent, that she was still pure. Because so many years’ experience had strengthened the idea that she was cursed to an incredible level.
Battling with psychosis could be extremely painful, for psychosis is already part of who you are. We could see various scenes where Senua screams and wails out of the pain that the kind of “battle” brings to her. I myself used to carry a light tendency of psychosis, and I understand that kind of feeling perfectly, that feels like a part of you has gone rotten. And I have to stress it again that Ninja theory has done a real good job indicating that.
And when Senua finally defeated Hela, the monstrous devil inside Heilheim, actually inside her own heart, she learned to control her psychosis, and the disastrous feeling was gone. It’s a moment she finally came to realize she was clean.
“I sometimes see the walls melt.”
This is what an invited psychosis patient said on one of Ninja theory’s consult meetings.
The hallucinations, delusions and voice hearing presented have reached the level of true masterpiece.
Since my then psychosis symptoms lie mostly in voice hearing, I don’t know how the other visual symptoms feel like. One of my friends, who also plays Hellblade, and is a very thoughtful person, he says it’s not like that, hallucinations and delusions don’t look like that. That’s different. Since I don’t know how that feels, I can’t judge.
But I say that the performance is impressive. Psychosis has long been a taboo in both movie and video game industry, attempts to present it have either gone to madness or, half failures. Bur for Ninja theory, they made that into a kind of art, a kind of enjoyment, I personally enjoy the connecting marks, bridging bridges. I felt comfortable with that, because Ninja theory didn’t make them into simple repetition and disturbance, like what patients would feel. They intended to make the process as comfortable as possible, with the combined effects of UR4 engine. It’s already an achievement in expressive art.
Hellblade’s success on presenting psychosis is worthy to be labeled a revolution, let alone the many other factors, that being maybe the best indie AAA game ever, adopting the best ever real-time motion capture technology on screen performance, and that our Juergens perfectly acting as Senua while primarily working as the video editor for Hellblade!
I won’t bother to bring out those aspects for that it would make the review way too long. If you’d like to know more about them, you may check out in my Steam discussion!

However, the gameplay is generally lacking. There is a lot of platforming involved, but it is not challenging as the game indicates what you have to do. The combat system is rather simple as you spam the same combos over and over again.

It's difficult to pin down exactly what genre this game is, but I really enjoyed playing it. The story was compelling even if it didn't entirely seem to fit together... but that's the problem with a story about rewriting memories... and the futuristic Paris was great to explore. The gameplay was split roughly into three sections - the platforming section (very calm and non-challenging, but with lots of helpful hints for finding hidden areas), the combat section (no-one in the future has guns, but the melee combat was very much Arkham Asylum and the ability to customise combos made it surprisingly deep) and the memory re-writing section (interesting although I wasn't always entirely sure what I was meant to be doing and would have enjoyed it more if there were multiple possible outcomes that would change the story). Those minor gripes aside, it was a great game with pretty graphics, fun fighting sequences and a compelling story.

Soooooooooo..... where do I even start? I bought Skullgirls because I saw it in a few Videos from YouTubers like Joshscorcher and thought it looked interesting. I first played this game with a keyboard because I didn´t have a gamepad, and although it was playable, it wasn´t all too much fun. Then, a year or two later, I got one and replayed it after I got the 2nd Encore Upgrade. I think I can now safely say that Skullgirls is, without a doubt, the best fighting game I played to this day. Controlls are responsive, gameplay is fluent and balanced out nicely, Characters, while limited, are all unique enough in their playstiles and mechanics to make up for the limited roster. Online is where this game shines the best when compared to other fighting games. I played Street Fighter 4 and 5, Smash Bros Brawl and WiiU/3DS, UMvC3, Rivals of Aether and many others, but none comes even close to Skullgirls when it comes to stable netplay. If only more players would be online, it would be just perfect. And most impressive of all, the story is amazing. Weird, right? A fighting Game with a good story isn´t really something you see so often...
Pros
+Great, responsive controlls
+Amazinig Characters with interesting and unique Stories and playstyles
+Well composed soundtrack
+Amazingly stable Online play
+Detailed and Informative Tutorials for both general Gameplay and indivdual characters
+A lot of cultural and nerdy refernces hidden in character colors and quotes
Cons
-Limited Roster (although not a con for me, for some it can be one)
-Online mode is empty most of the time
All in all, Skullgirls gives you fluid and fast gameplay with a unique cast of characters and what I think to be the best netplay in any fighting game ever for 10 bucks. If you want the full and best experience, get the 2nd Encore Upgrade. Other than that, I recommend this game to anyone who is a pro, a casual or someone who wants to learn fighting games, and seeing how this is one of the first fighters I´ve ever played seriously, I think that´s not so much of a stretch to say. Gamepads, although optional, are more than recommended for the full experience

Running With Riffler Review by Dionysis Spinos (as posted on
It is time for another awesome review. This time I picked an early access indie game called Running With Rifles and believe me I didn’t think , the time I chose it for a review that this game will be that good and so fun playing.
Let’s first start by explaining you what this game is all about. In RWR you join the game as a simple soldier…ohhh yes you heard me well as a simple soldier….no hero, no veteran soldier or something like that…you are just another soldier sent to serve his country and the simple goal of this game is to win the battle and follow the commands of your superior officers. RWR is a tactical shooter game with open-world elements and that is not it. The game offers so many stuff with a lot more to come and imagine that the game is still an Early Access title.
But first things first, let me tell you what I loved about the game. I loved so match the fact that the game features an open-world aspect. Even as a simple soldier you can discover an entire map via campaign or multiplayer giving you the opportunity to find new ways to win your opponent and kill enemy soldiers. Also, the game features hundreds of locations to explore from towns to trenches and snowy valleys all available for the player to fight his way to victory! Another thing I loved about the game is that it includes dozens of different weapons to choose from cover items vehicles you can use from tanks to all kinds of killing machines that will help you reach your goal! Also, I think it is really important to mention that the graphics look really beautiful as well, the sound and the music is really great and it sure helps the title be more appealing to the player. Furthermore, it should really be mentioned that in the game you don’t stay forever a soldier.
As you play, you will have the chance to be promoted to higher ranks and gain higher command to soldiers and equipment and this is a feature of the game that it is really one of my favorite. Also, something that I haven’t mention earlier is that you can use your environment and surrounding to your advantage...from great covers to hide you and your squad to abandoned buildings and other things that make the game even more fun to play. Finally, there are even more features to come in this game from boss battles to more maps and achievements.
The game is really amazing and it is worth checking out for sure, I loved the freedom that this game gives the player and the fact that you begin as just a soldier and you can achieve higher ranks and do so many things. One last advice: it is really easy to die in this game so don’t underestimate the AI. Hope you will have as much fun playing the game as I did.

Spooky’s house of jump scares is a free horror game.
The aim of the game is to get through 1000 rooms in Spooky’s house. Spooky is a ghost who owns the house, and despite that she seems nice, innocent and… (I hate to use this word) cute, she’s actually evil.
The gameplay is that you move through recycled and randomly generated rooms, except for the occasional scripted areas that reference other horror games such as: Silent hill, Resident evil, DOOM 3, Amnesia the dark decent etc. You have over a dozen monsters referred to as specimens all with signature audio and visual ques to know which one is chasing you, most aren’t too bad, but some are quite annoying. The most annoying are the puppet and the silent hill straight jacket monster inspired specimen. Later on you do get an axe which is useful for the lesser enemies and breaking objects blocking doors and the final boss. Sometimes some of the doors are broken, sometimes some of them are locked, but for the most part you’re going room to room and there’s no going backwards. You have a stamina bar which runs out in four seconds but it refills very quickly, and you randomly get “jump scares” by cardboard cut outs of the most un-scariest and most innocent looking anthropomorphic objects usually spiders, pumpkins, tree stumps and ghosts, though later on they sometimes look disturbing.
This is a game that isn’t meant to be taken seriously at all, it’s actually quite a funny game due to its self-aware tone, the funny notes you find lying around, the incredibly unhelpful maps you find on a wall sometimes, the arcade machines with parodies of video games that you can play, references to other horror games; it even does the resident evil door animation sometimes, and the ending which I won’t spoil.
This game does have a few problems though, the reach for the attacks for the monsters is unfairly long, though this isn’t too bad but the worst is the puppet since he teleports behind you, and he only moves when you’re not looking at him, though every time you open a door when being chased by him he gets a free attack on you. You will get stuck on comers for some reason, and that’s not a good thing about a game where you are mostly running away from monsters. The most annoying part is that you can only save if you come across a save point, the first half of the game it’s per 50 rooms but in the second half it’s per 100 rooms and it gets quite annoying to replay bits when you died at room 654 or something and you have to go back to room 600.
But for the most part this is a fun game to play, and it’s for free.

The start of this game is really tedious. Movement is slow, you have a sprint bar that needs to recharge after a few seconds, a jetpack that needs to recharge after a few seconds. You have gathering equipment that can only work a few seconds before overheating and needs fuel to work, so you can run out. You have a life support system that helps you live in toxic biomes, and if you're so lucky to start in one, it'll contstantly be beeping and reminding you to also recharge it.
You have to look for minerals to make items so your spaceship can be repaired. The minerals are dotted across the planet in arbitrary distances from eachother. The planets are filled with plants and creatures, and if you're lucky they won't have cries that will constantly assault your ears as you're walk-sprinting towards another node to finish the repairs on your aircraft.
I didn't make it past the early game, there are too many obvious forced longlivity parts to it all. Your inventory is limited, and you'll slowly make it bigger. Your stamina to sprint is low, you'll probably be able to up it. Your craft is small, you'll probably be able to make it bigger. You can build, so you'll make a base and fill it with stuff, the occasional one mushroom or one creature you find on one of the planets you visit.
The progression wouldn't be as bad if it didn't feel as empty, empty in content and soul. Procedurally generated environments and creatures lack may give you a lot to see, but the stuff you see is all forgettable and boring.
If you have the guts to make it past the refund timer, you may have enough fun, but I advise against it.

first off, please read this in its entirety (i start by ranting about the release version!)
So i was a little taken in by the hype for NMS and on release, sure, it was missing a metric f-ton of promised features. But on the whole, it was a very nice looking game and gave me a fair few hours of exploring (though I'll freely admit, not worth the money it was asking for; it sat on my list of "hey its on 60% offer, you should try it if you're bored" games).
Inevitably, i got bored of it, planets just became a bland mix of vibrantly coloured backdrops to mine a random selection of already limited varieties of resorce, oh, and maybe adding a slot to my backpack once in a blue moon. to do what? no really, what was i supposed to do with it all? trudge to the centre of the galaxy punctuated by a vauge interpretive plot that would only be fit for a modern art museum, only to have to do it all again? forever?
still, i enjoyed the 60 or so hours of play i had, so i was content to just leave it there.
-----------------------------------and now------------------------------------------------
so, hey, qudos to Hello Games for powering through an abysmal launch, many devs would have rather buried all copies of it somewhere remote, and pretend it didnt happen (de-ja-vu, didnt someone do this already!)
anyway, 2 full updates later and its looking like a much better game, where as before NMS looked like an alpha framework  for a decent game, as of 1.3, its started to grow into its exosuit.
the lore is so much more tangable now, and i havent even started the Atlas questline as of writing. the addition of freighters and bases gives alot to save up for and build with those full cargo holds we used to have and gives us an option to somewhat settle in a system and call it home, rather than the constantly lost feeling of trying to backtrack to that one planet that had exotic stuff to mine and sell. geocraft make exploring a world alot more accessable and the addition of nanite clusters as a currency makes duplicating technologies a thing of the past (and you actually have to make friends with the npc races to buy better stuff now)
classic and creative modes are both satisfying to explore with, and new biomes and resorces actually make this interesting again!
survival and hardcore are as brutal and unforgiving as you should expect, the tense moments and challenges it creates are a refreshing addition to the game.
one point to note of though, the "joint exploration" aka "multiplayer" its a nice touch, you can 'meet' up with your friends and chat, though you cant actually do much else as of yet. still, watch this space, this could just be a way of them slowly implementing actual multiplayer, we'll see.
if you are new to this game, dont look too much at the reveiws for the launch version, and take the game at face value; if you played the lauch version and hated it because it wasnt what was promised, i emplore you to come back and try it again.

Conflict: Desert Storm was one of my favorite games for PS2 as a kid, and within the first few minutes of playing, the nostolgia was already there. I was a little annoyed when I discovered that my Xbox 360 controller doesn't work with the game, but the mouse/keyboard controls are surprisingly not bad, with only a few clunky bindings. The game doesn't feel near as difficult as it was when I was a kid, even when I play on hard. I recall having a tough time even on easy difficulty back on the PS2 version. The most difficult part about both versions is the tank combat. Engaging with a tank is fairly tricky, due to the fact that tanks are really well armored on the front and sides. Tanks are really only exposed in the rear, which is explained in the heavy weapons training session. When I used to play this game and heard a tank rolling nearby, I would litterally sh*t myself because of how accurate and deadly they were. After confronting a few tanks in the new version, I still feel the same way, although they don't seem quite as accurate. The graphics haven't been altered in any way, so unfortunately the game doesn't support any modern resolutions. This isn't game-ruining though, I personally enjoy the dated graphics. If you're someone who played this game on PS2 or the OG Xbox, and want some nostolgia, I would highly recommend it. Coming from someone who has played the orignal version, I have to say, it's held up extremely well. I've never written a review on a game before, mostly because I'd only write a review on a game I had a huge issue with, or a really good time with. For anyone wanting to relive the past, or just try the game out when it's on sale: Don't hesitate. It's a great game if you're willing to get past the old graphics and ocasionally clunky controls. I give it a 10/10.

The first game I've played wherein the protagonist has paranoid schizophrenia. Tenderly written, and terrifyingly accurately depicted, the quest upon which brave but damaged Senua embarks is spurred by delusion, and hampered by threats which are the products of a tragically psychotic mind.
Terrified and confused, but ultimately courageous and conquering, Senua is a heroine for all who suffer from mental illness and battle demons on a daily basis.
The gameplay itself is entertaining enough hack-and-slash fair with some puzzles along the way, the graphics are nothing short of breathtaking, the sound mixing is superb and does a good job of mimicking the experience of "hearing voices".
However, the true standout is the writing, whereby the exposition of story - as brilliant as it is - is ancillary to the development of Senua's fascinating character, who - being a shieldmaiden during the age of Vikings - would be tragically unaware that her experiences are purely the result of an illness in her mind.

This IS a great game. I remember watching a friend play almost all of this game when it was first released on xbox 360 and i remember how blown away i was by its fluid character movement through games open world something i had never seen before this game. The game had amazing music, sounds, world detail, combat, and story that made me very very hopeful for the future of gaming. I remember saying to my friend that it would be the most amazing thing after a few more installations of this IP how great it would be to have the games story move into the modern era with Desmond taking town to new templars. While i have not actually played the rest of the overkill that is AC annual releases it does not seem to have done this yet… This game remains very good.
HOWEVER!
This is a Ubisoft Title and with that comes the 90% of the time fact that it will just not run on computers a few years newer than the game very well (ie XIII & Beyond Good & Evil)
A few of things i ran into finally playing this game in the year 2015 and what i had to do to make it work for me.
-Absolutely no in-game overlays can exist it will just crash. raptr, steam overlay, caused ShadowPlay caused crashes for me. Shadow Play also caused graphical artifacts and sound distortion randomly. (while having all of these turned off or disabled there were still time that game crashed but i was able to get past the title screen)
-The game will crash at random times when you complete certain actions like killing a templar in the game world because the game tries to connect to ubisoft server that does not exist anymore. Its recommended that you turn off the internet to computer you are playing it on but you can also use your firewall setup to block it.
-iirc correctly this game may have come out before the wireless xbox 360 setup was available for pc. I “think” it was patched in later in the version that you can buy on steam. So the game does see the “wireless” controller but by default it is set-up incorrectly the triggers serve as camera movements left and right but are opposite. the colors of the buttons and on screen prompts are counter clock-wise wrong by one position. this can all be fixed with a little bit of tinkering in the buggy options menu or in the ini files.
-not as important but still relevant. this is an open world game with  many thing to find and collect. two of which i found rather pointless. Flags & Templars. They serve no real purpose in the game. they existed on the console version for achievements and trophies that do not exist on the pc version at all steam or uplay. This is not a uplay game just fyi it was long before it existed and was never incorporated. but anyways while i am usually one to take my time and find all of the things in games this game gave me no motivation to do so, neither achievements or in game unlockables…
-the actual controls and character movements now feel very tank like. a sort of inbetween modern 3rd person games and classic tomb raider for lack of better comparison.
In conclusion This IS a great game and it is very fun but it was not made to be future proof. It takes a good bit of work to enjoy. I can't recommend it on modern systems but if you are willing to do the work get it running it is a lot of fun perhaps mostly nostalgia.

The age old battle FIFA Vs PES rages on, this one has lasted longer than the Great Nintendo Vs Sega Consoles wars!
This year will be no different with both games trying to dominate the charts. In recent years FIFA has been easily the winner is this a case of history repeating itself or will PES come out on top? Since the Playstation I have been a PES player and hardly ever touched FIFA only playing FIFA when going around to friends houses who never understood the gameplay and strategic capabilities of PES. I have one friend however, when ever we met up all we did was play PES easily sitting down for hours playing…just one more game.
Due to EA Sports swallowing any license associated with football since its incarnation (except for Champions League). Konami have been clever, allowing users to manually correct player names,  club emblems, kits, and now chants stadiums, flags, shoes, Advertising boards… the list goes on! This has proved exceptionally popular allowing people to build their own dedicated football title. But since the launch of the Playstation 2 there has never actually been a version of PES that actually played as well as the original incarnations, recent releases had many flaws, and never moved forward both graphically and in playability. Adding to this my team getting demoted to the Championship did not help my as the “modders” at that time were only interested in the top tier divisions this also made me turn to FIFA as I never wanted to play as any other team than the one I had supported all my life (even if they were called North West London).
Back in 2016 I read the reviews of PES 16 It sounded awesome, the reviews were positive and I had just upgraded my PC, “Now is the time to go back” I said to myself this game has the looks, the modding community is flourishing and the game looks fantastic…but then reality check, after buying the game on the PC I realised the version on the PC was inferior to the console versions, to this day my steam library shows 42 hours of game play on PES 2016, I tried I really did, but again I was lured back to FIFA.
Roll on 2018… Again lots of positive reviews, the hype train is kicking in and I have some left over wages, the time feels right! Eagerly waiting for the download to complete, I have a lightbulb moment! “modders” I start searching the web for option files and patches for the new version (it has not even been out a day yet!) having found loads of option files allowing me to play as my beloved QPR straight away, no messing all I need to do is add the option file and away we go.
The download completes I run through the setup process, again the controller options is a seperate Executable on the PC (when will Konami put this in to the game?) Then eagerly launch the game for the first time, watching the amazing intro… waiting then BAM, the menu appears and I feel like I am back in 2012 “huh what wheres the glitz? The glamour?” Playing FIFA for the last few years I clearly have become spoilt! There are no “razzle” “dazzle”, “wooshy”, “swooshy” menus, just some-thing I could have drafted in photoshop in 20 minutes, the music is OK, it has recent tracks from Linken Park & The Clean Bandits and other current artists, but even then the audio does not have the same “omph” as FIFA does? “dont panic, its just the menus” I tell myself.
Before playing a single game I proceed to import the config file, this is completed by following easy instructions, I select “my” team click through the game options and start the game and then it happens… It feels really familiar in a very good way, it looks the same yet better, (using the fox engine)  the player animations are fluid the commentary is still as terrible as I remember. Can this be the game I loved all those years ago?
I am running down the wing, fake turn, carry on running then press X button, then it happened… muscle memory has kicked in, and in a moment of excitement I reverted to FIFA controls, digging in to those brain cells trying to remember once again I take control, slide tackle run cross shoot… score, yes its all coming back “The love of the game” “This is it” I tell myself… This is it!
After wrestling with my muscle memory I win my first game, I go back in to the menu to see what other modes this game has to offer, Online Co-op modes now include 2v2 & 3v3 and of course local friends. Online also incorporates PES League integration, allowing you to compete in the eSports competition with myClub. MyClub also allows you to build your CO-OP team with your friends so you are now able to combine squads.There is the now legendary Master League this now includes Challenges and goals, you will now be given a set of objectives and challenges according to the state of your team, which are important if you want to stay in the job! Finally there is the return of Fan Favourite, the mode returns with more ways to play and new various new elements.
Many hours in and I write this review of PES 18, the future looks promising I doubt very much I will purchase FIFA this year, the modding scene for PES is too large to ignore and the game itself possibly plays better than any version I have ever played. The game is far from flawless however with the goalkeepers still flapping more than David James in a kipper shop and the crowd chanting as if you are playing at Camp Nou even if you are playing one of the low league teams. Reading between the lines all this can change especially on the PC with the help of the modders (for example I already have a SkyTV swipe for replays)
The game runs very well on Win10 with maxed settings.
