Ursprünglich eine Mod für Arma 2 gewesen, aber aufgrund der Beliebtheit jetzt als eigenständiges Spiel erhältlich. Strategische, anspruchsvolle und äußerst spannende Gefechte an der Ostfront, wahlweise auf russischer oder deutscher Seite. Realismus pur dank dem Arma 2- Grundgerüst. Am besten für Kenner der Arma- oder Operation: Flashpoint- Reihe. Die einzelnen Missionen können sehr langwierig sein und locker 2 - 3 Stunden dauern. Man muss taktisch und im Team vorgehen, Einzelgänger haben keine Chance! Man beginnt als Schütze, muss aber bald seinen ersten Infanteriezug befehligen, und das ist bitter nötig um die Missionen zu erfüllen. Später im Spiel gesellen sich ganze Panzerzüge dazu. Der Spieler kann (und muss) sämtliche Fahr- und Flugzeuge selbst steuern, allerdings sind bei Panzern mehrere Soldaten nötig, da jede Position im Panzer besetzt sein muss, damit er am besten funktioniert. Wer sich einmal in das komplexe Befehlssystem reingefuchst hat, wird mit spannenden und nervenaufreibenden Gefechten in  wunderschöner Grafik belohnt. So gut wurde die Ostfront in noch keinem Shooter umgesetzt! Störend sind höchstens die etwas mangelhafte Wegfindung der KI-Kameraden und gelegentliche amerikanische Sprachsamples (Kein deutscher Landser hätte damals "Oh♥♥♥♥♥♥" oder "♥♥♥♥!" gerufen), die noch ein Überbleibsel aus dem "Hauptspiel" Arma 2 sind.

I was on a business trip to Hong Kong and when I came back early Monday I experienced jet lag for the whole week. I woke up every morning around 5am and couldn't sleep anymore. So i needed to find something to entertain myself during that morning period. Then I remembered about Wolfenstein 2 - game that I insta pre-ordered after the day it was announced, but never tried since it was released, because of other games and work.
So for the whole week, all my sleepless mornings was full of Nazi killing actions, fighting my way to the truth, to the freedom and, most important part, for revenge. I almost forgot that feeling, when you enjoy the full story rich single player campaign game, without even bothering yourself with those microtransactions-lootboxes bs. And now, ladies and getlemen, we are back on the track!
First Wolfenstein game (2013) left us with a kinda bitter taste, a cliffhanger and all the players were pretty much excited and hyped after the second game was announced. I didn't care much about it, because to be honest, I wasn't a big fan of 2013 Wolfenstein, which was boring for me at certain points and all I cared about was William J. Blazkowicz, I really wanted to know about his future.
The moment I launched the game, I was shocked already in first 15 minutes - game starts with a row of action full cutscenes, mixed with William's childhood flashbacks, some of them are pretty much rough and violent, shocking if you like. I appreciated that move, because these cutscenes let the player understand what to expect from the whole game.
The whole shooting experience is really enjoyable as well, they did a massive work and improved a lot since 2013. The only disappointment for me was a variety of weapons, I was expecting more comparing to the first game. And, speaking of weapons - you will be forced to make a choice at the beginning of the game which will affect what weapon you will get in the future.
One major thing, that really impressed me in the game and I am still not quite sure how they can implement all these Nazi emblems and fascist propaganda stuff, which are strongly prohibited in most of the countries all over the world in their Wolfenstein games without any problems and scandals, especially now, when you can easily get in trouble only because of simple tweet, joking on something, what wasn't prohibited few years ago. So I am taking a bow before Machine Games and mostly Bethesda, for their brave and fearless development of game, talking about such topics. That is really insane.
Ok, to sum everything up!
You should grab this game if you:
+ Love FPS games
+ Miss that old times when single player rich story campaign game wasn't a big deal for developers
+ Wanna have some fun time shooting and blowing everything around
+ Once again - love rich story games with amazing, sometimes shocking and graphically insane cutscenes
+ Want to survive insomnia :D
+ Love challenge. Try this game on a highest difficult and you will not be disappointed, trust me.
+ Wanna have a chance to stump Hitler with your shoe after the rehearsal :) Worth it!
Avoid this game if you:
- Not into action shooting games
- Have an old GPU, the main reason of the Mixed reviews on Steam is because of "bad optimization" , but I guess we all know what does that mean
- Can't stand Nazi topic at any possible form.
Enjoy!

Assassin's Creed came out in 2007 and here I am 7 years later playing this game for the first time.
I must say that I have purchased it during the sale but I can tell you right now that its worth the full price. Not to mention it's only like $10 anyway!
So what's so fun about it you might ask. Let me tell you. After you finally start running around and killing the enemies the game becomes fun! I have once spent 80% the mission just hunting the guards and doing all the other random things. For me, the selling part of this game is running around and jumping on the rooftops.
Controls. I understand that this game was ported from a console so controls for PC only users will be funny. I didn't not try to reset them because they are still well put. But, its not your normal WASD + ctrl and space. You will just have to get used to that.
While playing this game you don't often notice the sound effects and the music, but I can tell that it plays its part in delivering the whole picture very well. Its nothing impressive, but what is important that it does not spoil the experience and only enchants it. Although I have not tried, but I can see myself actually playing some other music while running around the city.
The very first time I ran this game was actually in 2007. The computer I was running it on couldn't even handle it. That is partially the reason why I only came back to the game now. At the time of release the graphics very amazing. The foggy city environment impressed me in particular. The models of characters are very well made as well, buildings are quite detailed. Nothing really to complain about as 7 years later it still looks good.
You might say, what an unfair review, where are the negative things? Well they are here as per any game. For example I don't quite like how character moves sometimes and how he cant do certain jumps and things. But its all negligible I think. Oh, and once I flew from my horse really high. The worst thing is that it only saves your game when you have completed something which can be quite an annoyance.
The story is not all there is to do. You can actually explore the cities to find some random flags. I am not too sure what they going to give you at the end, but there's quite a number of them to be found and  they also might be in places where you wont be able to reach from the first time. So a few more challenges. Oh and I almost forgot to mention the Templars. They are very hard to deal with, but there are always ways to abuse the system( find out for yourself).
Re-playability is low in my opinion, because once you finish this game you can get the next one and then the next one and so on. You will be playing the same game but with the different filling inside.
So in overall, I think the developers made a externally good game( which evolved into a big sequence of games). I would recommend this game to pretty much anybody.

Everything good and fun about this game is also everything that's frustrating.
The story is good. The combat is mostly fun. Free running is mostly fun. The "jump and tackle/stab someone" move is awesome. But almost all of those have very frustrating moments that get all the more frustrating the more they happen.
Lockon is absolute crap. There was moments where I was trying to quickly assassinate someone with a throwing knife and ended up either missing or getting spotted before I could strike. To make matters worse, even if I was spotted but still close enough for a throwing knife kill, the game locks on the closest enemy to me.
To enter combat, one must press R to enter combat mode (read: lock on to enemies). This is EXTREMELY frustrating when you're trying to quickly dispatch one or two enemies in your way before moving on (when you're in group of five or more). There are also times you'll think you're fighting only to realize the game didn't automatically enter combat mode for you. It's extremely inconsistent.
When on ledges near enemies, there doesn't seem to be away to assassinate your enemy without first awkwardly jumping down and hoping he doesn't hear you (unless you have throwing knives). I once had someone RIGHT in front of me but botched the stealth assassination because I was out of knives and couldn't do the "jump wrist stab" move.
The assassination get repetitive after awhile. You do the same thing over and over. Get 3 sources of info, report back, assassinate. Get 3 sources of info, report back, assassinate. Et Cetera. The concept is cool, but gets less interesting each time.
When given advice on where to investigate, the game doesn't seem to keep a log of the info the local bureau has given you. That never get's annoying. Plus, it seems (from what I've seen) you must re-synchronize every time your told to investiage the "southeast" or "north" or whatever. That or they expect you to immediately recognize or remember what a Middle-Eastern hostpital looks like.
Free running is super fun when it works. It's super frustrating when it doesn't. Altair might jump in the wrong direction, jump too far, not jump far enough, jump into a wall instead of an enemy, jump off a building, etc. This will ruin a lot of missions for you, or make them take longer.
Also annoying is when drunk and crazy people in the streets push you into others and you're chased by the guards because of it.
So yeah, as much as I hate certain parts of the game, I still recommend it. Just know what you're getting into.
And here's hoping each future game gets better and better.
Also, the game seems to run like crap on DX10 (when there are more then 10 people in a crowd, the FPS drop like bombs). I had to open the Local Game Files (or whatever Steam calls it) to launch the DX9 version which runs a million times better (also why Steam only shows me having played the game for about 1 1/2 hours). And it's not because my PC can't handle the max graphics or anything. It's in the software. I can run BF4 on High-Ultra settings with my current setup.
Good game overall but a bit repetitive in the scenario, the game mechanics and progression.

I followed the development of this game for several years. After it was released  I avoided it, because of all the negative reactions. However, I remained hopeful that the developers, who promised free updates, would eventually follow through on their original promis.
I cannot compare this to it's original release, however I will say that I enjoy what I have played so far.
That being said I wanted to also write this as an address to the community as a whole.
I read several reviews on this site. I saw several people who have decided that we are being payed to write a possitive review. After playing it myself, I HIGHLY doubt that is the case.
I want to also address the people who want to say that they felt cheated, and still consider that they were conned.
Now there is a lot I can say. I have been watching this whole pandamonium play out.
First off, I have to ask you all, have you ever made a mistake in your life? And if so do you feel you deserve a second chance to make it right?
If you answer no to the first question, then wow, I would love to meet you. I have never met a perfect person before. :)
If you answer no to the second question, than man, you need a hug. You may no feel you deserve a second chance, but I hope you can find it in yourself to forgive youself.... :p
*ahem*
Now to consider a bit of what I feel happened....
First off does anyone remember no man's sky being delayed?
Did anyone see the comments that people made when it was delayed?
If you didn't look, I saw on several forums, people said things like,
"The developers need to hurry up and just finish it!"
Likely the developers were recieving angry mail from fan's directly with this message.
Now consider that the developers eventually caved in under the pressure of annoyed fans, who wanted them to "go ahead and release it."
Now imagine that these people who said "They need to go ahead and release it," some of them are now the same people complaining saying "They conned us."
Sit with that and consider it carefully.
How often is it that a developer spends over a year after release working on free content for a game?
If a developer offers free content, he obviously didn't feel it was complete in the first place.
Doesn't it make sense that he caved into the pressure of angry fans, who asked, "You should hurry up and finish it?" Or does that seem like a crazy theory?
Maybe we as fans should just wait patiently next time a developer delays a game.
This is a small studio full of developers that have likely not released many games on the market. Out of a lack of experience they caved into the pressure.
Now they are working around the clock to right their wrong, and improve this game despite all of the negative critisism? Do you feel they at least deserve the chance to right their wrong?
Can we also use this as a lesson to learn to stop pressuring developers to "hurry up and finish an unfinished game?"
Also consider now, for those of you who want to hate on this game, would you like them to stop these free updates? Would you like them to stop working so hard to improve this game? Do you feel that would be a desireble outcome? Do you feel any good is comming out of you being negative? Especially at this point in time?

After the mess that was the launch of No Man's Sky I think it deserved the response it received. We were promised many things, many of the things we were promised were not in the game we paid $60 for. Hello Games (especially Sean Murray) have been dragged through the mud since release. They could have taken every single cent from the huge amount of sales the game made and ran, but THEY didn't. From the rumors of Hello Games offices being abandoned to the MONTHS of silence from Hello Games . They've come through, and from my understanding of Sean's GDC talk they simply ran out of money. NMS is an incredibly ambitious title for such a small team to create. I won't excuse their handling of the situation but in reality, even if they had told everyone that they ran out of money there would have been an uproar. Not nearly as big but none the less...an uproar.
I bought this game, I told my friends to pre-order. Non of us refunded it as we all had spent too long to be in the window but while we were stuck with this game we accepted what it was and that we were essentially out $60. Then, the first update came. It wasn't much but it was a glimmer of hope that Hello Games cared enough about this game to at least salvage it. Each subsequent update made that glimmer bright and brighter. With Atlas Rises I don't think anyone can logically question that Hello Games at least has the integrity to push through this dark, and dreary year they've had to see this passion project through. I've put at least 15hrs in since the Atlas Rises update and I've barely scratched the surface of what this update has brought.
Is it worth $60? Did the version we were shown back before release look worth $60? If so then I would say yes. It is now 96% of the way towards being the game we were shown. (still no giant sand worms Sean!) The game we all fell in love with, the game we all spent our money on. The game Sean Murray teased and teased only to let us down for reasons we may never have the complete answers to. It's right there, in front of us all now. It's been a year since the implosion of the hype trains core. We've had time to settle, Hello Games has been rebuilding and damn it. They've rebuilt.

Vector is a indie auto runner game kind of like bit.trip runner, where you sort obstacles and try to get perfect scores in each level while also running from the hunter.
In this game all your moves are parkour like, and you only use two buttons, up to jump and down to slide, every now and then you will need to match the jump button at the exact moment to perform a special sweet looking parkour moves which also get you some distance advantage over your opponent.
There's more than 30 levels to play and a about 20 bonus levels to play, and you can also unlock the hunter mode where you become the hunter and it's your job to shock/kill the runaway runner.
The story is non existant but it's not relevant in this kind of game, the soundtrack is decent but not memorable, it kind of feels the same in each level, and if you replay every level until you get 3 stars you will be sick tired of hearing it.
Fun game worth it even at full price for a few hours of fun, at the moment of this review it's on a bundle with a few more awesome games.

I got this game in a bundle and was interested in trying out a 2D speedrunning/parkour game. The experience was both satisfying and frustrating at different times, and it is a game that I revisit with my best friend.
If you like speedrunning/parkour, flashy tricks, precision platforming gaming, and semi-casual gameplay, then you will enjoy this game.
The aesthetics are nice - the amount of detail in the different backgrounds is good, and the different character animations (in particular, the large amount of speedrunning tricks) can be pretty flashy. A well-executed run is very aesthetically pleasing because of the smoothness in the movement transitions; however, this will also show you how bad you are doing when you are bumping into every obstacle. The music and sounds are good, however, I quickly decided to play my own music to add to the intensity of the gameplay. The levels are short enough to allow this game to be played in bursts, which is something I appreciated greatly.
The controls are easy to familiarize yourself with, however, I personally prefer using a controller - both the keyboard and controller have very responsive controls. Many movements require you to hit the appropriate key once your character enters a specific window (a square showing the type of movement), and you will not be able to do these special tricks without entering the window. The game rewards precision immensely - you will quickly notice that jumping even a few steps too early/late can result in your immediate death. There is a tutorial that is a little too long, but also very helpful in teaching you most elements in the game. The learning curve is minimal to moderate, and much of the game involves repeated trial and error (ex: finding that perfect spot to jump from to land on an obstacle instead of crashing into it). The most challenging part you will encounter is getting the timing correct. For achievement hunters, you will have a grand time trying to get 100%, there is a large enough amount of levels to keep you interested and playing.
During gameplay, your character is running toward an end point at the right side of the map. Along the way, you may collect pickups that add to your score (you need all of them for full stars (3/3) at the end). Trick boxes will litter the stage, and you need to have unlocked the specific skill found within before you can actually execute it. In the later levels, you will also have to
There are multiple stages and many bonus ones as well.
Overall, the game is a lot of fun and remains challenging at a very appropriate pace. Any parkour/platforming enthusiasts will enjoy Vector and should definitely give this game a try.
Recommend!

The port runs fine for me. No complaints. The frame rate is not amazing but the console version never did any better, and the PC version can handle four times the people crowding the streets.
I've played this extensively on the PS3 so what follows is my experience from that.
Part love letter to otaku culture and Akihabara, part goofy comedy, with a dash of Yakuza and Gladiator Begins, Akiba's Trip is hard to describe easily. A loving recreation of Japan's nerdiest district, trying, not always successfully, to imbue it with a sense of wonder and mystery, with all the sorts of crazy characters you might expect to see in such a place, from overwrought lolitas to tsundere idols to obsessed otakus to goofy foreigners excited to drink in the culture. The nonstop ads for animes, video games, and the like providing the background noise as you wander the streets. The worldcraft is not as good as GTA or Yakuza, but there's something to like about this virtual Akihabara.
The actual gameplay is just as charming, and just as rough around the edges. It's an action-RPG beat-em-up where you aim to damage an opponent's clothes enough to tear them off. While there is not a lot of skill to the system, your weapons always hit with a satisfying thunk, thwack, or clank, and most combats involve you trying to weaken every enemy's clothes to set up for a massive chain strip, which gives the combat a satisfying meta-game where the simple guards, counters, and guard breaks don't otherwise provide much to go with. Naturally, you want to collect every type of clothing and weapon you can to fill out those collectible books.
Side-quests, exploration, multiple endings based on which girl you end up with, the game is quite short but meant to be replayed. The difficulties then are built more around your level gear than your own skill, but the game exercises one bit of brilliance here: Your XP is reset each game. So you can always redo a low difficulty without being overpowered play just by shelving your overpowered 999 weapons and clothes and crafting up something from scratch again, whereas if you need to take on the high difficulties, you can always whip out the good gear again.
If you have a heart that likes charming, unpretentious, and goofy anime schlock, you should enjoy Akiba's Trip.

This is a copy of the review I put on a social media page. Forgive the inconsistencies.
A while back, I recommended a psychological thriller genre game called 'Observer', starring Rutger Hauer. I found another amazing game, this one is a bit better than Observer, and touches on subjects of interest to many people in my friend list. It is called,
Hellblade: Senua's Sacrifice
Some time ago I watched a video on Youtube that was made by a woman with sever schizophrenia. Her goal was, to show healthy people what it was like to suffer from this disease. It showed that sufferers of this condition will frequently experience auditory and visual hallucinations. Most times they will be victims of many voices, each with their own personality, fears, and desires, and they will bombard the victim with conflicting information, sometimes to the point of sensory overload. I will link this video below the main post. There is a trigger warning at the beginning of the video that is well deserved. It gives you a window into a mind you might rather not step into.
The reason I mention this is, the main character in this game is a victim of schizophrenia, and based on what I have seen, it is a frighteningly accurate portrayal. In fact, this game uses the schizophrenic condition as a play mechanism. It is necessary to tell the story and to play the game and is really quite brilliant.
The theme of this game is Norse mythology, more so than any other game I have ever played. In the first hour of play you will find out why. If you ever wanted to be a Viking Shaman on a vision quest, this is as close as you will ever get (though a Viking Shaman is not what Senua is). As an added bonus, there are stones throughout the game that tell some of the deeper aspects of Norse mythology through the medium of another schizophrenic shard of personality. It's really quite disturbing and beautiful.
The visuals of this game are stunning, but the puzzles are some of the most interesting I have ever seen. This game is best played in headphones as the global positioning of sound is an important aspect of the game. This has the added effect of putting Senua's voices in YOUR head. It is almost a schizophrenia simulation and can be quite disturbing at times.
I won't spoil the game. Check out the trailer. It's relatively inexpensive. I purchased it with a refund I had sitting in my Paypal account.
The line between art and game is blurring and this is definitely on the art end of the spectrum.

People have complained that this is just "ArmA 2" in the Second World War. They also complain that there are "too many" WWII themed games. They also just got ArmA 2 for Day Z. While it's true there was a time when WWII settings were popular, this was late 90s, to mid 2000s, spurred on by the success of MOH:AA and the first CoD. When CoD struck gold with MW, the emphasis went to modern warfare and then when L4D did the same, now we have zombie titles as far as the eye can see. So, in otherwords, these people are morons.
So, Iron Front is $29.99. A fair price. What do you get from it? The best incarnation of the ArmA 2 engine and a much more well developed experience than ArmA 2, especially in regards to vehicles combat. They optimized their game very well and are clearly lovers of the history here. The hardware, all of it, is pain-stakingly detailed and accurate. The powerful ArmA 2 mission editor is there, the AI is improved, it's all an improvement on ArmA 2. For $29.99? Yeah, this is all worth it. An obscure theatre in WWII is welcome and the developers have already released DLC for it. Two campaigns covering the Soviet and Wehrmahct forces in both English and their native languages. The developers are history buffs and did the subject matter due justice without showing any overt bias to any faction. If you love sims, if you love more realism in you games, this is one you honestly should get. It's clearly made BY history buffs FOR history buffs.

It will♥♥♥♥♥♥you off so far you'll revert into childhood.
I've played nearly all of the souls games at least twice - including the original King's field games - enjoyed Limbo's malarky, finished Rogue Legacy, tackled Nuclear Throne, Inside, Enter the Gungeon, Ikaruga, Jamestown, bullet hells, roguelikes, etc. I like my games hard and, generally speaking, when i decide to stop playing one of them it's because i've had my fill of them. I usually leave them with memories of a good time.
But THIS game. THIS freaking game.
I will leave this game with a sense of disappointment. Of having being meticulously stabbed in each toe while watching a Miyazaki film at the theatre. What the hell, man. I don't think i've been so angry at a game in recent memory. I'm an adult, why am i taking the time to write this even - i have things to do.
I want to be able to look back and point at a game i see as a bad example: how not to be snarky. How not o be uncharitable with your game. It's almost spiteful in its design. I don't beleive i'm even saying this - this game has some of the best art and environement design you'll ever see in a 2D game. But it's also purposefully toying with you.
I guess if you had to comparte this game to a person, this would be that rich kid with all the toys, and he'll only let you play if you do what he says, exactly what he says. If you don't, he'll put you in a cage, until you do what he says. I'd rather play with my other friend, Dark Souls - he's dirty and messed up, eats out of the dirt, but at least he's honest and lets you do things your way.
5 out of 10 adulthoods - play it if you enjoy snarky games. Otherwise, just watch someone else play it - it's extremely polished.

Controls are tight and responsive, which is a good thing since Ori subscribes to the "easy to learn, hard to master school". Some parts of the game can be teeth grindingly hard, but it will never feel impossible.
Music and sound are both a delight to the ears with the music being the perfect blend of background music, yet just noticable enough to draw your attention.
The only disappointing part of Ori is that it can feel a bit short, and there was no real boss fights. Some amazing action sequences but it would have been nice to have a good ol' boss battle at some point.

Here is an honest non "It's cool to hate on No Man's Sky" review. Lets start with Pros/Cons.
Pros:
- Atmosphere.
- Graphic style.
- Massive universe.
- Exploration.
- Ship v ship combat.
- Space battles
- Unique Multi - tools.
- Unique freighters, some can even be purchased.
- No loading screens.
- Unique creatures.
- Lore.
- 30+ hours of story (as of 1.3)
- Multiplayer-ish. (players dont have character models [yet] .)
- Portals, for easy travel between specific planets.
- Base building.
- Different game modes. ( Creative | Survival | Permadeath | Normal )
- Unique star ships with different classes. (A, B, C, S)
Cons:
- Optimization.
- On foot combat. (once you reach a certian point in normal mode, sentinals and hostile creatures are no threat at all.)
- Quests sometimes un pin themselves and make it so you cant turn in quests, making you have to re pin the quest in  progress.
- How much plotinum launch thrusters use.
- Price of freighters and starships. freighters can go up to 139,000,000u!
- inventory managment at the start of the game.
- How long it can take to get from point A to point B.
All in all, I respect Hello Games for sticking with their product after all the ♥♥♥♥♥torm at launch. GIVE THIS GAME A CHANCE, ESPICALLY ON SALE!!!! The start will be slow, but I have yet to truly hate this game, or even get bored.

This is a copy of the review I put on a social media page. Forgive the inconsistencies.
A while back, I recommended a psychological thriller genre game called 'Observer', starring Rutger Hauer. I found another amazing game, this one is a bit better than Observer, and touches on subjects of interest to many people in my friend list. It is called,
Hellblade: Senua's Sacrifice
Some time ago I watched a video on Youtube that was made by a woman with sever schizophrenia. Her goal was, to show healthy people what it was like to suffer from this disease. It showed that sufferers of this condition will frequently experience auditory and visual hallucinations. Most times they will be victims of many voices, each with their own personality, fears, and desires, and they will bombard the victim with conflicting information, sometimes to the point of sensory overload. I will link this video below the main post. There is a trigger warning at the beginning of the video that is well deserved. It gives you a window into a mind you might rather not step into.
The reason I mention this is, the main character in this game is a victim of schizophrenia, and based on what I have seen, it is a frighteningly accurate portrayal. In fact, this game uses the schizophrenic condition as a play mechanism. It is necessary to tell the story and to play the game and is really quite brilliant.
The theme of this game is Norse mythology, more so than any other game I have ever played. In the first hour of play you will find out why. If you ever wanted to be a Viking Shaman on a vision quest, this is as close as you will ever get (though a Viking Shaman is not what Senua is). As an added bonus, there are stones throughout the game that tell some of the deeper aspects of Norse mythology through the medium of another schizophrenic shard of personality. It's really quite disturbing and beautiful.
The visuals of this game are stunning, but the puzzles are some of the most interesting I have ever seen. This game is best played in headphones as the global positioning of sound is an important aspect of the game. This has the added effect of putting Senua's voices in YOUR head. It is almost a schizophrenia simulation and can be quite disturbing at times.
I won't spoil the game. Check out the trailer. It's relatively inexpensive. I purchased it with a refund I had sitting in my Paypal account.
The line between art and game is blurring and this is definitely on the art end of the spectrum.

A hidden gem, in all honesty. The review scores from sites like metacritic are pretty skewed and unforgiving. It has a lot to like about it, even if there are some elements that aren't so good.
Pros:
-The main character is pretty likeable, interesting, and is realistic. She makes the occasional quip or sarcastic remark, she's remorseful, she's skilled and strong but she doesn't pretend to be an invincible hero. She discovers her past and what she has done, and both accepts and laments who she is. She's flawed, but just as anyone should be. Also she's somewhat non-standard for a main/female video game character, and the deviation from the norm is very appreciated.
-The story is all about memory. Recovering lost memories. Altering others' perceptions and world views. Learning what it means to really live, to embrace even the bad memories. Almost everything in this game involves the technology that surrounds this new day and age of "Sensen" and digital memories. Lose your memories, get them back, kick♥♥♥♥♥ and make everyone remember. Really cool take on the 'dystopia' setting.
-The setting is a somewhat run of the mill 'future dystopia' kind of thing, but it still manages to pull you in with the beautiful scenes and art. From sewers, to modern apartment complexes and malls, to prison, it's decently diverse in where it takes you. You even revisit some levels, but they're not the same: they've changed with the events of the game as it unfolds.
-The combat is a little clunky at first, but after a little adjusting and unlocking more of the system, it becomes pretty fun and fluid. It's kind of like the Arkham series of Batman games lately but with a couple of minute differences (like no counters). It can also seem a little repetitive if you don't enjoy a whole lot of beat-em-ups. She unlocks a variety of abilities and types of punches and kicks in her repertoire, and towards the end of the game it sort of challenges you to use these effectively. Also she controls pretty well. She feels sleek, athletic, and powerful. Outside of combat, not as much, but she still feels pretty responsive. (also the camera isn't that bad. It just has hiccups sometimes.) Boss Battles are generally good and fun to play, although a couple are a little irritating.
-The Memory Remixes are really, really creative. They're a little sparse, but they're very fun and cool. Play with people's memories to 'change' outcomes in real life- or so the victim thinks. Make them believe that they killed someone. Make them believe something is their fault. Make them take on a different perspective. Super unique, one of the highlights of the game.
-The soundtrack is good. Certain songs, I'd even say that they're lovely. Songs fit the situations well, no complaints.
-Very good game-feel with a PC-controller (microsoft controller or otherwise)
Cons:
-Game is kind of short, I beat it in 9 hours and I was trying to take my time for a majority of it. Unfortunately, it doesn't have much in terms of replay value other than looking for things you missed (collectables) or piecing together parts of the story you may have not initially had already
-parkour segments (climbing around) can be a bit repetitive. Also, sometimes there's a clarity issue where even when there's arrows that point to things you can climb, it's not always obvious where you have to go. I'm not talking like 'this should be blatantly obvious with a giant arrow' but more like 'did I go this way already?' or 'where's the next thing to jump to?' I got lost a few times in one of the later chapters.
-The game is EXTREMELY linear. There's not much room for exploration, which is probably why they put so much effort into putting up the floating signs and whatnot around the levels (also putting detail into them, which is nice I guess).
-Game tends to give out a few too many tutorials, which isn't so much bad as it is like 'okay, I get it thanks'
-The difficulty is more subjective than anything. I found normal to be at least a little challenging, but people who play a lot of beat-em-ups might want to start on the highest setting.
-Not so good game-feel with mouse and keyboard.
All in all, I'd say it's a 4 out of 5 or a(n) 7.5/8 out of 10. Good story, good gameplay, creative mechanics, but could have used a little more polish, and a bit more length in the game itself. The hiccups are pretty easy to forgive, in my opinion. Don't let them get in the way of a good story (that actually made me cry at the end a little, i guess that's a small spoiler).

With the new generation of consoles finally upon us people are always looking for the next-gen features in their games, which for the most part are just dumb gimmicks to trick consumers into an experience they've had a hundred times before. Whatever happened to simplicity? Simplicity is bliss and we should enjoy simpler elements without them being saturated in heavy cutscenes or hand holding. Well my friends, welcome to Paper Sorcery.
At its core it's a strategy, dungeon crawler RPG, examples of this would be the Wizardry series and to some extent Final Fantasy. You traverse dungeons, slay monsters, get loot. Simple right? It would be if there wasn't a strong skill system, character choices and loot options, yes there isn't always a X>Y when it comes to loot. While the combat may seem bare bones to the average incomprehensible fool, it's actually quite deep and for the most part well thought out for a game of this size. There is a huge variety of skills and character combinations, making every group unique and gives them a different playstyle from one another.
Now to acknowledge the elephant in the room, the art style. The game's sprites are hand-drawn, and might I say very high-res. Now while the monsters look very generic when it comes to a fantasy setting there's such a large variety of monsters it can be glanced over as you never really see the same types of monsters outside their respective blocks. Less could be said for the UI and the animations of combat which leave much to be desired as they're very simple and seem nearly uninspired when compared to all the other art assets. My favourite sections would have to be the open areas before each boss, huge rooms which boast no boundaries, allowing for some unique backdrops
So is this game perfect? No, but for $5 you're not going to get much better. The game suffers from no options menu outside resolution, which are chosen before you load the game. At least audio sliders are needed, as much as I enjoy some of the music they're very overpowering and sometimes I just like to listen to the combat sounds. Keyboard functionality is their, but it is very very lacking, clicking through menus seems sluggish and keys such as 'esc' do nothing for the most part. There are also some graphical glitches, though very minor and in no way affect the gaming experience.
For $5 this is a steal, tonnes of content and replay value. It boasts a unique artstyle using blank space which only adds to the amazingly solid RPG experience. Also, did I mention a single man made this? GGWP

Now here's the twist:  instead of playing a band of heroes out to vanquish evil, you're playing the role of an evil socerer with a band of monsters, undead, and other evil minions out on a mission to break out of an extra-dimensional prison that exists in a book.
If you played rpgs like Dragon Warrior, the combat should be very familiar. You tell your poke'monsters who to attack and what spells/abilities to use. The prison guards will do the same to you. So you beat on each other back and forth until either of you dies. Hopefully not you.
I don't know what the rest of these fools are smoking but the music is fakkin sexy. Like if Daft Punk and M83 had a one-night stand and out popped this delish little track 9 months later.
Oh yeah, and somewhere in the middle you end up working for the Reaper, returning his lost souls in exchange for a access to The Catacombs, where tasty loot and random combat encounters lie. A nice place to grind for levels and gems (gold).
The graphics are stylish monochromatic cel-shaded sexiness with just a dash of color thrown in (think MadWorld* meets Mike Mignolia's Hellboy). In short... just buy the damn game already. You could do a lot worse for $5. A *lot* worse... a lot.
*not the slit-your-wrists-and-cry-like-a-baby song by Gary Jules featured in Donnie Darko, but the awesome ultra-violent severely underrated Wii game from Sega.

The short version comes first.
Unfortuantely, I rate the game a 7/10. The campaign took ME about six hours to complete. However, I see that other people have more hours then me (some even by a large margin). I played pretty fast, and played the game on medium-hard difficulty. The game feels like the other Wolfenstien games, so if you enjoyed the past ones you will enjoy this one. Good humor, makes you feel like a bad♥♥♥♥♥ and cool weapons.
Going into more detail, I honestly felt like the game could have been worked on longer. The game felt a bit incomplete.
- Graphics: The graphics were honestly disappointing to me. They did not seem all that much better then the last games. To be clear, the graphics are not bad, but they are not good. Do not go into this game expecting great graphics.
- Story: The story was decent, at best. The ending of it was not as astounding as I wanted it to be, and it does not even come close to as good as the last one. It ends on a cliff-hanger (which, hopefully, they'll continue the story with DLC).
- Gameplay: Game felt just like any other Wolfenstein game. However, the gameplay is why I feel like this game is incomplete. Movement can be very clunky at times, falling down a shaft or off of a wall is just goddamn awful. Your character is basically floating for a good while until you walk far enough off of it. Lastly, when you are using an assault rifle with a scope, there is still bullet spread and the bullet does not go to where your scope is pointing. This made it difficult to take enemies out at longer ranges.
All in all, the game was disappointing, but not bad. I do not believe it is worth $60. I would wait until the game is on sale to buy it.

More importantly judging the game on it's own merits rather than comparing it to FIFA all the time: The gameplay is probably the best yet in any PES game but the classic problem I have encountered in previous years remains, the computer never commits fouls. In all my time on PES 16 I was awarded 1 freekick and 0 penalties and that was after playing hundreds of games and I can already tell this issue has not been addressed. Maybe it's my play style but I still think to reflect more closely a football simulation the opponent should do some rash sliding tackles, shirt pulling and body checks but this never happens. The CPU will either not tackle you at all or they will win the ball cleanly, there is no middle-ground.

Pros: Best gameplay, good graphics, natural motions, animations etc. Improved online gameplay options such as 11v11, quality immersion when playing as certain licensed teams like Liverpool at home for example
Cons: Typical annoying commentary, CPU never fouls, no budget adjustment in Master League
If I discover any of this is inaccurate I will edit accordingly, this is a fairly early review.

Yet, I find myself always drawn back to the game, always wondering what badass parkour moves I can pull off next, or by curiosity to see what the next level has in store for me. For me, the game doesn't dissapoint as running from multiple hunters can make the game seem hectic, and keep the game interesting, along with the music and the environment that the style of vector makes. Seeing the obstacles in black, and the enviroment in full, glorious colors really depicts how the main character, vector, feels. This, at least to me, really ties in with the introduction scene of vector. Being trapped and doing the same tasks on a daily basis, and only having one desire, and that is to be free! However, there are some things that really make me furious at certain times while playing Vector. At times, there will be certain animations, or scripts, that you want vector to do, yet he won't do it. I found several times that I press the up button several seconds away from the object yet he would do the animation that would prohibit me from getting a certain cube. This would then cause me to restart the level just so I can get that one damned cube so I can progess. Because of this, it gives the game a sense of trial and error that is very misleading to me, for the "challenging" aspect of this game is to remember where to exactly jump so you can get all the cubes and tricks within that certain level. However, after beating that level, I get a sense of accomplishment, and sense of pride that makes it worth while for me.
So I'm giving Vector a 7/10, to me the game is very fun, but it's fun in short bursts, delays in script triggers, and level memorization rather than an actual challenge really knocks the game back from what it actually could be.

Playing it on PC is going to be my third time through this game, all I can say is, I can't wait to play the others in the series.

You get to go around stabbin' dudes in the throat.  Sure there's more to it than that, but what else do you need, really?
How about a great story with interesting characters?  Would that entice you?  Here we have Altair, an experienced assassin who's gotten a bit too big for his britches, so the leader of his order has decided to knock him down a few pegs.  In order to get back in the good graces of his mentor and his colleagues, he has to go track down several targets by the book and get back in touch with his roots.
But not all is as it seems . . . the morality of what he is doing begins to trouble Altair as he learns that his targets seem to be doing evil but also seem to have good intentions at heart.  And signs begin to point to a larger plot threading these targets together, bigger stakes to be won.  Eventually Altair has to learn what is going on, discover who he can really trust, and find a deeper understanding of himself and his creed.
But hey, let's not downplay the throatstabbing!  And the gutstabbing!  And the knife throwing and the sword fighting and the many other ways there are to murderize your enemies.  Plenty of running around on rooftops, jumping people while their backs are turned, and escaping into the crowd before the guards crack your skull open.
There are a lot of great ideas in this game!  Of course . . .
. . . a lot of those ideas are not fully realized.  The first
very much feels like the testing ground for a lot of promising stuff, and sadly not all of it clicked right away.  Many of the missions and sub-missions are interesting at first, but lack variation, gradually becoming dull through constant repetition.  The combat can likewise become something of a chore, mostly just standing there waiting for your opponent to attack so you can counterattack, then waiting for the next opponent to attack so you can counterattack, ad nauseam.  Fast travel hadn't been introduced yet, so just getting from the central hub to any of the destination cities could take a depressingly long time.  Many of the stealth elements were handled in a very strange way . . . Altair can slowly plod around cities in full assassin regalia and a ton of weapons strapped to his bod, for example, and garner no attention whatsoever, but if he dares try to move even as fast as a somewhat brisk walk, the guards immediately sense he's up to no good and start viciously attacking.
In short, AC is dragged down somewhat by its own carefully constructed drudgery.
Now this may all sound like I went back and played this game after playing the others am thus judging it unfairly against the progress made by those that followed, but I must point out that this is not so!  I started here and have been working my way through the series in order.  These problems are all things I noticed my first time through, and I was pleasantly surprised to find afterward that the later installments fixed a lot of them.  And despite all of that . . .
. . . it's still an immensely fun game to play!  The greatness in the series overall is very easy to sense in this game because it's extremely close to the surface.  Unpolished, perhaps.  Clunky, in a way.  But still quite serviceable and attached to a very good story.  Definitely worth buying and playing.

The original AC was more of a tech demo than a proper game, but still has some good aspects that some people might desire.
+The environments are lovely, if a bit whitewashed, and the game runs buttery smooth 60FPS max settings even on my 6-year old hardware.
+Combat is MUCH harder than in the sequels; if you get cornered with 4+ guards surrounding you, you're screwed. Counterkills still exist, but the chain kills introduced in Brotherhood are not, which I like.
+This game is much more stealth-oriented than the sequels. If you alert your target, not only are they difficult to kill in a straight fight, you will very quickly get surrounded by guards and have your♥♥♥♥♥handed to you.
+You are encouraged to obtain useful information about your target and ways you can take them out, whether it's a map of patrol routes or a hiding place to jump out from. These are obtained by completing side missions (see below for why this is a bad thing).
There are quite a few problems with this game though:
-Doesn't play nice with controllers; every time you turn on the game it defaults to KB/M, so you have to go into the options menu to switch to controller every time.
-Unnecessarily convoluted game exiting. To leave you have to exit the animus, then quit. Took me too long to figure that out.
-Combat can sometimes be slow to respond which, considering how lethal fighting is and the fact that you don't have medicine to heal mid-combat, can be a death sentence.
-NO FAST CLIMBING. The godsend of AC2 over the original was being able to climb nonstop hand over hand. With AC 1, you will stop at every move, then move to the next area. Makes traversing areas painfully slow if you've played any of the other games which feature this faster climbing.
-Altair's voice is plainly American, while everyone else in the Animus has period appropriate accents. Very immersion-breaking.
-Guards sometimes detect and attack you for no apparent reason, so it's best to avoid any areas with guards entirely, or try to blend through them. This doesn't always work for some reason though.
-Very little story. Go kill these guys, then something happens at the end that sets up for AC2 (significantly better).
-PLEASE SIR, CAN YOU SPARE ANY MONEYY!?!?
Overall, if you really want to experience the series from the beginning, it does have some nice aspects, but if you've already played the others it will be very hard to go back and deal with the archaic combat and freeclimbing systems.

*Hellblade: Senua's Sacrifice*
_A third person horror adventure, set in real Nordic Mythology..!!_
Wow...!!   This game is simply put, *amazing*  I'm in awe..!!
This was my absolute wildest highlight of 2017.
Sometimes you run into one of those games, that will leave such an impact on you, they'll stay with you for many, many years. They can even redefine your very perception of what makes a game a memorable experience.
Senua's Sacrifice is one such game. At least - it is for me.
It's a truely unique story, fleshed out within a game that really works.
It makes you wonder, and ponder on how fragile but also resiliant, the human mind can be. Something no other game has done this well, ever.
It's a story about Senua, a medieval Pikt whom sets out on a quest to Hell itself, in order to save her lovers soul from the clutches of Hel. The Nordic Mythology's ruler of Hell. (Or Hella, as she is named in the game)
Senua's real battle though, is within her own mind.  She hears voices whispering to her - she sees people and events long gone and can't always trust her own perceptions of the world. She feels haunted by what she calls "The Darkness". An entity she feels is trying to consume and destroy her from within.

YOU hear and see it all too. See, you're one of those voices..  ;) She even knows you are there. But she tries to ignore you. As an example of this, whenever you turn the camera around so she'll look at you, she always turns her head away.  ;)
Constantly there are voices all around you, commenting on this and that. Screaming, begging and enticing. Sometimes all at once. It gives you a freigtening idea of what it must be like to be having a psychosis.
In fact the game was developed closely with real mental disorder experts and with people recovering from psychoses - to give you - as real an experience as possible in a game.
The graphics are made using the Unreal Engine 4.0. With beautiful landscapes, dark and gritty locales and some of the best character animation I've ever seen.
Senua moves fluently and realisticly. Especially in sword fighting combat. If you ask her to dodge an incoming blow, she'll do it immediately, even in the middle of a swing. You don't have to wait for a set animation sequence to complete.
It makes handling Senua a real pleasure. I truely loved the combat parts. Feeling the character responding amicably and fluidly. A bit like Talon in Shadow of Mordor. Senua was made using real motion caption by an excellent actress. And it really shows in the cutscenes. So much emotion was put into it..!!
And the voice acting. Oh man, it's among the best I've ever experienced.
For example: The voices in your "head" were recorded using special equipment, designed to give your brain the perfect perception of distance, movement and direction. These voices simply fly all around your head whispering and yelling.. All voice acting in this game is done to perfection. Senua, the visions, The Darkness - everything. That said, this game MUST be played using a headset.
The gameplay can be described as a somewhat normal 3rd person adventure game. You run around in various locales where you must complete puzzles, find hidden story markers and find your way through levels. Most levels have some sort of puzzle or illusion you'll have to figure out, before advancing.
There is also combat of course. Sword fighting with various Norse "ghosts" or undead. In the start it's pretty straightforward. But later on, more challenging opponents joins the fray, requiring you to develop new tactics, keeping track of the battlefield so you won't be out maneuvered and the mastering of Senua's abilities. It's not overly complicated. You have 2 different types of attack. A quick attack, and a slower more powerful one. These can be comboed and will reward you with a critical strike if done properly. You can also evade or parry. But that's it. I completed the game without ever using the parry skill..   Still, I found the combat sequences extremely satisfying. Simple but challenging. Especially when you have 6+ opponents circling around you. Oh yeah, there's a melee attack as well. It comes in pretty handy at times..  ;)
The boss fights, and there are a few, can be pretty hard though.
And you don't want to screw up too much. Senua is infected by "The Rot". And every time you fail, it will grow upwards on her arm. And when it reaches her head - it's game over. Permanently..!!
I completed the game in my first try though, so it's still possible.
Conclusion.  If you love a good adventure game, and to immerse yourself in a truely epic, but also extremely dark story - this game is a *must* for you.
Especially if you're interested in the Nordic Mythology. There's a lot of lore and storytelling about it in this game. Most of it, pretty accurate too.
I'll give it s 9.5 out of 10 score. The only thing keeping it from a 10, is that it's rather short. I completed it in 9 hours. And I really wanted a bit more.
In all fairness. Extending the story further, might also have been a bad thing.
It was nicely balanced as it were. But I still would've wanted a little more out of it.

Would I recommend this game?  Long story short... no.  Right now I've put 20 hours in and with some side-questing just beat the game.
For $60USD you get i.e. what I liked about this game:
1)  Really great voice acting
2)  Excessively wild cutscenes
3)  Touching character development
4)  Some really pretty graphics (when you get the settings just right)
5)  A resolution to that situation in 2014 where you wondered "I respect the decision to end the game this way but just how are they going to cash in on a sequel now?"
What I didn't like dropping $60USD for:
1)  Frustrating difficulty spikes in the early game
2)  Action that was kinda flavorless
3)  Adventure that was held hostage in very small levels
4)  Graphics with issues
5)  About 7 hours of actual gameplay
6)  Over 12 hours of side quests through old areas
7)  Lots of cutscenes that broke up the gameplay mid gameplay
8)  Gameplay in and out of combat was actually less involved than in the last game
9)  An end that came so abruptly I was waiting for the credits to end and the third act to get on with it
So in a little more detail?
The action (as in Action/Adventure) was boring most of the time.  The path of least resistance to solving most fights was to get behind something and keep shooting Nazis until the commanders called for backup and then shoot the backup and then shoot the commanders when they were all that was left.  This worked maybe 95% of the time and it wasn't very fun.  I didn't have much choice in doing anything else because the moment I was discovered it was like every single Nazi in the area was supposed to know where I was, then a mob would instantly organize and telepathically coordinate each member's most effecient route to my current location.   Its not like bullets don't hurt them, there's just always so many of them all shooting you from everywhere all at once and in a weird turn of events it feels like I'm the one with storm trooper accuracy.  And is it me or were there more guns in the last game?  Plus the new dual weilding is cumbersome.
The adventure was almost nonexistant, the levels are just so small and compartmentalized (yet I still got lost in the delopadated buildings) that there isn't much there.  I never felt like I actually went anywhere, I just went from one area that was just big enough to hold a football field or two through some connecting passages to another similarly sized area.  Just every area was either a big areana or multi-level building with lines of sight from floor to floor that was in a big areana.  The map was barely servicable and I usually spent fifteen minutes trying to find where the invisible walls ended and where I was supposed to go.  It was never natural, nothing like "go up" that you could just intuit; ok there was a train level where "go forward" was the theme.  Even similar levels in Doom (2016 and OG) that are "linear mazes" aren't this hard to navigate or even memorize your first time through.
Playing on very hard the difficulty spiked so horribly in the Penthouse and Courthouse levels that even after dropping the difficulty down to hard and then medium the experience left me so angry I couldn't take anymore and just went to bed.  Like 20 minutes (minus cutscenes) before the Penthouse level I flat out exploded a three story tall ultra death robot with maybe seven~eight blasts with the laser cannon from Wolf2014, then waltzed through waves of Nazis with un-upgraded weapons on the way up to the Penthouse without getting myself killed once... then I hit a wall and just can't beat the Penthouse because its so hard.  Same story for the courthouse.  Maybe it had something to do with the incredible number of enemies, how they always knew where I was, the lack of reliable cover, how difficult it is to pick up armor; its just a total orthoganal experience to what the last game offered.
Lots of folks have said they had major bugs.  I will say that I didn't have any major bugs and I was running this game under the absolute most ideal circumstances:  With an entire system made out of brand new top of the line hardware that previously had only been turned on for a few hours (long enough to download/install drivers/updates then play Far Cry 3 Blood Dragon while Wolf2 downloaded in the background).  And even then this game that made a marketing/selling point that it was all about being played at 4K it ran on my new rig at 4K at 60fps on ultra settings... and had the weirdest out of control screen tearing that I have ever seen.  I mean screen tearing when there are no frame rate issues and the resolution was to step the resolution back just a little bit so it wasn't 4K, then problem solved.  Also turning all the settings up to max made the picture really ugly, turning things down a little removed this weird crawling vaseline effect on the screen and the strange blurring filter that dynamically blasted the detail out of everything... plus the game loaded higher quality textures (you don't have the option to set textures youself) at that point and it stopped looking like garbage.
I am so dissapoint.  If I could tell past me to pass on this game I really would.

[Gameplay]
The game is fast paced and Fun, you have a lot of control of how your team plays by messing with the tactics and of course Advanced Tactics which allow for more indepth play. E.g. Hate your defence leaving you exposed on the counter? Pull your defensive line back or use Deep Defensive line or even just tell 2 of your defenders to always stay back. Hate your striker getting tired from tracking back? Make him stay up. There is so much you can do.
[MyClub]
I missed last year of any Clubs mode because I just got bored of Fifa's handicap and I got PES 2017 too late in the year that there was no point. 2018 Is great fun however, the servers are impeccable and I have had no issues (1 minute is the longest I've waited but no lag at all).
The best thing about MyClub is the Rewards and Challenges that get you Club Coins and GP that you can spend on Ball's without having to waste money or unreal amounts of time. [Other Modes]

[Licenses]
There's already a save file you can import to change team's and leagues and I expect modders to add in the Scoreboards and Presentation if you want it in the near future.
[Referee's]
My biggest complaint of 2017 was the awful decisions by ref's (Probably caused by being a 360/PS3 port) but there's none of that anymore, they have all been spot on so far.
[Graphics]
Proper PC Version with proper PC settings. 10/10

The best Football game this year by far, fluid, fun and just does everything right. 10/10

Caster is a perfect metaphor for the gaming industry as of writing this review. Caster represents an awesome idea that actually works and has only one real flaw with it, and that's how it's just too easy (Even so, that's eay to fix.) However, because of its unique style, it will not truly achieve the praise it needs. It's also unfortunate that the game has been essentially discontinued. That doesn't mean the community can't take it up on their own to continue it.
Caster doesn't truly fit into the predefined genres we have today, the closest similar game would be Borderlands. It's definitely a shooting game, and also has some RPG elements. I guess we can call it an FPRPS (First Person Role-Playing Shooter.) It's third-person perspective and simple graphics also gives it that PS1/Arcade feel to it, and it's definitely appealing. Plus it easily gets 60+ fps on even the most burnt potato out there, so anyone can enjoy it.
There isn't much to the story, but the story that is there is enough... barely. All you're truly given is a name to the main enemies and some minor exposition. Basically, not a lot of text boxes.
This is where Caster truly does shine. To start off, your character has free roam over wherever you are. As such you are given the ability to dash and super jump (which is a powerful double jump) to enhance the fun of it. With the base dash and jump, you're not moving very far or going very high, but as you upgrade you become more epic. Eventually you'll be dashing for longer distances, running on water, and even running on walls. I'll be damned if I could find another game that makes wall-running and shooting both fun and easy.
When you start off, you'll only have your basic shooting "ability" "Pulse." It's not very strong starting out looking and behaving very similar to Mega Man's basic attack. It needs to be upgraded to become even better. Missions are where you earn the credits to upgrade this ability. And as you do more missions you'll gain access to more abilities, each with their unique-ness.
Environment interaction. For a game off this size, it's incredible to have environments that are fully interactable. A lot of things can cause craters to form, from both you and enemies. If you super jump and fall long enough, you can leave a small crater and create a shockwave. Your basic shots can build craters too.
There's even one instance where enemies will try to stay underground and take pot shots at you.
Enemies, however, is the only true point where the game doesn't shine. The enemies in Caster are way too easy. Upgrades for abilities just do massive amounts of damage, and enemies don't get adjusted for this in each level as you progress. Eventually, even on hard, you'll get to a point where you're just like: "That's cool, and now it's dead. Next level." It's a damn shame too, because adaptive enemies would pad out the gameplay much better than spreading them out. Too bad that'll never be fixed :c
Sonic the Hedgehog + Mega Man + Borderlands - Difficult AI = Caster
While I'm not truly a "Modder" (At the time of writing, at least) Caster looks way more than simple to mod. There is mod support from what I can tell at the time of writing this. I would also wager that this game would be a perfect start for getting into modding, as it's so simple and open to the idea of community-created content. Hell, why stop at making single-player campaigns? You could probably add some sort of multiplayer to this game easier than any other indie game on Steam. This might be where the game has a future, and it would be up to the community.

Just finished the game, and I honestly think it's one of the most, if not THE most, underrated beat'em-up style game I've ever seen. Personally, I am not a fan of games where "you just press a couple buttons a bunch of times and eventually the bad guys will die" - even ones that have combos and stuff. But this game totally broke that barrier and left me wanting more after each play session. From the amazing story, to the intense music, to the awesome voice-acting, to the easy but fun combat system - it was just such a refreshment to see such a game do what it did the way it did. DONTNOD really pulled out all the stops with this one - and it was only their first game! I would like to note that this game is incredibly linear - so if you don't like being told exactly where to go and what to do, except for the bonus collectables you can get when you stray from the beaten path, it's possible that this game isn't for you. But I personally enjoyed this game a ton and will certainly be replaying it for Achievments later on - and I will definately be on the edge of my seat, waiting for what DONTNOD has in store for us in the future.
The art style is amazing, the writing is awesome, the music is super futuristic and crazy, the combat system is really fun and intuitive, and all of this comes together to keep you really engaged in what your doing. Some negatives I have for this game include the constant feeling that you're being herded in one direction by the game, the some combat CAN get kind of repetitive and dull, especially during Boss fights.
One tip I'd have for you if you plan to play this game is to use a controller. It doesn't matter what controller, as long as you don't use Keyboard + Mouse. This makes it WAY less confusing, especially since this game was made assuming the player is using a controller.

I wish I could recommend this game. It is beautiful and insightful on many fronts, the story is engaging and has the potential to be quite deep, and the combat mechanics are flashed with inspiration. There is an optional puzzle element of visual recognition ("where is this?") and path-finding ("how do I get there?") that increases in difficulty as the game goes on.
The game-defining memory-editing segments are not as puzzle-oriented, but they move the story along well and it is viscerally fun to find new ways to mess someone's memory to the point of mental breakdown. If you like to explore to every dead-end, this part of the game is engaging but far too short.
Two thirds of the way through, however, the combat becomes an exericse in player stamina. The combats lag on until I found them far too much of a grind to complete the game. I ended up watching a play-through of the game, and the story's conclusion is fitting for the rest of the story, but the pacing of combat simply broke me out of any flow and then out of any desire to continue.
Sorry, Don't Nod. Maybe if you made a Telltale-like game featuring a similar roundabout-change-things mechanic as Remember Me's memory-edits. Maybe a young and innocent time-traveller? I would play it!

This is a runner, not really a speed runner, but an obstacle parcours runner. It is pretty entertaining, WHEN the character does what you want him to.
You will only press 3 buttons in this game: up for jumping, down for sliding and right for accellerating (at certain points in the level, though that gimmick is totally superflous and you could just auto accellerate...).
Your goal is to reach the end of the level. You are always being chased by a hunter, who is exactly as fast as you are, so if you mess up too much, bye bye. You can also collect bonus points and money as well as do tricks at certain points in the level. Collecting all bonus points often means taking a different and longer route than the hunter, which makes for extra excitement. If you die, you start from the beginning, no check points. Doing the tricks simply means pushing "up" whenever you are DIRECTLY (mother♥♥♥♥ing directly) at the trick point, not a split second too early or too late or you miss it...and this is where I have my first gripe with the game. Pressing the button in exactly the right time is not easy. It's like a QTE. Of course, this is a mobile port, so yadda yadda, BUT the controls are sometimes a bit weird and of course, how you jumped an obstacle just before another obstacle can also mean the difference between success and failure, so it's not just getting across obstacles, it is also importand HOW you do that. There's regular jumping on the obstacle, then somewhat clumsily roll over it or slide or hop like a pro. That all is determined by WHEN you press the jump button and it gets kind of tricky and a bit unresponsive imho. So, the controls could be better and maybe also more diverse.
My second gripe is also with the tricks. In order to do them you have to UNLOCK them...wtf. That means spending cash in ever increasing numbers. You only get cash by completing levels and you will most likely have to do levels multiple times to earn more cash to unlock all the tricks. Do you need those tricks in order to complete the level? According to the game, yes (it says so on the level screen), but really no. You can complete a level without a trick just as well, you just can't get the three star rating. Still this is a stupid idea for a PC game. The same goes for the gadets. You can buy those for currency as well, but apparently they are one time use only...so ♥♥♥♥ you. That being said, I have only unlocked one gadget for now, but still I can only imagine that it will be the same for the others (this one lets you get away from a nearby hunter...but for 400 currency and 1 time use...that is just a ripoff and means replaying the levels even more often to get enough cash. I can possibly understand it for mobile if the app is free and then you offer ♥♥♥♥ing micro transactions for money, but...nah...it is annoying.
The graphics are minimal, but that is ok. The foreground is black, the characters are black and the backdrop is a static image of one of the three different levels. The only issue here are frame rate drops that occur occasionally.
Getting to the end of a level is a challenge in and of itself in the later stages, but getting all three stars is even harder.
Third and final gripe: In order to unlock the other levels you have to earn a certain amount of stars. Like gripe number 2 this is a mobile idea. Gating content behind possible pay or skill walls. I beat the god damn level, so let me continue with the rest of the
Well, thanks.
That's the same♥♥♥♥♥♥Trackmania does with its "get gold on all levels to unlock these levels"...Just let me play them and keep the hardcore stuff for the completionists...no one will cry a river.
Conclusion: I bought this on sale and it has a lot of content and the game play is enticing if minimalistic. There is quite a bit of content in it, so you can give it a try if it is reduced in price I'd say.
Instead of just doing a mobile port, however, this could have been made into a really solid experience with a solid graphics engine that does not have any framerate drops like this one. Possibly include a few more diverse levels and most of all get rid of the pay♥♥♥♥♥♥ Then there could have also been more active gameplay elements. Jumping and sliding are ok, but you could also include real QTEs for the tricks and make them mandatory but also offer the chance to complete the level if you fail them. And make gadgets meaningful choices instead of yet another money sink...
This game could have been so much more than it is, but maybe the money will go into a proper "sequel"...

Vector is a trial-and-error timing game. There's no strategy, no skill, and barely any gameplay involved.
What little gameplay does exist consists of restarting levels over and over and over until you figure out (memorize) the right timing for a sequence of button presses you need to hit to finish a level and move onto the next. Wash, rinse, repeat.
Another frustrating point is that the camera is too zoomed-in on the action, obscuring what's coming next, preventing you from being able to plan your moves, and essentially forcing you to fail in order to progress.
Vector is probably a decent mobile game to play in short bursts on the toilet, but as a PC port it's pretty terrible.
