Caster is an average third person shooter that does not contain any notable qualities, aside from the ability to destroy terrain and perform ridiculous map-crossing leaps.
Your objective in each level is to either kill every enemy or do a generic fetch quest (there are a few other missions with different objectives but they're uninteresting, for example; shoot a tree). Every level is incredibly short, and even on my first time, each one averaged no longer than a minute. Speaking of game length, the entire thing isn't longer than an hour. The game abruptly ends with a "To Be Continued...", and despite being released in 2009, there has been no continuation, and it seems the website does not hint at anything of the sort either.
Enemies are all very generic, and each one of their attacks can be easily avoided by just sprinting around or jumping. Even if they do manage to hit you, they deal hardly any damage, and they are easily dispatched; even more so with the weapon upgrades.
The story is uninspired, and unless you've never heard or seen the "It's humans against aliens, you're our only hope!" plot, then I doubt you'll be interested. As I stated earlier, the game ends at a very unexpected random point with sequel bait.
A map editor is available, but I did not use it or download custom maps, so I cannot comment on that.
I did not find Caster to be particularly interesting in any way. Terrain destruction and super speed can be fun and worth it if you paid 0.14 cents, but beyond that, there's not much else that the game offers.

An FPS game that has stood the test of time. CoD 4 has proven that what really makes a multiplayer game such as this great is the dedicated servers--and the admins that run it. To give a specific example, the FF (Fatal Forces) servers have been around for years and still have a many dedicated admins and a large playerbase. There are even servers with different player made game modes, most notable being zombie survival.
This game is also a better example of what a first person shooter should be than the later CoDs. There are less gimmicks and ridiculous exploits (like quickscoping or commando knifing) while still having mechanics like C4 traps (and knifing but without the commando perk) that can still liven and diversify the gameplay. The killstreaks are not overpowered, making it more difficult for a single player to dominate the game (especially if they are hacking) and consequently putting more emphasis on gun firefights and teamwork.
So if you are ever going to buy a Call of Duty game, this is the only one you will ever need.

I'll start by saying that I picked this game up, just after launch, on the Playstation 4. I later picked this up on Steam, I think around the time Pathfinder Update came out.
Now, on launch, this game was basically a shell of what Shaun Murray promised. Many people, like myself, felt cheated and lied to. It was a $40 game at most, and barely at that. Now, the rest of this review is based on the gameplay after the Atlas Rises update. If you played this game on launch and stopped shortly after, this game is much different now. There are new world types, galaxy map is improved, Space Stations tend to have more than one type of alien species on it (making the 3 main races feel more interwoven and actually interacting with one another. There is a series of missions with a story to it, giving you a sense of purpose to fulfil while exploring. There are also guilds that offer simple jobs for credits, items, or even blueprints. The Freighters not only allow you to build a base on-the-go, but actually offers further reach during warps. Space combat is improved. There have been times that friendly space ships actually help attack pirates that are attacking me.
This game is getting closer to what Shaun failed to deliver a year ago. Just goes to show that, yes, this game was released a year too early. It's at a point now that, if it was released today, I'd feel it is likely worth the full $60 pricetag. Still, I'd recommend getting it on sale if you can. Yo I have never written a review on Steam before, but I loved The New Order so much I feel compelled. I'm gonna keep this point form - concise rather than eloquent.
I'm running this on a bare-bones mini-ITX rig Pentium G4560/1050 Ti (gimme a break the thing cost a dime and is great) and I get perfectly acceptable performance on high/ultra (50-60fps dips into low 40s in big open areas, of which there are hardly any but get to that later...)
This game, while fun at times, is markedly inferior to its predecessor.
As has been noted in many other review the stealth element isn't really there anymore. This is a real shame as The New Order had a fanastically implemented and incredibly seamless stealth component - it gave you options and made the whole experience that much more engaging. Here whenever I saw the indicators for two commmanders I just thought yep I'mma stealth one fight through 20 other guys (some of which seem to spawn in impossible places due to the inevitably triggered alarm) and then scrub the other commander guy. It's a drag. You can stealth successfully sometimes but it feels more like getting lucky than the game being designed to accommodate it.
Shooting feels good. Movement feels good. Some weapons are utterly redundant (machinepistole anyone? didn't think so).
I'm of the mind the levels looks great but it is very much a corridor shooter, moreso that the New Order which was full of more open-ended environments to wage war in. There are some combat bowls but you will generally bringing Nazis to their bitter end in variety of hallways.
Feedback from damage is sucks. The cues to show that you are taking damage or are on low health are very weak - this makes health management and knowing when to run significantly less intuitive, especially as the firefights can become hectic on higher difficulties.
It was this and the lack of flexibility with the stealth that made the game a punish for me to play at times. Higher difficulties can make be quite frustrating as I'm taken out almost instantly by a black outline (enemy designs are not particularly inspired) of a Nazi with very little indication that I've even taken a hit, let alone what direction it's coming from. The flow of combat that defined Machinegames first Wolfenstein effort is only found her intermittently, the engagements lacking the coherance and freedom that The New Order had in spades.
Story is utterly fantastic b-grade pulp. Cutscenes made me feel giddy - really cannot speak highly enough. FANTASTIC voice acting and writing. It's a schlocky wonder. I only half-enjoyed the accompanying game though.
If you can handle playing with a controller, rent or borrow on a console or buy it/finish it/sell it. On PC I'd wait for a sale. It can still be fun but definite sopomore syndrome at play here.

You'll be running expecting a cute little jump scare, then they throw a monster at you and it genuinely creeps you out, then you feel badc afterwards because its like "why was I scared by this?"
Haha. Great game, but not a whole lot of different content, as the begtinning is kinda slow, but as you progress, it gets more fun.

The game begins fairly cute, and then slowly intoduces some little jump scares in the way of cardboard cut outs springing from the walls. The first one happens and you tell yourself, "Okay, this isn't so bad. II may get startled depending on where they happen but I can make it through these jump scares."
And then nothing happens for a while. And you begin to wonder if your'e walking in circles. But no, that room looks a little different than the one you're thinking of, right? And there's a painting here you don't remember.
And then you find the first note, from a person in a very similar predictament to your own. And you get that brief moment of rest, but the room goes down a la Cube, descending to a level with less cute and more creepy.
And then it starts following you. There's got to be a weapon somewhere, right? The game began with a controls list, and using a weapon was on that list. But where, where the weapons, and what can you do in this dark maze over a pit to escape that grasping hand?
I forced myself to the 100th room for the next save, in case I develop the courage to return. Some judgements, roughly half an hour in:
Atmosphere: Great. At first my eyes were unhappy, but they often are in first person games. They got used to the style and eventually quite liked it.
Scares: Plenty, I'm guessing. At 100 rooms of 1000 I've only seen the upper crust of the spooks, reading the notes and running from the thing.
Sound: Simple, works well for the game.
Overall: Recommended, if you enjoy scares and/or don't mind feeling like a giant pansy for being scared of a cutesy game.

I got this game as a bonus for a Humble Bundle so from my perspective it was essentially free.  That being said I feel like I overpayed.
Do you like button mashing?  Do like linear gameplay? Do you like absurdly frustrating boss fights that result in you uninstalling the game (I can't be the only one).  If so this game may be for you.
Aesthetically speaking I like it. The visuals are gritty and twisted, the style is mostly contigous. The story leading up to the first boss was definitely intriguing, the concept has potential. This however is the unrealized version of these things.
The combat is in fact dreadful. Yes you can technically "craft your own combos" but what that really entails is struggling through an undescribed, unintuitive interface to select between different versions of the same thing, the only thing that really matters is that you can consistently hit the dodge button. This part was somewhat expected and so I was starting to overlook how tedious and unfulfilling the combat was, I mean hell I was on a role.  Then it happened...
So I alluded to it previously but when you are building your combos in the interface different buttons map to different moves.  You don't get a legend or explanation for which button is which move however and in fact they are represented by these little symbols.  Meh, after getting your face eaten a few times you can manage to pull off one of the two combos you've created and then repeat until the battle is over.  Then you get to the boss, suddenly the tone changes from futuristic memory thieves to what might as well be wrestling, it's that over the top.  At first you even get to follow the same lack luster combat techniques used for previous encounters and then suddenly ... horribly ... in order to proceed ... you must respond to quick time events (okay you're saying, that's not the end of the world) but instead of the events being dictated with something you could recognize they are instead flashed on the screen as the cryptic symbols from the combo configuration screen.  So basically you have a fraction of a second to attempt to correlate that little symbol with one of the buttons on whatever device you may be controlling the game with, good luck.
♥♥♥♥ this, ♥♥♥♥ them, ♥♥♥♥ quick time in general, but especially ♥♥♥♥ this cryptic♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t quick time that demands you memorize their little crappy symbols and how they map out.

There was a time where you had to go watch videos in order to learn fighting games. Somehow, Lab Zero (or all studios involved in the making of the game) decided to take the "here's our Training Room, deal with it" style of welcoming new players to the genre.
Skullgirls features one of the best tutorials for any fighting game to date. In fact, it is the pioneer when it comes to actual excellent training modes, something that is included in Killer Instinct and Guilty Gear Xrd. If you find Street Fighter, Injustice or Mortal Kombat a little too intimidating or don't own an Xbox One or Windows 10, Skullgirls is a perfect alternative to Killer Instinct for newcomers to the genre. You basically learn the ropes of the genre by discovering terms like mix-ups, tick throws and all that kind of stuff. The game does let you learn the little details and nuances by doing the practices as much as you want with its incredible selection of lessons from movement to defense before going into offense.
You can even set the Training Room in order to learn the hitboxes, frame data and combos. The Tutorial also allows you to learn character-specific movesets, technically special moves, for the content that you own. If you ever see this game on sale, you owe it to yourself to give it a shot. Maybe you'll discover why fighting games are more nuanced than they look. Maybe this will be the game that will make you good at it... like actually good instead of just pressing buttons.
At a sale, the Training Mode is worth its asking price alone. The character designs and animations are great as well, Ms. Fortune being my favorite for some reason. And the soundtrack is wonderful! Skullgirls will give you the tools right off the bat and probably make you a slightly more experienced fighthing game player unlike others who are stepping into the genre by playing the more-known-yet-not-great-at-teaching titles.

Stash is a very intriguing game, It has aspects that I find both familiar and foreign, as well as downright awesome, but also odd and possibly annoying. I enjoy the fact that it's turn-based as well as click to move with the game itself plotting a path to where you want to go. Negative: sometimes the paths take you through locations that prompt you whether you want to enter or not. I find that a little annoying. I wish the pathing would take you around the location and/or not trigger the prompt unless I had specifically clicked on it.
I really enjoy combat. It has a really old-school video game feel to it. I played a game a long time ago on a Sega Genesis that was similar. Grid areas, turn based, etc. There is also a very noticeable difference in combat between the classes offered and how you have to approach encounters. I like that a lot. 4 classes and every one of them is genuinely different.
Overall I like the game. I really enjoy the company as well. Frogdice games are something I have been playing for ~20 years. They have a tendency towards "subtle depth" in their games. They don't beat you over the head with the lore. They let you uncover it - and I have a distinct feeling that same approach is included in this game as well.
I would recommend this game to anyone that enjoys spending hours and hours at their computers. It would be great for people who are looking something to do in the background that they can walk away from without worry that they're losing something.
The community also seems very helpful. Any questions I've had has been answered rather quickly. Something not always found in a game.

I paid 14 cents for this game so my expectations were extremely low, I figured if I got 10 minutes of gameplay I got my money's worth.
What I ended up getting was a delightful Sonic the Hedgehog/Megaman hybrid, in a 3D 3rd person setting that harkens back to the N64 PSX days when 2D platformers were first experimenting with the 3D style, except Caster's mechanics work fine.  You go from level to level, which for most of it is a choice as to which level you take on.  Each level has different objectives, there are about 3-4 different styles each with the occasional story sequence thrown in.  There are plenty of weapons to choose from, my favorite is the seeker, you probably should upgrade that first among the other weapons.
Performance wise I haven't ran into any issues, this game despite being made in 2010 knows I have a 144hz monitor and caps at 144 fps.  Major credit for that.  You would think this game would be great for a controller, but on default settings the camera control on the right stick is all messed up, best to just stick with the keyboard and mouse for this one.
In conclusion, for 14 cents it's a no brainer, buy this game.  It's regular price is $3.00 I really don't think that is asking for too much for this game either.  Plus this game supports modding so it's worth it just for that.  I should also mention that the soundtrack is pretty awesome too and is worth the money alone.
For the low price, and for what it is, with the inclusion of mod support, I give this game a 4 out of 5.

I had played this game a few years back, but now decided to give it another shot. It can certainly still compete with today's games, especially from a graphics standpoint, which is, in itself, quite remarkable.
If you have never played this game, I would call it a merger between Splinter Cell, Batman and Hitman. You have to blend into your environment and hide at times, you have to navigate rooftops, you can be a vigilante, and you have your mission to complete and have a certain freedom on how to do so. While this game is certainly not as refined as its successors in the series, it was, much like the first Splinter Cell, the first Batman (Arkham series), and the first Hitman, a diamond in the rough, with exceptional gameplay, graphics and design. At least for their respective times. While the subsequent titles had a lot of refinement and improvement, this first Assassin's Creed still stands its ground in the sands of time. Add to that the soundtrack, and you have great entertainment.
The only downside - to me - is the obvious console breeding ground, and the somewhat shady save point situation, but I guess that's the way it is. I'm getting used to the whole checkpoint idea these days, albeit with a heavy heart. I do miss my quick save option.
Either way, give this game a try, especially if you can snap it up in a deal! You won't regret it if you like the other games mentioned above. Also, it's not as repetitive as people say; while the handling is, true, the way you approach diverse challenges isn't.

I got this game as a bonus for a Humble Bundle so from my perspective it was essentially free.  That being said I feel like I overpayed.
Do you like button mashing?  Do like linear gameplay? Do you like absurdly frustrating boss fights that result in you uninstalling the game (I can't be the only one).  If so this game may be for you.
Aesthetically speaking I like it. The visuals are gritty and twisted, the style is mostly contigous. The story leading up to the first boss was definitely intriguing, the concept has potential. This however is the unrealized version of these things.
The combat is in fact dreadful. Yes you can technically "craft your own combos" but what that really entails is struggling through an undescribed, unintuitive interface to select between different versions of the same thing, the only thing that really matters is that you can consistently hit the dodge button. This part was somewhat expected and so I was starting to overlook how tedious and unfulfilling the combat was, I mean hell I was on a role.  Then it happened...
So I alluded to it previously but when you are building your combos in the interface different buttons map to different moves.  You don't get a legend or explanation for which button is which move however and in fact they are represented by these little symbols.  Meh, after getting your face eaten a few times you can manage to pull off one of the two combos you've created and then repeat until the battle is over.  Then you get to the boss, suddenly the tone changes from futuristic memory thieves to what might as well be wrestling, it's that over the top.  At first you even get to follow the same lack luster combat techniques used for previous encounters and then suddenly ... horribly ... in order to proceed ... you must respond to quick time events (okay you're saying, that's not the end of the world) but instead of the events being dictated with something you could recognize they are instead flashed on the screen as the cryptic symbols from the combo configuration screen.  So basically you have a fraction of a second to attempt to correlate that little symbol with one of the buttons on whatever device you may be controlling the game with, good luck.
♥♥♥♥ this, ♥♥♥♥ them, ♥♥♥♥ quick time in general, but especially ♥♥♥♥ this cryptic♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t quick time that demands you memorize their little crappy symbols and how they map out.

The most letdown game this year.
Apart from crashing problems, the game itself is rubbish as well. The shooting with the rifle feels so bad, you can feel some bullet impact in the first round when it hits the target but not for the rest of the rounds and the bullets don't tear the enermies apart so often. Also the enermies just suddenly lie down on the ground when they are killed, it feels like they are anesthetised instead of pierced by a sharp, fast-traveling object.
However, things won't get better if you choose to use weapons other than the rifle. The shotgun is only for CQB and light armoured targets, it cannot even kill a medium armoured infantry target 5m away within 3 rounds (maybe due to my difficulty) while two headshots from the rifle definitely kill all kinds of infantry unit except supersoldiers. The submachine gun is similar, it feels great at first til I find that it took me 30 rounds to kill an medium armoured soldier 1 metre away from me, then I never used that.
Weapon switching system is awful too, maybe they wanted to make it like what's in the DOOM which is a masterpiece, but they took away the time slowing effect when switching guns. What's more, you can't use mouse wheel anymore but only pressing v on the keyboard and using your mouse to point at the weapon you want, making it a terrible disaster coz one single enermy soldier can shoot you dead within 3 seconds while you are still holding your slienced pistol.
The most terrible thing is the style of the gameplay, comparing with Wolfenstein New Order the weapons used by both you and your enermies are significantly enhanced in damage, which means you have to be very careful and try not to get flanked. This somehow advocates players to eliminate most targets from afar and end the rest of them swiftly. However this clearly is not wolfenstein style but more like COD or BF. In wolfenstein you enjoy the fun when slaughter those cruel Nazis and make them run from you for their lives, but in this game you are almost 50 to 50 when faced with one Nazis soldier (in hard or higher diificulty) and the only thing differs is that you are better in accuracy when shooting at each other. This is not the BJ I want and not the wolfenstein I expected.
Finally, some small elements are not pretty good in this game such as those weak supersolders and weak heavy weapons. I cannot find any reason to use heavy weapons, laser requires charging, heavy shotgun is almost a joke, the other two one are good but that doesn't make up the drawback that they decrease your movement speed. Supersoldier are rubbish and no wonder why *********************(not to spoil).
Some say the graphic and stories are great, I dont deny that but if the most essential and fundemental elements are not satisfying enough I cannot say I recommend this game.

I really enjoy this game. I expected a load of garbage based off how low the price was (+sale was only 14 cents!), but I found myself having a really good time. I love games like Crackdown and Saint's Row 4 that allow you to fly, run, and jump at incredible speeds. Caster is just like that, but then again, it's not. The game feels (and looks) like it was a test run for the developer. There's no real story, graphics look like a cross-breed of N64 and PS1, and the levels are small and have almost nothing of interest in them. However, the physics in this game were very interesting. Certain attacks did certain things, like leveling the ground or erecting it. You're attacks can also "heal" trees, which I thought was pretty nifty. The enemies are creepy, and (even though they were nearly barren) the maps were fun to explore. I spent the first maybe ten minutes of the game just messing around with the physics, jumping and running around, shooting holes into the ground, just having a fun little time. I hope the devs make something out of this game (or finish/update it), I honestly love it. For 14 cents, yeah, I do recommend this game. However, for five bucks? Maybe not. Basically, if you're lucky enough to see this "review" before the sale ends, what's spending/blowing 14 cents? It's not going to harm you. (At least, I hope it doesn't.) So why not check this little gem out? And hey, if you end up loathing the game, you can just sell the card drops for a profit. It's a win/win. So whatta ya say?

A game designed by gamers who are devoted to their craft. This game has so many great things going for it and it's still in Beta!
The Devs and community are easily the best part of this game. They genuinely care about their players and community and go above and beyond with the amount of time they actually spend interacting with them. Every player has a voice when it comes to content or improvements in the game and can post them freely on the Frogdice forums or discuss with the devs using the in-game chat. Updates are pushed out weekly and most offer new content, bug fixes, and new systems as requested by players. The devs also change what content is prioritized by community suggestions and requests. This just adds to the awesome gameplay and content by giving each player direct access to those in control. No other game I have every played has gone this far in terms of customer service and attention to their community.
The game itself is bright and colorful and has delightfully inspired creatures that invoke a sense of nostalgia for older RPG's while still bringing a new and fun approach to the genre. The tile based combat system is a nice touch that offers lots of tactical options and a fun way to play with other players.
The crafting system still needs some work but what is already in place is a great system that is easy to get lost in and spend time crafting out gear for yourself and friends. The newspaper system for buying and selling is easy to use once you get a few upgrades out of the way and offers pletty of options for getting what you need to advance your craft.
All in all the game has a great learning curve and will keep you coming back for more. As the content gets pushed out by the Devs it will only get better and better.
edit: 2000+ hours and I still love this game.  I still haven't played through all the content and there is still lots to do.

I would describe Ninja Smasher as metroidvania-lite. You collect hidden powerups, defeat bosses, and gain new skills abilities (double jump, wall climb, etc.) as you advance through the game. However, the game is constructed in such a way that progress is quick and the next (or last) save point is never far because it is also a mobile game. As a result, it has the hallmarks of a metroidvania, but it has a much more arcade-y feel.
You can expect to get about 3 hours out of the game for the first playthrough, but completing your first run unlocks three new heroes with different mechanics from the main character. If you really like the game play, I imagine you could squeeze another few hours out of these bonus heroes.
The sound effects and music could be implemented better. If the game chose randomly between a few different sword strike sounds and had unique sound effects for secondary weapon hits, it would go a long way to reducing the monotony. Better transitions between areas and more varied tracks would help on the music side.
Overall, I'm impressed. Most of the games I get on Steam for $5 dollars are underwhelming, even at that price point, but playing Ninja Smasher has me hoping the developer finds some success. There is a lot of potential here and I'd be happy to buy a full-fledged metroidvania from Q-Cumber Factory!

Considering the Zoo Tycoon franchise seems to be done making new games, this is a great alternative if you're looking for a zoo sim that has updated graphics in comparison. It has about the same management design, although the range of available animals are smaller than ZT.
In comparison to ZT, they actually add a mechanic missing from that series that makes sense: climate controls. For example, if your zoo is a cold tundra, rather than simply placing some savannah grass for an African animal, you also need a heater to keep them warm, or they'll probably freeze to death.
As a possible con for some people, if you're like me in sometimes wanting to make a sandbox game to just make your animals breed into a huge colony, you're going to be disappinted here. Each species has a maximum number of animals you can have in their exhibit before they stop breeding. Beyond that, there's a maximum number of animals you can have in your park period before ALL of the animals stop breeding entirely regardless.
Overall, I recommend this if you're looking for a graphics update to the Zoo Tycoon series while having similar game mechanics.

I'll start by saying that I picked this game up, just after launch, on the Playstation 4. I later picked this up on Steam, I think around the time Pathfinder Update came out.
Now, on launch, this game was basically a shell of what Shaun Murray promised. Many people, like myself, felt cheated and lied to. It was a $40 game at most, and barely at that. Now, the rest of this review is based on the gameplay after the Atlas Rises update. If you played this game on launch and stopped shortly after, this game is much different now. There are new world types, galaxy map is improved, Space Stations tend to have more than one type of alien species on it (making the 3 main races feel more interwoven and actually interacting with one another. There is a series of missions with a story to it, giving you a sense of purpose to fulfil while exploring. There are also guilds that offer simple jobs for credits, items, or even blueprints. The Freighters not only allow you to build a base on-the-go, but actually offers further reach during warps. Space combat is improved. There have been times that friendly space ships actually help attack pirates that are attacking me.
This game is getting closer to what Shaun failed to deliver a year ago. Just goes to show that, yes, this game was released a year too early. It's at a point now that, if it was released today, I'd feel it is likely worth the full $60 pricetag. Still, I'd recommend getting it on sale if you can. I can't believe I'm actually going to give this a recommended rating.

In the 2nd Wildlife Park, I was annoyed at the staff buildings since they took up so much room and were never really a problem in my Tycoon games. They did fix that in Wildlife Park 3.

Overall the game feels like it really doesn't know what it wants to do. If there were short-but-to-the-point tutorials like the ZT games, these games would be better as well. Going to try scenarios maybe and YouTube for tutorials or pointers but after that, I'll be completely out of love with this one.

Pro Evolution Soccer 2018 is without doubt the best football game since the PES 4,5 and 6 glory days. Not only is the PC version finally on par with its PS4 counterpart; it is actually far superior with an excellent technical performance and astonishing visuals thanks to the latest Fox Engine build.
Graphically; the game looks almost photorealistic at times and the attention to detail is phenominal in places. The animations of players is an remarkable achievement and the immersive feel of the stadiums just offers an incredible experience. It is a groundbreaking step up from the 'hyrbid' builds we've had in recent years which is just polite terminology for 'PS3 port'.
In terms of gameplay; the pacing is a bit slower in this outing and it feels spot-on. Matches are less erratic and everything flows much better. Players are more composed in their play and the ball isn't bouncing around the pitch like a hot potato. You have to be more tactical and patient in your approach instead and it works really well.
Unfortuately, despite a string of key improvements to the game; the user interface is still incredibly dated as is the recycled commentary which drags the presentation down. It's not a major issue but Konami really need to improve this aspect next year. Online server and connection issues still persist as is the poorly supported online entity which is a shame.
Overall; PES 2018 is a stunning game and Konami's best effort for over a decade. From a gameplay and graphical standpoint, it's simply outstanding at times and if you're just looking for a football game to enjoy; it's an absolute must buy despite some dated elements and a disappointing online portion.

I have been playing online chess seriously for about a year (tried different softwares/websites). This game has a lot of potential. However, it does compete against websites like
which have been around for a long time and have perfected themselves with time. But people like me will join this community thinking that it would be great to play fellow gamers in chess which is an unsual thing in Steam! I Here is what I think should be done as a matter of priority:
- We should be able to search for players (per location or else)
- To refuse an invitation to play
- To resign
- The game should prompt you to confirm your move when done
- Chat rooms would be perfect (by theme or else), where people could interact with each other and perhaps have a chat before the game. This would be a massive advantage compared to other games in the market.
- There should be a time limit to your turn. At the moment if you play the day after your opponent plays or a month later there is no penalty. Your opponent could be waiting weeks before you move and this is frustrating. It is very important that there should be a time limit to your move and this could be agreed by both players before matching.
I believe that if the above is introduced it would make the game excellent. I am currently matching some people and enjoying it but I am looking forward to the development of the game. Hands down one of the best fighting games you will ever play.
Skullgirls is what you get when you take a team of passionate developers and a dedicated fan base, then mash them together.
The gameplay is a two 2D fighter, with a play style thats somewhere between the line of street fighter meets marvel vs capcom, fortunately, so long as your willing to take some time and practice, even if its just one character, you can stand your own ground in competetive online multiplayer. Skullgirls roster is a little on the small side with only 8 playable characters ( not counting the 6 DLC fighters), but good thing to note when it comes to fighting games with small rosters is that the options may not be all over the place, but at least you know that balancing is being taken seriously.
Online are pretty straight forward, you play best out of three, then rejoin a lobby unless your in your own private lobby or in a tourney. online is stable given the kind of game skullgirls is. for an indie game, while its never really frequnt, you will run into players online in most instances you play. however there will be days when you find yourself waiting endleslly for a quick match opponent and nothing will happen.
Learning how to play, even if your someone who doesn't ever play fighting games, the tutorial in skullgirls is amazingly well done. its got itself defined to the very last detail on combos and game macanics that you'll be able to master so long as you take some time to practice. I myself am yet to finish the tutorial by the time this goes up. simply put, its alot more advanced then pushing one or two buttons, you'll be coming back to it every so often to try learning something else about the game. Further more, some of the things the game teaches the player are even universal tips on just playing traditional fighting games in general.
The story to this game is weighed heavily on which character you choose for the story mode, and every character has a path that differs greatly among everyone. while there are many details left unmentioned and while somethings may need to be pieced together, its beyond worth the time to try out with everyone at least once. There's so much there, along with so much of it being left open to the point you would be like me and ask yourself "there's a comic series for this...right?"
Things such as the soundtrack, artsyle, and even the play style of skullgirls aew juat enjoyable themselves and make it feel like for just 10 dollars, your definetly gettin your money's worth with this one.

Yes I recommend this game. Is it a GREAT game however? No I don't believe it is, but it is a game worth playing.
Pros:
- The game is beautiful, there's no doubt about that. The game art is simply gorgeous and engulfs you in its splendor.
- The gameplay is perfect. Movement is fast and precise, and so much fun.
Cons:
- To me, the game seems lifeless. It's so generic feeling, unimaginitive. The story is souless. Which is a shame, because it is trying to be magical, but without any mystery and originality.
- Some game design elements are questionable. Firstly, almost every pickup is some kind of orb. Skills, life, energy, the other type of skills (two types of skills, confusing). None of the other pickups really feel like they fit into the universe either, other than visually. And then everytime you pick something up, no matter how many times you've done it, it will tell you how to use it with a big chunk of text covering a third of your screen. This drove me absolutely crazy.
- Some of the later level designs are questionable. When you've spent the entire game so far, learning your skills, being nimble and fast and platforming your way through the difficulties, only then to come accross completely different types of levels where you're flying and avoiding stuff, or carying junk that acts as some kind of magnet (??) that has nothing to do with the skills you've been learning. If this was brought in earlier in the game, I might understand, but introducing this later at a high difficulty is extremely frustrating. After building this feeling of "I'm getting good at this" for the player, all of a sudden this turns into "F@*k this game". That's not to say that I do not enjoy difficulty, I happily re-did difficult runs many times, blaming only myself for not succeeding. But with these odd levels, I blamed the game.
In any case, just my two cents.

Failing these until I got it right never felt frustrating -- I was pushed to succeed and they were exhilerating to play through. The story is simple, yet effective, and succeeded at focusing my will on little Ori. I even choked up at the end! I would recommend this game to anyone of any age as it is a shining example of what games can do as an artform, an entertainment platform, and as a medium of experimentation.

I really wanted to like this; I love artsy indie games.  And it does looks great, but it also plays horrible.
Everything seems to be designed to make you waste your time because if you just got it the first time through, the story would take about an hour to complete.  You RUN slower than molasses (hope you like holding down the shift key for no reason).  The interface is oddly hard to use for a game so simple.  The world is full of objects with no value and you have a limited inventory (there's literally objects named Camera1, Camera2, etc).  There's tons of backtracking after every minor completion to find the one thing that changed.  Levels have rooms with nothing useful in them, just to pad out space.  There is no save feature - if you have to quit, you lose your level's progress and have to repeat it.  There are enemies that will send you back to the start if they touch you.
Less than 5% of the players make it past the second level because it's illogical and random.  You have no idea what to do or why you're doing it.  The worst part is that puzzles need to be completed in the exact correct order or else you can run into game breaking bugs that make you start over (I had to redo the house because the parents appeared, but never turned to stone).
There is no real story and the ending is a predictable cliche.
Stay away.  If you do play it, do yourself a favor and look at the walkthroughs.

Just like the title implies, this is a very artistic little game. Very atmospheric, with a unique artstyle and subtle, melancholic music. It's also quite creepy, with just one example being a mysterious Ghibli-esque monster that makes scratching noises in the background and devours you if you get too close. It definitely made an impression the first time it happened to me!
The game doesn't bother to explain much and doesn't hand hold you. You're left alone to explore and make sense of the story, which is told in a surreal way. As for the puzzles they can be pretty challenging to solve, especially since you're allowed to pick most items without knowing which ones are actually useful and which are just decoration. (Also there's barely any guides or walkthroughs on the internet so you're on your own!!) But even so there are enough hints to point you to the right direction eventually, and personlly I never got irreperably stuck or frustrated with any part of the game.
Like a lot of other reviews mention, there are a few technical annoyances, like the clunky inventory controls and the lack of manual saves. However for me those few downsides didn't even come close to substracting from the overall experience of the game, which left me very satisfied. If you like puzzle heavy adventure games with a cool atmosphere then you'll enjoy this.

First episode into the game and I was having a hard time containing my excitement.  This was the first "AAA" game I had played in quite a while that oozed with so much...atmosphere?  The trailers and screenshots don't quite do the prescence of Neo Paris justice, and I can see how they  may come off as a typical cyberpunkish utopia/slums contrast.  However, Dontnod's designers manage to take those tropes and somehow make them feel fresh and envigorating.  Even the UI for the menu's in the game are interesting, different, and don't feel like a hastle to sift through (the Combos Lab aside).  The Horn of Jericho is probably my favorite and the most memorable enemy offered up by the game, something about the giant angry robot projecting a shouting human mouth while roaring is captivating and creepy at the same time.
The game does a really good job of pacing out the combat, puzzle solving, and platforming, delivering all three in varying doses without any single one getting too tiresome before switching gears to something else.  Collectibles are cleverly placed and most use different cues like memorizing an image to find later in the level or audio cues so they can be easily located without too much "hunting forever to get that one achievement" syndrome.
Narrative pacing is slow to start, and just when I was beginning to presume certain portions were just poorly written the story fills in the holes and brings the player back in.  Since the protagonist starts out the game as an amnesiac this is a good hook to keep you in sync with the status of the main character.  They know just as much as you do, sometimes even less...
Some enemy models get tweaked as the game progresses, so while there's not a lot of variety to the silohuettes, the combat system forces you to rethink your strategy by changing the status quo each time a new enemy type is introduced or by throwing unique combinations of enemies into a fight.  The boss fights never seem unfair, though its not always immediately clear what your goal is to wear down the enemy in those scenarios (if you are ever stuck for a prolonged period of time on a battle or in a puzzle the game can offer a hint to help you along, but this was usually not provided in my playthrough as I eventually figured it out in time).  The combat system has you slowly unlock button presses with special effects throughout the game, which can then be chained together in templates provided for combos (XYYXYY, XXX, YYYXXXXY, etc.).  These special effects range from additional damage to healing on-hit.  While not my favorite part of the game it was fun to have some control over what my attacks did when facing specific enemy types.
Platforming is not an open world experience like Assassin's Creed, you can't climb anywhere (usually only on highlighted beams and ledges).  Despite movement being somewhat restricted I never felt like I was running down a linear series of hallways like some games suffer from.
Puzzles come in a wide variety, some include modifying the environment through use of various machinery and your AR glove, while others involve cracking passwords or figuring out how to outsmart a drone formation patrol.  The most notable are the memory remixes, where you enter the memory of another character and look for glitches to remix to make them believe something in the past occured in an alternate fashion to help will them to the protagonist's cause.
A couple of the remixes left a bad feeling in my stomach, combined with a few of the actions the player was championed into accomplishing by their "leader".  The moral consequences of making someone believe in a different past are rarely explored, and many of the negative actions the player has to take to get to the ending evoke a "Spec Ops: The Line" feeling with a lot less hating yourself and a little more "did the ends justify the means?" pondering.
The smaller gripes I have with the game include jumping being very nearly worthless when not in a platforming scenario, unskippable cut scenes (if I die with a checkpoint right before a battle, etc.), the sometimes confused UI in the Combo Lab, and the game pausing whenever I Shift-Tab (I could at least be browsing the web during the second+ viewing of those cut scenes?).  My love for what this game does RIGHT completely eclipses those annoyances though, Dontnod has built a solid third person game with mechanics that are classic but feel fresh, and have built a beautiful world around that gameplay.  Do yourself a favor and give this game a try.

This place, this little diversion from the fighting and all that in an effort to rush through the game, was the reason I played Remember Me. I saw a screenshot, and it was beautiful, stunning even. The game was so pretty. And the concept was just awesome.
So, when I installed the game and got ready to play, I was not expecting what I got. But I was happy. The combat system was a bit boring, since it basically boils down to spam your big damage combo to kill things, then spam your hp combo to heal back up, and maybe abuse some cooldown combot to get your abilities back faster.
It's not bad combat. It's just that the real, BIG highlight of this game was the memory rewriting. You've no idea until you've done it how fun it is. It's just so novel.
Worth buying if it goes on sale.

So, I played this game for roughly 5-6 missions or so and I got a decent bit of feeling for the game. This is what I have to say:
~====~
Graphics
~====~
This game is good for what you are into when it comes to gaming though the graphics aren't the best which is fine, but sometimes if someone would want to have the best graphics on because they are used to it or they just want full graphics then this won't be the best for you. The characters are a bit blocky which is also fine, but in "This day in age" we aren't used to seeing super blocky characters unless the whole game is made like that. For example, Minecraft is made to be a blocky game so that you can enjoy the building aspect in it to it's fullest extent, though when you play this game you would assume it to be a bit more adjusted to the kind of graphics we see today. The animations are pretty good and the game has a lot of potential in this category but for now I give it this:
~Not the Best but hopefully be improved upon~
~====~
Combat
~====~
There isn't much to talk about in regards to combat in this game but, the combat in this game could be a bit better and also a bit less repetitive in it's own way. Basically, you spawn into the mission, you're given an objective to do then you do the objective and the mission is done. The objectives aren't all too complicated but they do get repetitive after a while of playing, I know I have only played for 35 minutes or so but that's because I don't feel like going through the same stuff constantly. So I would give the combat this:
~It gets Repetitive after a while~
~====~
Story
~====~
I am not gonna lie but I didn't pay attention to the story all that much, I started the game and I was given a black screen with text explaining the story. After about a minute or so I realized I had to click the mouse to continue the text scrolling so I kept reading a few more messages. After I read a bit more, I figured that this would just show me millions of text boxes to read so I just skipped through them so I could actually play the game. So, I would give the story this:
~Possibly Good if you take the time to read~
~====~
Final Verdict
~====~
This game isn't really worth to buy unless you get it on a great sale like I did or you really like these kinds of games. I would check out videos by players about it to get a better feel for the game before you buy it.

Story: 5/10 - The plot felt a little bland to me. Unique idea, but didn't seem terribly fleshed out.
Gameplay: 5/10 - I'm not a big platformer, and this game IS rather difficult. Some of the rooms and levels are merciless and will leave you forced to walk away for a while. The game is constant action, which can be quite grueling with a keyboard. There is very little downtime and on escape levels especially, you will find yourself on the pause screen just trying to catch your breath. No room is impossible; with enough tries, muscle memory will help you trudge through, but it's not challenging in a fun way.
Graphics: 8/10 - Gorgeous. Immersive. Beautiful colorscapes. Probably one of my favorite 2D games visually. Virtually any screenshot from in-game could easily be a wallpaper. Really great stuff. That being said, this game was tough on my computer. I have a pretty good system, but I'd have to close most everything down to make my character run at normal speed. Streaming was ruled out when it made the entire game run in slow-motion with the audio track minutes ahead of what was on the screen.
Music: 10/10 - I was a player who stumbled across Ori and the Blind Forest because Pandora kept playing me fragments of the soundtrack, which I absolutely loved for a year or two before knowing anything about the game. The music is truly incredible. It lends itself perfectly to every part of the story, as well as being very calming and centering in the midst of an extremely frustrating gameplay. The soundtrack was definitely my takeaway from this game.
Replay Value: 2/10 - I often find myself wanting to be IN the game again. Being able to nimbly leap and fly through a glowing, mysterious world is a joyful experience. But everyone who's played this game can name rooms that they'd like to never have to play again ever. A second playthough is beneficial once you are more seasoned with the controls and know how to beat the rooms and can get more powerups, but beyond that, I find it pretty pointless.
Do I recommend this game? It depends. It does leave you with a sense of accomplishment, but only after grueling hours that friends won't be able to relate with because it's an indie game and a lot of people have never heard of it. If you like platformers and sidescrollers, you will surely enjoy the challenge. If you're more of a casual gamer or get frustrated with steep difficulty curves like I do, I really think there's no harm in watching a playthrough to enjoy the good things the game has to offer without the infuriating experience which you will undoubtedly have with this game. I did enjoy Ori and the Blind Forest and I'm glad that I played it, but be prepared... The game is unforgiving.
Overall: 6/10

For an early access build, Stash is remarkably stable, what few issues do exist are patched very quickly by one of the most approachable and communicative development teams I’ve seen of late. I’m sure we’re all familiar with the trend of releasing a buggy mess into early access, grabbing quick cash from release hype and then disappearing into the ether. I’m happy to say Frogdice has not followed this trend with Stash. This is clearly a labour of love for the developers, and I look forward to seeing it evolve through Early Access and to completed release.
That being said, I would be remiss if I didn’t point out that for an early access game with a price point, the game does feel a little bare. Whilst I can understand that the developers do want to focus on core mechanics before adding the artistic flair, it is a factor which is keeping me from playing this game more often. I do recommend it for people who enjoy getting in on the ground level of a game’s development, and I honestly do believe it will be a feature amongst RPG aficionados ‘Must own’ recommendations come final release.

Wildlife Park 3 is a game where you get to create and manage your very own wildlife park. You make animal enclosures, pick the animals to go in there, hire vets, zoo keepers, gardeners, garbage men, place visitor facilities, plants, decorations and so on. As a game, its full of soothing music and the campaign tells you exactly what to do.
The game is good at telling you what the animals and visitors want when you click on them. Such as buffalo want to wallow in mud or have a mineral deficiency. Not just that, but icons hover over the heads of both animals and visitors. The visitors have smiles or frowns over their heads. The animals have icons indicating their needs such as its too hot out, if they're thirsty, hungry or need more foliage. The animals can do a variety of things such as mate, have babies, get sick, scratch on trees, play with toys and wallow in mud. Clicking on an animal shows their information in a panel at the bottom. This panel is full of information how their needs are being met. Everything from grass, meat, mineral and water to scratching, temperature, ground and foliage. To be honest the charts are appreciated, but not needed when the comment box for each animal bluntly tells you where each animal is deficient.
You don't just buy an animal or hire someone like you would a piece of furniture, you need to hire from applicants and buy from animal traders. Every animal and employee is unique unto themselves, so you need to select the right one for you. Not just that, but consider their price, age, health and skills. This all goes into the management aspect of it. You can sell off animals and babies. Its all about keeping your wildlife park running. When you click on an employee, you can see their range radius that they will tend to. The radius is a giant square that you can shrink or expand, but its always a square instead of just being assigned to a specific enclosure or two. The staff will attend to all feedings, watering, droppings and vets will attend to sick animals automatically. They'll also gain skills when working with animals too.
When your visitor approval rating go up, so do your 'stars.' With more stars, you can charge more, upgrade buildings, unlock more buildings and have a selection of better animals. It is a wildlife park, not a zoo, even though someone in the tutorial calls it a zoo. Since it is a wildlife park, it sticks to that theme, you'll find wild animals here. You'll find bison, wildebeest, gazelles, lions, giraffes, hippos, penguins, cheetahs, bears, pumas, sea lions, leopards, chimps, gorillas, elephants, zebras and so on. Some might say the game is limited in its how many species of animals that it has. Perhaps some DLC will offer different animals, but since this game was originally released in 2011, I think that monkey escaped the zoo a long time ago.
The animals aren't the only things you'll need to keep alive. The trees are living too. They'll need the correct ground underneath of them to flourish. Not only for the animals to eat and shade themselves, but in this game, the animals get spooked from seeing jeep rides drive through their enclosures. So you'll need to obscure the jeep ride tracks with foliage as exampled in the campaign.
I love games like these that blend management and creativity into making your own area. Games like Roller Coaster Tycoon, Zoo Tycoon, Prison Architect, Sim City and Cities XL. With that being said, I really want to like Wildlife Park 3, but it just feels so cumbersome, devoid of goals and just not fun overall. The 'campaign' is really just a tedious tutorial with some okay to good voice acting. This is one of those tycoon games that has characters commanding you. How to pick up animals, where to drop them. After about 3 hours, I felt like the tutorial wasn't specifically telling me what to do.
The tutorials seemed to have bugs or issues, such as the next button not working or even when you do what they tell you to, they still will not continue. Sometimes doing as you please and saying that area needs something, doing it then it breaks the tutorial and prevents it from continuing even after undoing what you did, causing multiple restarts when really I just want to build my own wildlife park. Perhaps none of their testers deviated and did anything the game wasn't instructing them to do. For completing each campaign mission, you'll unlock an extra decoration or something to add to whatever parks you have in the future.
There is freeplay mode, which seems to be the real game since the campaign is just a tutorial. With freeplay, you get to select a plot of land from dozens from around the world. You then select how much money you start with and rules such as if your animals and or plants can get diseases. The problem here is some of the areas just feel very small even for one animal enclosure, let alone dozens. Each plot of land has their own climate, either grassy, desert or tundra.
While I can't say the graphics are the best, they're not the worst. You'll see stiffly animated animals and beautiful foliage, hiding in tall grass and experience all of the seasons with rain and snowfall. It is a nice layer of graphical detail. Even better than that, if you really want to examine things, you can use your mouse wheel to zoom straight up to the animals to see them play, swim, and eat or just to see how bored your staff looks.  You can also see how the characters don't move their lips when talking, but that's a nitpick unless you really want to figure out who is talking to you. When you are super zoomed in, you can see in first person perspective, and walk around. The only problem is right and left keys rotate you instead of strafing you, but when you're not zoomed in all the way, you can strafe. I guess it offers control diversity to what you prefer.
That is just the tip of the iceberg as to how the controls feel out of date. There are no hotkeys, you need to push the rotate button instead of mouse dragging to rotate like similar games a 3D engine. Its all so cumbersome. Luckily the 3rd tutorial teaches you to hold the mouse button and move up or down to rotate the item, otherwise you'd need to click the rotate button on the panel and check to see how far the item rotated. When I want to pick up an animal or employee, I need to highlight them, then click on move from a bottom menu, then move them and drop them. It just feels like an extra step and it could have been streamlined like other games have done.
The game is full of needlessly poor design choices. Yellow text on yellow and red gradient background so it blends in. Paths aren't considered ground so much as they are considered 'visitor facilities.' To top that off, paths are called 'ways,' in the menu, but even the game calls them paths and thoroughfares.
The game doesn't feel fun compared to most every other sort of build your own this or that tycoon game. There's nothing to do, no goals to achieve other than the blunt commands in the campaign tutorial. Visitors will have thoughts and I guess that tells you what you should do. They want to see other animals, so then you add more animals, and then they want to see more animals, so you add more animals. It would be nice if there was a campaign with goals such as have 600 visitors to your wildlife park within 2 years. Have X amount of animals in your park within 4 years. Have a park value of X amount in Y years.
Even though this is a finished product, the third game in a series, it feels much more like the start of an unfinished game. I bought it in a $1 bundle and you can too. Maybe the fourth Wildlife Park will be better and have more to offer.

After about a couple of hours of gameplay and completing the tutorial and several missions, I want to weigh in on what this game has to offer.
Others have covered some of these points already, but I'll summarize the biggest shortcoming as thus:
The overall aesthetic design of this game is atrocious.
The graphic design seen in the UI, main menu, even to the closing screen, are amateurish at best, I prefer the UI in Roller Coaster Tycoon 2, and that game is over a decade old. If you're prone to frustration, you will most likely give yourself a headache trying to figure out this clunky and dated interface. I still haven't figured out where (Or if) it tells you how much a purchase will cost before buying it.
On the bright side, the actual game itself can be beautiful at times. The screenshots are pretty true to the game.
However, don't expect it to go much farther than that. The gameplay grows shallow after little play. Once you set up an initial enclosure, it's hard to care much more about it as there's little else to do besides make it prettier or bigger. Training of the animals is gone, there's so few of them that you run out of combinations of species to set up in one enclosure, and the only visitor attractions you can really build are safaris (Jeep and rail) and air tours.
Everything else, as far as the small bugs go, pales in comparison to the sheer lack of gameplay that can be found in this.
Don't get me wrong, what's actually done in this game is done fairly well, but the game is not worth the 10$ pricetag, not when you can pick up the 1st Zoo Tycoon ultimate edition for the same price at the time of writing.
I bought it at 3.40$, and I feel like that was fair, I got what I paid for, but do not purchase this game fullprice, it's simply not worth it, and it pales in comparison to the previous Zoo Tycoons, and even the previous Wildlife Park 2, which is a complete shame, as this market is absolutely starved of games like this. There's only a handful of games which can liken themselves to the same genre, and what is there pales in comparison to what came before it.

Seems like a perfectly good game, but I would not recommend it. I found Senua and the voices in her head to be interesting and satisfying, and I enjoyed the Viking lore. The combat is entertaining, though limited. However, I stopped playing the game after maybe 3 hours because the negatives are significant. There are two big negatives: the mouselook controls are HORRIBLE, and the linearity is more than I could take. Mouselook: as far as I can tell, you can't adjust the mouselook speed. It is obviously set for gamepad speeds, looking around to your left or right with a mouse is like trying to move through molasses. Thick molasses. I actually found myself not looking around because I really did not want to wait that long. As for the linearity, this surprised me because I usuallly enjoy games that are very linear ("on rails") but have a good story to tell. The lack of choice in this game makes it so linear, I kind of felt like it would have been better as a game with a "auto-play until the next puzzle or combat" button. Other than the puzzles and the combat, this game is entirely non-interactive. There is no sense at all that Senua is a physical presence in the world. I guess I've become spoiled by games that show my footprints imprinted in the snow or dirt, or birds startled by my arrival. This is not that game.

I can say that I have been a video gamer since 1996 when I convinced my mother to purchase a computer to play the latest Blizzard games. There was a level of wonder to new ideas that has been lost for the past 10+ years for me. This game captured that wonder in a way I couldn't have possibly imagined. It is so refreshing to have a developer step outside of the standardization that has become video games and take a risk on an extreme idea. I have to say that as a combined video game, I feel this is the best product I have touched since completeing the Ocarina of Time 15 years ago. Sensu's character is believeable, extremely well acted and tragic. I was immmersed in this game from the very first whispers in the opening scene. It was horrifying, painful, imaginative and equal parts disturbing at times. I felt for the character Senua, I found myself seeking out the story runes in each area and found myself walking through this wonderfully imaginative enviroment instead of running through to the next objective as in most games. Truly one of the greatest titles I have played. Any complaints I have read on lackluster combat are a mute point, combat grows with your experience, and on the hardest combat settings is downright brutal lategame. The puzzles are completely original, and difficult at times, but I felt very rewarded. I feel Ninja theory has stepped outside the box and then used it as a stepping stool, props to the actor palying Senua and this developer, truly one of the greats!!

This is the story about some guy who is kidnapped by someone else and forced to use the mumble to mumble mumble the memories of mumblemurf for some reason or other. The game doesn't have subtitles. An unfortunate design choice for two reasons.
The first reason: Many of the actors(?) haven't quite figured out how to open their mouth while talking.
The second reason: talking is pretty much everything that happens in this game.
Don't believe the lie about open-world gameplay, parkour moves and total freedom. All I seemed to do in this game was to hold forwards from one dialogue-ridden cutscene to the next. Sure, I had the option of parkouring about the place, but it didn't bring forth feelings of open world movement and pulse-pounding action. Freerunning simply felt like a carrot being dangled over my nose on the other side of a window, designed solely to frustrate me while I wait through another cutscene.
Wait seems to be the keyword in this game. The intro in particular is an irritating wait. Intros are to be skipped. We see them the first time, and then we skip past them because we've already seen them. But no. The developers don't care about me wanting to play a game, they've got religious nutters to placate, leaving me to tap the escape-button with no real hope of being let into the game any time soon.
Still, if you've got good hearing, a high tolerance for tricky control schemes, and a genuine interest in Mumblemurf's backstory, I'm sure the game is good.

Why? Well read on mate...
Personally i think that TNC was heavily leaning on the extreme success of TNO. While TNC is lots more of the fun Rambo styl action of the previous title, It is no where near as good as TNO or even TOB.
Gameplay:
Fun but lacking. The shooting of course was fun, TNC has everything that made the previous game fun and more. However the "more" part is where the game starts to feel unpolished. For example, now that any combinationof weapons can be dualiwielded the devs had to change the weapon wheel, It is now 2 weapons wheels (one for each hand) wish you have to switch back and forth from, However for one the switching speed of the wheels is incredibly slow and selecting a weapon is also feels very clunky and slow therefor both these things (when used) throttle the gameplay speed by a great degree. Luckily however there are hotkeys for dualwield, attachments..etc wich however are also a little slow, However still a better alternative over the weapon wheel.
Aside from that there are new movement abilities to put it short theres is one to reach high places, one to to get into small vents and one to smash through through walls and run over enemies. All of these while seeming very fun and intresting in concept again feel incredibly unpolished and again clunky and dont integrate themselves smoothly into the rest of the movement mechanics and gameplay. There is some very fun energetic level no doubt wisch really show how good of a job Machine Games can do with this franchise, But saddly there was really enough of them especially not when the game is a good chunk shorter than it in my opinion it should be, And what i believe is the worst thing of all about the levels and the gameplay of the game itsself is that there is an insane amount of padding. For example one location of the game was reused MULTIPLE times (yes in different contexts and with different objectives) however is was still the exact same level give or take a few small areas. And what i find especially insulting is that at the end of the (to short) game what you can do is take up missions from the playyer home to go out and kill commanders, But the commanders are mainly in places to already had missions in so basically they are letting you revisit already used locations and getting you to kill a Commander in it and thats pretty much all you do, It feels so much like padding and i expected so much more, And really the commander missions would be fine, infact normally ide say its great that they give you some more stuff to do after the main campaign, a great addtion would it not be for the fact that the main campaign felt a couple hours to short.
Guns:
The guns are fine (even tho personally i think the selection is a bit boring for the regular guns) However the timeline (ill get to that) specific Guns are fantastic and even more fun than the Lasercannon from TNO. However my personally i was extremely dissapointed in the shotgun as it has next to no kick behind it and doesent feel like the powerful shotgun cannons from TNO. But as i said personally i think the selection of weapons is rather bland compared to the previous game (no laser rifles saddly), But on a plus side the Heavy carry only weapons are very fun to use and a great reward for killing mini bosses. And finally the Fire Hatchet wich in this game replaces the traditional knife is also very satisfying to use and i think its a fantastic alternative to the knife, combat and lore wise. Also it creates some fantastic gorey melee kills.
The Story:
By far the biggest dissapointment for me, So first of all the game essentially is split into 2 parts mood wise, The first half being very sad and similar to the general atmosphere of TNO. HOWEVER!! In no way does it do it aswell as TNO. B.J again has inner monologue like in the previous game but unfortunately while being being very reflective of B.Js character and giving us a good insight into his character, it is very poorly written and overall it sounds "whiney" and cheesey, In this first sad half of the game we also get alot of back flashes to B.Js child hood, This i think i actually very good and again provide alot of insight on why B.J is the way he is and they also provide some very intresting gameplay.
Now to the second half of the game wich is alot more upbeat and has alot of humor built into it. While this is refreshing and does create some great moments in the game it can be a little annoying and overwhelming as it does cause a drastic change to the character of B.J, wich not agree with everyone.
However aside from all that the overall Villain of the game is Frau Engel from TNO, Now in the previous game she worked fantastic as a side antagonist as she was a very intresting character, But really she does not work as the main villain, Deathshead was a obsessed evil nazi scientist who performed unspeakable things on innocent people...... and Frau Engel is just kind of a power hungry evil nazi, What im saying is that she is not nearly evil enough to be the main villain of a game wich in previouse iteraions has main villains like DeathsHead or yanno FREAKING HITLER IN A MECHSUIT. Now without including spoilers i have to say that there is so much more they could have done with the character of Frau Engel, They literally just took her out of the TNO and plopped her into TNC without really changing a thing about her, shes not cazier, Shes not more powerful and she in no way is a better or more intresting character than she was in the previous game, Infact ide almost say shes less intresting because we never really get any tense interactive moments with her like the train card game in TNO. ....shes just kinda the ruler of ruler of germany and from time to time she pops up and is a B**ch to you, and then proceeds to further the story a little bit by. But the one saving grace that i have to award her with is that her writing and the voice actors performance are phenomenal. Im a fluent German and English speaker so i could understand every word she said, and it was incredibly well written and sounded very authentic and was alot more natural than in TNO. Aside from that the story is fairly boring, However there is some fantastic characters and other returning characters that are also very well performed. So in conclusion very good characters great voice acting performance but BY FAR  the greatest let down of the game is the ending wich is terrible and completely unsatisfying.
Overall:
Gameplay- 7/10
Story- 5/10
Conclusion:
If you havent played Wolfenstein: The New Order then frankly this game might very well be on your top games of 2017 list, But for people who enjoyed the previouse game and its standalone expansion, Wolfenstein: The New Collossus is an incredibly dissapointment and i personally can not understand how a Dev that created such a fantastic game as TNO would put out a mediocre experience like TNC. I mean seriously normally most of the problems in this game could be looked past but not if the bar was raised to damn high with the previous title. And frankly i would normally definitely recommend this game but seriously the kind of ending they give us in this game is inexcusable for a wolfenstein game.
Seriously if u havent bought this game yet, Save yourself the money and go buy The New Order, its an amazing game you will love it if you into games like DOOM(2016) and mybe even the standalone expansion The Old Blood wich is also pretty good as far as DLC goes. So overall im saying dont buy it now, its not worth your money, but sometime in the future when its cheaper. And also even if your going to buy it atleast wait a while because currently the game is pretty broken and has alot of bugs, But im not going to complain about those to much because they are actively fixing them pretty quickly.

My kids had a lot of fun with LEGO Jurassic World, so we thought we would give this one a try. Unfortunately it has been far less enjoyabe so far.
The major issue is technical glitches. We've only played through the first couple of levels, and already encountered situations where: actions such as jump would just inexplicably stop working for all the characters; the NPCs would get "stuck" and not be able to perform an action to let us continue in the level. And although it generally looks nice and runs at 60FPS, it inexplicably drops down to < 30FPS for 10+ seconds at a time which is super annoying. (Seems to be a known issue, even affecting high end hardware).
The next issue is that unless you are very familiar with the Harry Potter characters and story lines you will often have a hard time figuring out what to do. And because there is no actual voice acting (just grunts and moans, unlike Jurassic World), if you don't already know the story of the HP movies, you'll be guessing what the hell is happening in the story.
So if you're a huge Harry Potter fan and can live with the technical glitches it's a decent looking game and entertaining in the way that LEGO games are... Otherwise, skip it and play Jurassic World if you haven't already.

Konami finally bother to make a decent PC version with graphics better than consoles, ultrawide support, 4k support and overall good performance on a 7700k/1080TI using a 3440x1440 ultrawide screen. But you'd generally expect that on a system like that
Starting off with bad points, as much as this game supports ultrawide, it's not fantastic support, FIFA does it better with ultrawide cut scenes, menus and replays, PES fails to do this unfortunately, but it's still good that it's supported and not some offbrand PS3 port
It's seriously expensive, £54.99?? That's the highest price I've ever seen for a standard game.
Online currently doesn't work but I'd assume that'll be rectified within a day or two.
The game still has extreme licensing issues, which is the main thing that puts most people off PES, the licensing is seriously bad except Champions League license like every year. Most Premier League teams aren't licensed which is an issue for a Spurs fan.
Onto better points, the game has fantastic graphics, animations and the game feels extremely realistic. I'm quite new to PES and professional difficulty felt about right and if you're a FIFA player, the game also offers FIFA based controls, so switching between them is easy.
There's a lot of game modes and plenty of teams (licensed or not) There's a lot of content in this game overall and you will be sinking a lot of hours into it, such as MyClub, Champions League, Exhibition and more online/co-op modes.
Going off the bad point about the £54.99, you can pick up this game for about £20-30 elsewhere (Don't use G*A or K*nguin though) At £20-30 I'd say it is easily worth it
The gameplay is fluid with a slower pace than FIFA, making for a more realistic feel to it, the passing is very accurate and it's decently easy to actually beat keepers in 1v1s, rather than keepers turning into absolute gods and saving 5 1v1 shots a game. (like in FIFA)
Overall, PES is a decent buy for a football fan with a much better PC port, but the classic PES issue of terrible licensing is still present, teams like Chelsea, Real Madrid, Juventus etc not being licensed in a game based around the Champions League.... I would recommend buying it if you can get it cheaper than retail, it's not worth £54.99 by any means.
If you have to pick between this and FIFA, I'd probably still say FIFA is going to be better due to the licensing, generally better PC port and better graphics. But if you can afford both, I would 100% recommend picking up both games, they're two different styles completely.
